Class and race are TRANSLATED onto this engine's single Dragonlance ruleset, not carried 1:1 — paladins fold into fighters, dwarf and elf take one fixed variant each. Every substitution is listed per hero in the import panel rather than smoothed over.
Spells known and equipment are not decoded.

The layout does not generalise: the same offsets accept 1/6 of Secret of the Silver Blades' 439-byte records, 0/6 of Pools' 510-byte and 0/8 of Treasures'. That cross-title null is now a STANDING TEST (packages/engine/test/coabSavedCharacter.test.ts's 'cross-title null' describe block, one skipIf case per title), so it goes red if any of the four counts drift, matching the shifted-offset oracle's own coverage. Round 29 also found the raw sweep is swamped by degenerate matches — byte 0 is a valid cleric code, so any constant-zero window trivially agrees — and requiring the class byte to vary collapses Curse to exactly its two known real offsets, which is what makes the cross-title zeros meaningful. Secret's own class/level offsets were located separately at 0x6c/0x111 and are NOT a single contiguous insertion relative to Curse's 0x75/0x109 (the class byte moves 9 bytes earlier, the level array 8 later; only the 17-byte gap growth matches the record-size delta) — docs/engine/research/secret-chrdata-layout.md. Round 30 built that importer (?import=secret, packages/engine/src/loaders/secretSavedCharacter.ts): it imports 5 of the 6 pregens, and the sixth is refused for a located reason rather than a mystery — Secret's race byte reads 6, which is not a value in Curse's Race enum, so the race defaults to human and this ruleset's non-humans-only multi-class rule rejects MALACHITE, the party's only fighter/thief. Round 30 also corrected the closing claim below. Pools' and Treasures' 510-byte layouts are no longer 'unknown (0 discriminating pairs each)': that 0 was a THRESHOLD ARTEFACT. Full n-of-n agreement is indeed still 0 for both, but at the same two-field oracle Curse's own loader rests on, class byte 0xae + ClassLevel[8] window 0x151 scores 5/6 on Pools and 7/8 on Treasures — one miss each — and that clears a shuffled null built for the honest alternative (how high can ANY pair score by chance) rather than the null that only ever restates the 0. The two misses (Pools' ABAGAIL, Treasures' OUGO) are reported as misses, not resolved, because each is the sole example of its own anomaly and no predicate built from n=1 can be checked against a null without circularity — docs/engine/research/pools-treasures-chrdata-layout.md.
import.scope: ?import=coab reads all six real SAVE/CHRDATA{1..6}.SAV pregens byte-faithfully (name, abilities including the raw str00 percentile, race/class bytes, ClassLevel[8], hp, thac0) and builds a playable party. The offset oracle — agreement between the class byte and the ClassLevel[8] array — accepts 6/6 at the true offset and 0/6 at one byte either side.

gaps: ECL DECODE CENSUS, SHALLOW AND DEEP (round 33 R1, restated round 34 R1, 2026-09-04): disassembleEclBlock stops at each block's FIRST EXIT, so a clean-EXIT count is a LOWER BOUND -- it never walks the combat, quest or descriptor subroutines placed later in a block's own bytes. walkEclReachable (packages/engine/src/ecl/reachability.ts) follows all five ECL header entry points and every GOTO/GOSUB/ON_GOTO/ON_GOSUB. Measured on this title's 22 retail blocks: 0 shallow desync block(s), 0 deep desync site(s). ROUND 34 CORRECTION: this line read 40 deep sites until round 34 R1 added ECL opcode 0x41 to the SHARED Gen1 base table at wordSet 2 (packages/engine/src/ecl/opcodes.ts, ECL_OPCODE_MAX 0x40 -> 0x41). That single entry closed EVERY deep desync site this title had (40 -> 0), with zero shallow-census regression. R1 shipped this as UNKNOWN_0x41 with semantics explicitly unclaimed, because EclDump's own SetupCommandTable is dense only over 0x00..0x40, so its silence about 0x41 is a property of EclDump, not of the bytes. THAT IS NO LONGER THE STATE OF THE EVIDENCE. A round 34 follow-up (docs/engine/research/gen1-opcode-41.md) went and read the handlers: all three base-table titles carry their OWN 0x41 dispatch entry -- CoK GAME.OVR 0x4048, DoK 0x2e0e (reproducing the pre-existing build/dok-ecl-dispatch-map.json row byte-for-byte, which checks the tooling), Secret 0x43ff -- located by structural match against the CoAB oracle. Each reads exactly 2 operands from its own `mov al,2; push ax; lcall <parser>` prologue, so wordSet 2 is now confirmed from BINARY GROUND TRUTH and not only from the eight independent derivations that already agreed on it (Gateway, Treasures at GAME.OVR 0x2c40, Pools at 0x240c, Buck, Matrix, DQK Gen2, R1's byte-shape derivation, and now this one). All three handlers share one idiom: read a 0/1 flag and a round word amount, count the ACTIVE party members, divide, and ADD/ADC the share into a 32-bit per-character accumulator (flag=1 walks the party chain, flag=0 hits one target). CoK's walks that chain through CCH +0x17F/+0x181 -- the SAME 'next combatant' far pointer that CoK's already byte-verified post-combat calc_battle_exp uses (docs/engine/research/decompile-ovr006-xp-treasure.md), from an investigation that borrowed nothing from this one. The mnemonic is therefore now GEN1_AWARD_XP. uncertain STAYS TRUE and the reason is specific: no loader or save-format doc in this repo names the accumulator field (CoK +0x116/+0x118) as the canonical experience field, and no oracle certifies the label -- what is proven is the STRUCTURE, not the name. Note also that these handlers DIVIDE where Pools'/Treasures' own 0x41 (POOLS_AWARD_XP / TREASURES_AWARD_XP) MULTIPLIES by 100, so the dialects stay correctly separate. ONE OF R1'S OWN CLAIMS IS CORRECTED HERE: 'the operand is always a multiple of 500' is measured at 98.4% (121/123) on an exhaustive walk of every reached site in all three titles' ECL1-3.DAX, with two genuine CoK exceptions (ECL1.DAX block 32 @0x1cec = 300; ECL2.DAX block 67 @0x1bff = 32633), both in the flag=0 single-target branch. Stratified by the flag -- which R1's sample could not do -- flag=1 is 95/95 = 100%. The null: word-kind operands of every OTHER reached instruction in the same blocks are multiples of 500 just 0.53% of the time (n = 29,954), a ~185x enrichment, so the roundness is a property of THIS argument. Caveat kept: that follow-up's from-scratch walker reproduces walkEclReachable's CoK (33) and Secret (40) counts exactly but finds 50 DoK sites where the engine's numbers imply 43 -- a difference in its simplified control-flow rules, not a disputed fact about the opcode. The engine's pinned counts in eclReachability.test.ts are the authoritative ones. Pinned in packages/engine/test/eclReachability.test.ts; deep counts are SITES and shallow counts are BLOCKS, so the two are not directly subtractable.

audio.detail: Shared step and UI audio paths exist, but audio is not part of the Verified route gate.
gaps: CoK's five MIDI.DAX blocks are measured as five disjoint per-hardware DRIVERS, not five songs: block 1 C/MS 0x221/0x223, block 2 Roland MPU-401 0x330/0x331, block 3 AdLib 0x388, block 4 Tandy 0xC0, block 5 PIT+PC speaker 0x42/0x43/0x61 — matching START.EXE's SOUND TYPE menu in order, with a mean pairwise port-set overlap of 0.014 against the ~1.0 that the 'one block per song' reading predicts (docs/midi-dax-format.md 1.5a). The note-event buffer a driver receives through its CX/ES install handshake is still UNLOCATED: not in any DAX block, any carved GAME.OVR segment or START.EXE, and a live 1MB RAM dump could not settle it because GameLink exposes no CPU registers. Song decoding remains unresolved. Note the search's null: 55 of 100 random 32-byte RAM windows also map to some on-disk file span, because overlay code is resident verbatim — any future RAM-to-file match must clear that bar, not merely exist.

ROUND 33 R6 (2026-09-04) SPLIT THE GAP ABOVE IN TWO, and only one half moved. RESOLVED: the CX/ES install handshake itself, previously 'UNLOCATED', is now directly observed. Two live GameLink RAM captures read a nonzero segment at the exact mov [0x0012], cx cell (0x5f39 and 0x6173, differing between snapshots) against a universal on-disk default of 0x0000, which falsifies the alternative that ES lives only in registers with no stored word. STILL UNFOUND, and now as a MEASURED NEGATIVE rather than an unattempted question: the MIDI.DAX music-timeline buffer. Both captured buffers decode cleanly under the format grammar (11,090 events, 0 malformed, clean 0xFC termination each) but BOTH appear verbatim inside Champions of Krynn/SOUND.DAX block 1 -- they are SFX-bank installs through the same generic slot-1 mechanism, not music. No static candidate cleared both its x86-code-alias disqualifier and its score bar either: the paragraph self-reference predicate returned 1 hit in 3 of 4 dumps against a shuffled-dump null of 0, and every survivor was disqualified as ordinary code or scored below the null's own maximum. Two pre-existing measurement bugs were fixed before any of it: a null sampler that drew 938 of an intended 1000 windows, and a case-insensitive-filesystem double-glob that counted every CoK .DAX twice (sources 1,592 -> 814, windows 45,504 -> 25,271) and had corrupted round 32's own top-5 with literal duplicate entries. Also corrected: the round plan's own driver-copy base formula (stub - 0x1b) matches block 3's on-disk bytes at 52/2151 = 2.4%, chance level, while the corrected formula matches 2096/2151 = 97.4% with every mismatch landing on the handshake cell and the AdLib scratch tables. A plan-supplied formula is a hypothesis, not a constant. tools/mididax_song_locate.py, docs/midi-dax-format.md 1.8.

ROUND 34 R6 (2026-09-04) CORRECTS THE 'MEASURED NEGATIVE' DIRECTLY ABOVE, not just narrows it (docs/engine/research/cok-sound-bank.md): SOUND.DAX block 1 is not merely an SFX bank. Its own header's first word (0x007d = 125, not the round-33 report's manually chosen 128) is a genuine, driver-disassembly-confirmed stream-start pointer -- the SAME 'mov ax, es:[0]; mov [cell], ax' install-time idiom independently confirmed in both MIDI.DAX block 1 and block 3. Segmenting the 13,936-byte stream on control-change markers finds three long, balanced, multi-voice passages (1,141 / 4,801 / 5,132 events, 5 voices each, Note-On/Off balance 0.994-0.999; corpus-wide totals 5,538 Note-On == 5,538 Note-Off exactly) -- the shape of real music, not short one-shot SFX. Three independent live GameLink RAM captures kept from round 33 (no new DOSBox-X session run this round) show the resident AdLib driver's own persisted cursor cell (block 3's 0x340, correcting the block-1-specific 0x2b7 the round-33 doc under-specified as universal) landing inside the largest, 4,801-event segment at two different points in a real session (an 'SSI presents' splash and live demo gameplay), with the cursor value itself advancing between nominally-identical captures -- evidence of a live, advancing playback position, not a frozen artifact. Round 33's 'this is SFX, not a song' verdict answered a different question (is this the MISSING music-timeline buffer) than this round's (does this SAME buffer ALSO hold song-shaped content the driver visits during play) -- the buffer holds BOTH short SFX-shaped fragments and long song-shaped passages. NOT (yet) claimed: that a real 0x388 AdLib OUT instruction fires from this exact code path during these specific captures -- block 3's static AdLib identity (port 0x388) was established in an earlier round from the driver's own disassembly, not re-verified against a live OUT trace this round, so audible hardware output remains inferred from driver identity, not directly observed this round. packages/engine/src/audio/dosSong.ts ports the decoder/segmenter to TypeScript (11/11 tests) but is NOT wired into apps/web/src/audio/gameAudio.ts as of this item (Phase B).

ROUND 35 R2 (2026-09-05) CORRECTS THE EVENT-FRAMING NUMBERS IN THE PARAGRAPH ABOVE: the event record is THREE bytes (2 data bytes + 1 trailing wait byte for 0x90/0x80 note events, 1 + 1 for 0xC0 program changes), measured from the driver's own code, not one. tools/mididax_event_frame.py derives each MIDI.DAX block's interpreter entry from its own slot-0 stub, disassembles it (capstone) and counts SI advancement per dispatch branch; blocks 1 (C/MS), 3 (AdLib), 4 (Tandy) and 5 (PC speaker) agree exactly, and block 2 (MPU-401) uses MIDI's own widths for 0xB0/0xD0/0xC0 plus the same trailing wait byte. That wait byte is the [0x2BD] per-tick counter (block 1: fetched 0x493, stored 0x4a0; block 3: fetched 0x4d3, stored to [0x346] at 0x4e0). Round 34's directional conclusion is strengthened, not overturned -- only the counts moved: 11,090 -> 3,699 real events (3,700 with the terminal 0xFC marker), 14 -> 7 segments (3 still song-like: 1,601 / 381 / 1,712 events, five voices each), 5,538/5,538 -> 1,846/1,846 Note-On/Note-Off pairs (against a shuffled-column null of 0.540), pitches 36..96, six velocity values, 7,860 ticks of timing. NOT a discriminator between framings: a clean 0xFC end with 0 malformed bytes passes under BOTH the old 1-byte grammar and the corrected 3-byte one, because malformed can only increment when a stream does not open on a status byte, which this one does either way -- so that count was never evidence for either framing and should not be cited as if it discriminated. Still decode-only; no playback, and no CoK tick rate is claimed, so no duration follows from the tick count. The pre-round-35 "#1 of 814 by >30x" corpus ranking was measured under the OLD 1-byte framing and has not been re-run under the corrected one. docs/engine/research/cok-sound-bank-framing.md, docs/midi-dax-format.md 1.10.

ecl.detail: Krynn Gen1 long-frame ECL is byte-decoded and the clean route executes retail ECL1 blocks 36, 16, 17, and 32 with shared memory and natural outcome resume.
gaps: ECL DECODE CENSUS, SHALLOW AND DEEP (round 33 R1, restated round 34 R1, 2026-09-04): disassembleEclBlock stops at each block's FIRST EXIT, so a clean-EXIT count is a LOWER BOUND -- it never walks the combat, quest or descriptor subroutines placed later in a block's own bytes. walkEclReachable (packages/engine/src/ecl/reachability.ts) follows all five ECL header entry points and every GOTO/GOSUB/ON_GOTO/ON_GOSUB. Measured on this title's 22 retail blocks: 0 shallow desync block(s), 0 deep desync site(s). ROUND 34 CORRECTION: this line read 33 deep sites until round 34 R1 added ECL opcode 0x41 to the SHARED Gen1 base table at wordSet 2 (packages/engine/src/ecl/opcodes.ts, ECL_OPCODE_MAX 0x40 -> 0x41). That single entry closed EVERY deep desync site this title had (33 -> 0), with zero shallow-census regression. R1 shipped this as UNKNOWN_0x41 with semantics explicitly unclaimed, because EclDump's own SetupCommandTable is dense only over 0x00..0x40, so its silence about 0x41 is a property of EclDump, not of the bytes. THAT IS NO LONGER THE STATE OF THE EVIDENCE. A round 34 follow-up (docs/engine/research/gen1-opcode-41.md) went and read the handlers: all three base-table titles carry their OWN 0x41 dispatch entry -- CoK GAME.OVR 0x4048, DoK 0x2e0e (reproducing the pre-existing build/dok-ecl-dispatch-map.json row byte-for-byte, which checks the tooling), Secret 0x43ff -- located by structural match against the CoAB oracle. Each reads exactly 2 operands from its own `mov al,2; push ax; lcall <parser>` prologue, so wordSet 2 is now confirmed from BINARY GROUND TRUTH and not only from the eight independent derivations that already agreed on it (Gateway, Treasures at GAME.OVR 0x2c40, Pools at 0x240c, Buck, Matrix, DQK Gen2, R1's byte-shape derivation, and now this one). All three handlers share one idiom: read a 0/1 flag and a round word amount, count the ACTIVE party members, divide, and ADD/ADC the share into a 32-bit per-character accumulator (flag=1 walks the party chain, flag=0 hits one target). CoK's walks that chain through CCH +0x17F/+0x181 -- the SAME 'next combatant' far pointer that CoK's already byte-verified post-combat calc_battle_exp uses (docs/engine/research/decompile-ovr006-xp-treasure.md), from an investigation that borrowed nothing from this one. The mnemonic is therefore now GEN1_AWARD_XP. uncertain STAYS TRUE and the reason is specific: no loader or save-format doc in this repo names the accumulator field (CoK +0x116/+0x118) as the canonical experience field, and no oracle certifies the label -- what is proven is the STRUCTURE, not the name. Note also that these handlers DIVIDE where Pools'/Treasures' own 0x41 (POOLS_AWARD_XP / TREASURES_AWARD_XP) MULTIPLIES by 100, so the dialects stay correctly separate. ONE OF R1'S OWN CLAIMS IS CORRECTED HERE: 'the operand is always a multiple of 500' is measured at 98.4% (121/123) on an exhaustive walk of every reached site in all three titles' ECL1-3.DAX, with two genuine CoK exceptions (ECL1.DAX block 32 @0x1cec = 300; ECL2.DAX block 67 @0x1bff = 32633), both in the flag=0 single-target branch. Stratified by the flag -- which R1's sample could not do -- flag=1 is 95/95 = 100%. The null: word-kind operands of every OTHER reached instruction in the same blocks are multiples of 500 just 0.53% of the time (n = 29,954), a ~185x enrichment, so the roundness is a property of THIS argument. Caveat kept: that follow-up's from-scratch walker reproduces walkEclReachable's CoK (33) and Secret (40) counts exactly but finds 50 DoK sites where the engine's numbers imply 43 -- a difference in its simplified control-flow rules, not a disputed fact about the opcode. The engine's pinned counts in eclReachability.test.ts are the authoritative ones. Pinned in packages/engine/test/eclReachability.test.ts; deep counts are SITES and shallow counts are BLOCKS, so the two are not directly subtractable.

gaps: RETRACTION (R1, 2026-09-03). This gap previously read that the Amiga single-bank wall-brick reassembly was EXHAUSTED and rejected — 96 hypotheses swept, plus a second blocker that the chunks' own palette is all-zero so no reassembly could be coloured. That was a TOOL BUG, not a property of the data: the sweep read the DOS bank with an 8-byte tile-STRIP parser when DoK's 256-tile banks are a 17-byte tile-ARRAY, so correct Amiga tiles were scored against garbage. With the corrected reader and a colour map derived from boot block 202's own palette, the natural chunk order (id, id+20, id+40, id+60) reproduces the DOS bank at 1786/1792 tiles byte-identical (99.7%), beating the best of the other 23 orders by 127 tiles on series 1 (255 vs 128 — that margin is measured on series 1, not aggregated over all seven) against a 1000-shuffle null of mean 3.37 / max 11. The all-zero-palette observation was true, and broader than reported (all 28 wall chunks carry one), but the inference drawn from it was wrong: the colours live in block 202.

Scope of that win, stated plainly: this is the SAME art DOS has, read from Amiga bytes. The toggle became truthful for DoK's walls; it did not make them richer. Six tiles (7 pixels, all in tile 255's bottom row) still differ.
It no longer falls back to DOS-EGA, but not every retail screen, animation, palette edge case, or picture placement is pixel-exact.
See docs/engine/research/dok-8x8d-amiga-format.md §3 for the corrected numbers, all three nulls, and the superseded original sections kept alongside them.

Measured 2026-09-05 (round 35 R5): ECL1#17's per-cell dispatcher emits 0 PICTURE effects across all 570 cells of the 38x15 map under EMPTY area memory with choose(0) at every step (also swept across all 8 backdrop values, 4,560 probes total, same result); the block's initial entry emits exactly picture 112, the id the host already hardcodes and paints. This is a scoped negative, not a general one: the block's own raw bytes contain two further PICTURE immediates the probe never reaches -- id 83 at block offset 4274 and id 85 at block offset 4587 -- and 17 of the 570 cells emit a `chain` whose target blocks were not measured. Not wired this round by design.

ROUND 36 R5 FOLLOW-UP (2026-09-05): the two PICTURE immediates round 35 R5's scoped negative named but never reached (id 83 at block offset 4274, id 85 at block offset 4587) ARE genuinely reachable, under a gate round 35's fresh-per-cell probe memory could never satisfy. walkEclReachable confirms both offsets decode to PICTURE and are statically reachable from ECL1#17's own header entries. The path condition, read off the disassembly and then run: [0x4cd0]==1 (the only live door into the encounter table -- [0x4cd0] has exactly ONE writer in the whole DoK ECL corpus, ECL3.DAX#98 at block offset 3245, reached via the retail chain ECL1#17 -> ECL3#96 -> ECL3#97 -> ECL3#98) AND [0x4c39]>=3 (the steps-since-last-encounter counter the ECL itself increments and zeroes; round 35's fresh-memory-per-cell probe could never carry it past 1). Swept over 16 memory configurations (the counter 0..7 x the flag {0,1}) x 570 retail cells = 9,120 probes: exactly 5 of 16 configurations fire (flag=1, counter in 3..7), 0 in the other 11, and the (0,0) corner of this grid reproduces round 35's own 0-picture baseline exactly. At a firing configuration: picture 85 is emitted 2 times by the VM and is host-visible 2 of 2 times -- it precedes COMBAT, which pauses the runner and lands it in DialogueTurn.pictureId. Picture 83 is emitted 6 times by the VM and is host-visible 0 of 6 times: it runs on, un-paused, into PICTURE #112 and EXIT inside the SAME effect batch, so the turn's last-wins pictureId reports 112 (the travel backdrop) at all 6 of those sites, never 83. Neither picture is ever painted regardless of that: openDokTravel calls openDialogueAt(runner, first, {title, spawn, onClose, onChain}) with no presentation, so renderPresentation's `if (!state?.presentation ...) return` (apps/web/src/ui/dialogue.ts:281) fires and currentPictureId stays null -- the same round-34 DialoguePresentation bug class as CoK's Throtl arrival (closed, round 35 R5) and Pool of Radiance's regional hosts (still open, see that profile's wilderness gap). It also decodes exactly one retail archive, BIGPIC1.DAX (blocks [112,113]); the actual art for both dropped sites lives elsewhere entirely -- block 83 is the sole block of PIC7.DAX, block 85 is in PIC1.DAX -- so a presentation fix alone would still need those two archives loaded. NOT FIXED THIS ROUND: apps/web belongs to another agent this round, so this is reported as a gap, not claimed as a capability. Pinned by packages/engine/test/dokOverlandPictureSites.test.ts, whose reachability and emission-count assertions were mutation-tested to RED (the site offset, the expected [0x4cd0] writer block/offset, the [0x4cd0] gate itself -- forcing it to 0 across the grid collapses the firing set from 5 to 0 -- picture 83 leaking from the effect batch into the host collector, and the PIC7.DAX block id). A further two-sided disclosure pin naming the missing-presentation defect directly (0 of 8 emissions painted, positive-controlled against the 3-4 of 18 other explore.ts call sites that DO pass a presentation) was being added to the same file concurrently this round (round 36 R7); its exact case count is not restated here since it was still being edited by that agent as this entry was written.

docs/engine/research/gateway-ending-route.md — Gateway `ending` leg, PROVEN (engine layer, static retail bytes + engine VM only; no native trace, no live browser wiring).

Ascore, `ECL6.DAX#20` (7644 B) / `GEO6.DAX#20` (1026 B), dialect `ECL_GEN1_SHORT_GATEWAY` (headerLen 22, vbase 0x7FFE, addend 0x8000, wordSetOverrides {0x1d:0,0x22:0,0x2c:1}, no cellDescAddr override), passed explicitly everywhere. **Dialect scope, verified:** on this block the Gateway split decodes identically to plain long `ECL_GEN1` (158 reachable instructions, 0 bad-opcode halts under both; no 0x1D/0x22/0x2C is reachable here). It *is* load-bearing against the sibling `ECL_GEN1_SHORT`, whose `0x0C=4` frame desyncs the stage-1 arm at `0x98D0` into a bad opcode at `0x98D9` and loses `LOAD_MONSTER #91,#2,#91`.

Header: magic 0x1388, vm_run_1 0x8161, search_location 0x809a, pre_camp_check 0x818d, camp_interrupted 0x81d7, initial_entry 0x8014 (= vbase+22; raw[22] = 0x09 SAVE, real boot code, not a GOTO trampoline).

Spawn grounded in the block's own initial_entry SAVEs: `0x805A SAVE #7,[0xC04C]` / `0x8060 SAVE #0,[0xC04B]` / `0x8066 SAVE #1,[0xC04D]` = **(0,7) facing east**, with `0x8030 SAVE #1,[0x4BE6]` (local map) and `0x8036 LOAD_FILES #20,#2,#255` (GEO block 20). Both `[0x4BF2]` re-entry guards fail cold — corpus-wide there are exactly two ECL writers of `[0x4BF2]`, `ECL5#99 @0x8014 SAVE #0` and `ECL5#98 @0x801C SAVE #1`, both part of the developer JUMPER debug pair. (The harness does not model `[0x4BF2]`, so the re-entry arms at 0x8071/0x8088 are documented but unexercised — correct for the cold boot this leg asserts.)

Dispatch: `0x80A1 AND #127,[0xC04F],[0x4C02]` (mask &0x7F is the script's own), `0x80AE COMPARE [0x4C02],#107 IF_GE GOTO 0x8113`, `0x8113 SUBTRACT #107,[0x4C02],[0x7F79]`, `0x811C ON_GOTO [0x7F79],#21,[...]` (idx16/17/18 = 0x977B/0x9799/0x97B7, idx20 = 0x83A3, idx0 = 0x89EE).

Encounter: a **three-stage chained mirror gauntlet**, descriptors 123/124/125, GEO cells (4,9)+(5,9) raw 0xFB, (4,6)+(5,6) raw 0xFC, (6,7)+(6,8) raw 0xFD. The stage is picked by the counter `[0x4C45]`, not by the wall (`0x97D3` COMPARE #1 -> 0x990F, `0x97DE` COMPARE #2 -> 0x9A17, `0x97E9` COMPARE #0 IF_NE EXIT). Rosters (three different fixed ones) against decoded `MON6CHA.DAX` — id 90 `ASCORE SKELETON`, id 91 `ASCORIAN MUMMY`: stage 1 `{91,2},{90,5}` (`0x98D7`/`0x98DE`, COMBAT `0x98E5`); stage 2 `{91,3},{90,3}` (`0x99B1`/`0x99B8`, COMBAT `0x99BF`); stage 3 `{91,1},{90,5}` (`0x9A94`/`0x9A9B`, COMBAT `0x9AA2`). All three `SETUP_MONSTER #255,#1,#255`, `PICTURE #25`. Retail narration verbatim: stage 1 "YOU STAND BY THE WALL, BUT ONLY SHREDS OF THE ANCIENT TAPESTRY NOW HANG FROM THE CEILING. THE MAP IT ONCE CONTAINED HAS ROTTED." / "THE WALL ITSELF IS COVERED WITH A TREMENDOUS MIRROR. " / "SQUINTING, YOU THINK YOU SEE YOUR FACES REFLECTED AS THOSE OF LEERING SKELETONS!"; stage 2 "THE TAPESTRY BESIDE THIS WALL, TOO, HAS CRUMBLED INTO DUST. " / "BEFORE YOU CAN EXAMINE THE BROAD MIRROR, THE SOUND OF BONES RATTLING BEHIND YOU SIGNALS THE BEGINNING OF ANOTHER BATTLE."; stage 3 "YOU ARE ON YOUR GUARD AGAINST FURTHER UNDEAD ATTACKS. THE ASCOREAN HOSTS DO NOT DISAPPOINT YOU, CHARGING FEARLESSLY TOWARDS THE PARTY."

Persistence, corpus-wide census — a raw-byte scan of ECL2..ECL6 with no reachability filtering finds **every** occurrence of both operand encodings inside `ECL6.DAX#20` and nowhere else: `[0x4C45]` 4 writers `@0x97F1 SAVE #1` / `@0x990F SAVE #2` / `@0x9A17 SAVE #3` / `@0x9ADA SAVE #4` plus 4 reads (8 occurrences); `[0x4C46]` 3 writers `@0x978C OR #1` / `@0x97AA OR #2` / `@0x97C8 OR #4` plus 6 reads (9 occurrences) — one word carrying three independent per-wall bits. **Multi-stage requirement met:** the terminal flag is written by `vm_run_1`'s `GOSUB 0x9AD2` (`COMPARE [0x4C45],#3 ; IF_NE ; RETURN ; 0x9ADA SAVE #4`), so it is provably still clear (1, then 2) after stages 1 and 2 and set only on the walk step after stage 3. Both the bits and the counter are written EAGERLY, before each stage's COMBAT — asserted at the combat pause and again after victory. Payoff: hidden-pit `DAMAGE #1,#129,#1,[0x7F7F],#100` then `CLEARMONSTERS` + `TREASURE` (itemBlockId 30, contents not decoded) + rosterless `COMBAT`.

Reachability over the real wall/door graph: **step_count 27, required_interactions [], final_facing west**; only two non-plain edges, both `door_flag 1` automatic — `(7,10)->(7,9)` and `(7,9)->(6,9)`. **The descriptor-127 checkpoint at (7,10) is forced**, proven by a BFS restricted to `door_flag 0/1` edges with no descriptor blocking: it yields the same 27-step path, and blocking (7,10) alone makes all three mirror cells — (5,9), (5,6) and (6,7) — unreachable. (The only alternative entrance, via desc-27 cell (3,6), needs a `door_flag 2` bash/pick/knock edge at `(2,6)->(3,6)`.) The checkpoint arm `0x83A3` prints "UNDEAD GUARDS COME AROUND THE CORNER." and is consumed by `0x8465 SAVE #1,[0x4C09]`. Continuations `5,9->5,6` (3 steps) and `5,6->6,7` (2 steps), both `required_interactions []`.

"Later" is evidence-backed: block 20 is the **highest-numbered local-map (dungeon/town) area** — the corpus `SAVE #1,[0x4BE6]` sites run 1..20 ascending across ECL2..ECL6 and end at #20; ECL6 additionally holds #21 (the overland/wilderness hub, `SAVE #0,[0x4BE6]`, already this game's proven wilderness leg) plus the endgame pair #27/#28. `ECL3#14` @0x8F3A: "'YOU HAVE ALL THE STATUETTES! NOW YOU MUST HURRY TO ASCORE. ...'". Block 20's own fiction: @0x894F "'WELCOME TO CENTRAL ASCORE!' ... 'PLEASE CONSULT THE TAPESTRIES OPPOSITE EACH WALL FOR DETAILED MAPS." and @0x9668 the mage's note "'HAVE YOU BROKEN THE MIRRORS' SPELL YET? ... FINISH NOW! V.'". Its descriptor 107 at (12,15) runs `0x8A02 NEWECL #27` into Vaalgamon's endgame maze, which returns via `NEWECL #20 @0x8622` and hands off to the finale via `NEWECL #28 @0x8A7F`. **This leg is the last walked, cell-dispatched encounter area — not the finale itself**; #27 and #28 are linear scripts (all four handler entries point at 0x8014, byte 0x00 = EXIT) and cannot be cell-dispatched legs.

Golden: `packages/engine/test/gatewayEndingRoute.test.ts`, 8 tests (A, B, B2, C, D-E, F, G, H), reads retail `ECL6.DAX`/`GEO6.DAX`/`MON6CHA.DAX`, `describe.skipIf(!haveRetail)` + `it.skipIf` on the monster archive, dialect passed explicitly, seed 0x1234. Research doc: `docs/engine/research/gateway-ending-route.md` (8-row REJECTED table). Gates: `pnpm --filter @goldbox/engine test` and `pnpm -r exec tsc --noEmit` clean.

Harness gaps, disclosed and non-load-bearing: the engine's PRINT models only inline/strref operands, so numeric `PRINT #1`/`PRINT [0x7F7F]` and `LOAD_CHARACTER` contribute no text (journal number and damage roll are missing in the harness, not in the data); per-step VM re-seeding makes the two 5% wandering-undead arms (descriptors 1 and 3) deterministically silent — no mirror arm contains a RANDOM; combats are resolved with `afterCombat('victory')` rather than simulated; and goldens F and G posit the flag state (`new Map([[0x4c45,4],[0x4c46,7]])` and two single-bit maps) rather than walking to it — test D-E does prove the walk reaches exactly that state, and perturbing F to an empty map makes the cell fire combat again, so F/G are corroborating assertions about VM behaviour under a posited state rather than additional walked evidence. NOT live-wired: no `?explore=` route and no e2e run.

middle.citation: docs/engine/research/gateway-middle-route.md — the shipwreck island (Gateway's MIDDLE natural-combat route, archive-distinct from the early anchor ECL2#1). ECL4.DAX#12 (3464 bytes, dialect ECL_GEN1_SHORT_GATEWAY, addend 0x8000) + GEO4.DAX#12. Spawn is grounded in the block's own initial_entry 0x8014 (= offset 22): SAVE #13->[0xC04C] @0x804F (09000d014cc0), SAVE #13->[0xC04B] @0x8055 (09000d014bc0), SAVE #0->[0xC04D] @0x805B (090000014dc0), with SAVE #1->[0x4BE6] @0x8030 and LOAD_FILES #12,#2,#255 @0x8036 selecting GEO block 12 — no chooseStart heuristic. search_location @0x831A masks the descriptor with the script's own AND #127,[0xC04F]->[0x4C02] @0x8321 (18 of 256 GEO descriptor bytes differ between &0x3F and &0x7F here, so the MASK is discriminating), then dispatches the high band via SUBTRACT #124 @0x8368 and ON_GOTO @0x8371 -> 124:0x8978, 125:0x8A97, 126:0x8B6E, 127:0x8C3C. Dialect note (independently re-measured, correcting the research doc's §10 row): the DIALECT choice discriminates only against the ECL_GEN1_SHORT family — ECL_GEN1_SHORT and ECL_GEN1_SHORT_TREASURES desync at 0x0C SETUP_MONSTER and yield kind 'end' with no roster, whereas plain ECL_GEN1 yields results identical to ECL_GEN1_SHORT_GATEWAY on both encounter cells. Reachability is proven over the real wall/door graph (tools/find_geo_path.py --geo <retail>/GEO4.DAX --block 12 --start 13,13 --target 14,5 --facing north): 19 steps N,N,E,E,N,N,W,S,W,W,N,N,E,E,E,N,W,N,N, final facing north, required_interactions [], and exactly one non-trivial edge — (14,6) north -> (14,5) wall_slot 15 with door_flag 1 (automatic; door byte raw[770+6*16+14]=0x01); a census of all 1024 directed edges of GEO4#12 finds 984 flag-0 and 40 flag-1 edges and ZERO flag-2/flag-3 edges anywhere on the map. The route forces TWO encounters: (12,10) raw 0x7E is the map's ONLY descriptor-126 cell and is a genuine articulation point (BFS reaches 70 cells from the spawn, 28 with it removed; --avoid-event-index 126 reports the lighthouse unreachable). Arm 126 @0x8B6E gates on COMPARE [0x4C09],#1, prints "THREE TALL, FOUL-SMELLING CREATURES ARE KNEELING IN THE CENTER OF THIS BEACH... AND THEN ATTACK!", PICTURE #41, LOAD_MONSTER #69,#3,#69 -> [{monsterId:69,count:3,picBlockId:69}] = SCRAG x3 (MON4CHA.DAX#69 = "SCRAG"), COMBAT @0x8C31, then SAVE #1->[0x4C09] @0x8C32. Arm 124 @0x8978 (cells (14,4),(14,5),(15,5) raw 0xFC) gates on COMPARE [0x4C0B],#1, prints "SEVERAL MEN ARE IN THE LIGHTHOUSE KEEPER'S QUARTERS, RUMMAGING THROUGH ITS CABINETS AND CHESTS. THEY ATTACK!", PICTURE #40, LOAD_MONSTER #70,#5,#70 + #69,#1,#69 -> [{monsterId:70,count:5,picBlockId:70},{monsterId:69,count:1,picBlockId:69}] = PIRATE x5 + SCRAG x1, COMBAT @0x89F1, then SAVE #1->[0x4C0B] @0x89F2 and the douse-the-light question at CALL [0x080C] @0x8A84 whose non-equal branch writes [0x4C36] @0x8A8D (modelled as choice index 0 = YES, per the engine's EclCallHostResult contract and the precedent set by Gateway's early leg — the index-to-YES polarity is a project convention, not a proven retail fact; the persistence result is polarity-independent because 0x89F2 precedes the fork). Persistence: both consumed cells revisit silently on the retail words and re-fire identically on fresh memory; the consumed [0x4C0B] additionally silences a DIFFERENT cell, (15,7) descriptor 12 @0x880F (the burning-lamp description), four steps back down the route, while (14,6) descriptor 13 @0x8882 is facing-gated (COMPARE [0xC04D],#0) rather than flag-gated. [0x4C36] has exactly two sites in ECL2/3/4/5/6.DAX: this write and a read at ECL4.DAX#13 @0x9295 SUBTRACT [0x4C36],[0x7F79]->[0x7F79] — recorded but deliberately NOT claimed as the quest leg. Narrative placement is inference, not bytes: cold-booting the ECL4 siblings shows #12 follows a sea voyage (#8 ships-to-Tuern, #10 arrival in UTTERSEA) and precedes #13 ("YOU PULL YOUR SMALL, BATTERED BOAT ONTO THE NARROW BEACH"), so it is provably not the campaign start, but "middle rather than late" is not established. Byte-grounded engine golden reading the retail files: packages/engine/test/gatewayMiddleRoute.test.ts (11 tests, existsSync-guarded, dialect passed explicitly at every call site, including the articulation-point BFS, the &0x3F counterfactual, the YES/NO fork, and the disclosure that descriptor-1 open terrain — 14 of the 20 walked cells (spawn + 19 steps) — carries a live 3% wandering-monster roll @0x8532 that is silent at the walk's seed but fires "SCRAG ATTACK!" with [0x4C17]=1 at seed 2003; note the golden reseeds the PRNG per step, so the walk's silence is one repeated first draw rather than 14 independent rolls). Two further reviewer-raised caveats, recorded rather than smoothed: golden test G proves the silent legal revisit on a hand-constructed memory map ({0x4C09:1, 0x4C0B:1}) rather than on the map the walk in test D carries forward — those are exactly the two words this route writes and the fresh-memory negative control is genuine, but the state is synthesized; and the research doc's rejected-candidate name for ECL4#11 ("Gundarlun") is unsourced (that block emits no print effects on a cold initial_entry), unlike ECL4#8/#10, whose names come from their own retail text — both now flagged in the doc. Live browser wiring is NOT claimed: no explore-route id and no e2e acceptance were added for this leg. Independently re-verified 2026-08-05 by a skeptic pass: all container/header/spawn/dispatch/GEO/roster/reachability/corpus-census claims reproduced from the retail bytes with a separately written decoder, and 17 mutation perturbations of the golden were all caught.

quest.citation:
docs/engine/research/gateway-quest-flag.md — quest, PROVEN (static retail bytes + this repo's EclVm only; no DOSBox-X/native capture, no browser wiring). Cross-archive quest flag `[0x4C21]` "Amanitas rescued".

SETTER: `ECL3.DAX#5` (Everlund, 5690 bytes; magic 0x1388, search_location 0x807C, initial_entry 0x8014) at vaddr **0x9026** (file offset 4136) `09 00 01 01 21 4c` = `SAVE #1 -> [0x4C21]`, reached unconditionally after the Amanitas-rescue COMBAT (0x8F12 `24`) and its own consumed bit 0x8F13 `09 00 01 01 32 4c` (`SAVE #1 -> [0x4C32]`). "Everlund" is byte-supported, not inferred: the block's own retail text names itself ("A BRASS PLATE ON THE WALL HERE READS: EVERLUND TOWN HALL" at (6,8); "YOU STEP INSIDE THE ANCIENT CITY GATES OF EVERLUND" at (8,15)). Dispatch cell **`GEO3.DAX#5` (5,13), raw floor byte 0xF9, mask &0x7F** (the block's own `AND #127` at 0x8083 `2f 00 7f 01 4f c0 01 02 4c`) -> descriptor 121 -> second ON_GOTO table @0x80F2 index 3 -> arm **0x8E3B**. Roster `LOAD_MONSTER #4,#2,#4` @0x8F04 + `#23,#2,#23` @0x8F0B = **MON3CHA.DAX#4 ZHENTIL FIGHTER x2 + MON3CHA.DAX#23 OWLBEAR x2**. Retail narration verbatim: "ON THE FAR SIDE OF THE ROOM AN OLD MAN STANDS CHAINED TO THE WALL, A DROOLING OWLBEAR FACING HIM ON EITHER SIDE. TWO MEN WATCH, AND ONE OF THEM IS SAYING '...HIM TRY TO CAST A SPELL--THEY'LL TEAR HIS ARMS OFF!'"; post-victory "'WELL, WELL, WELL,' ... YOU RECORD WHAT HAPPENS NEXT AS JOURNAL ENTRY #29." and "'GO NOW,' SAYS AMANITAS. ... YARTAR SHOULD BE YOUR FIRST DESTINATION--WE KNOW THE KRAKEN HAVE A BASE THERE."

WRITE SET EXHAUSTIVE, two agreeing methods (stack-aware CFG walk over all 26 Gateway ECL blocks, and a raw scan for the direct-memory operand encoding `01 21 4c`): **exactly 12 references corpus-wide — ONE write (ECL3.DAX#5 @0x9026) and ELEVEN COMPARE reads**, at `ECL2.DAX#1` 0x845E/0x8629/0x863F/0x8665/0x867B/0x8C97/0x917D/0x9378, `ECL2.DAX#4` 0x96FB/0x992F, `ECL3.DAX#14` 0x85B9. Ten of the eleven are in a different archive from the writer; none is in the setter's own block. The scan was independently extended to the other operand codes the VM resolves to the same word (0x02, 0x03, 0x7F — zero hits each) and to the runtime-string code 0x81 (three hits, all inside 6-bit packed string payloads following PRINT/PRINTCLEAR, none in a SAVE frame), so no non-0x01 addressing form writes or reads `[0x4C21]` either. The census is scoped to ECL bytecode operand references; it makes no claim about host-side range clears.

CONSUMER: `ECL2.DAX#1` (Yartar, 7578 bytes) ON_GOTO arm 30 (table base file offset 714, arm operand `01 7d 91`) -> **0x917D** `03 01 21 4c 00 00` / 0x9183 `16` IF_EQ / 0x9184 `01 01 d2 89` GOTO 0x89D2. Dispatch cell **`GEO2.DAX#1` (14,2), raw 0x9E, masked 30 — the only masked-30 cell on the map**. FLAG SET -> 0x9188 `03 01 03 4c 00 01`, 0x91AA `0c 00 ff 00 00 00 ff`, 0x91B1 `0b 00 00 00 06 00 00`, 0x91B8 `24` COMBAT, 0x91B9 `09 00 01 01 03 4c`: turn `{kind:'combat', text:'KRAKEN SPIES ATTACK!', monsters:[{monsterId:0,count:6,picBlockId:0}], setup:{spriteId:255,maxDistance:0,picId:255}, pictureId:14}` = **MON2CHA.DAX#0 KRAKEN SPY x6**. FLAG CLEAR (negative control) -> the same cell yields `{kind:'say', text:"'WHAT'LL IT BE?'", awaiting:'menu', choices:['FIGHT','LEAVE'], pictureId:6}`, no roster, `[0x4C03]` untouched.

REACHABILITY: spawn grounded in ECL2#1's own initial_entry re-entry arm (0x8065 `COMPARE [0x4BF2],#21`; 0x835B `09 01 b2 03 01 4d c0`; 0x8372 `COMPARE [0xC04D],#2`; 0x838D `09 00 00 01 4c c0`, 0x8393 `09 00 0b 01 4b c0`) = **(11,0) facing south**, VM-verified. `tools/find_geo_path.py --geo "C:/Program Files (x86)/GOG Galaxy/Games/Gateway to the Savage Frontier/GEO2.DAX" --block 1 --start 11,0 --target 14,2 --facing north --event-mask 127` (the tool needs the FULL retail path; a bare `GEO2.DAX` raises FileNotFoundError): **step_count 5**, directions **south, south, east, east, east**, final_facing east, blocked_cell_count 0, **required_interactions []**, one door edge (13,2)->east->(14,2) wall slot 1 **door flag 1 (automatic)**; **no flag-2/flag-3 edge**. Every intermediate executed through the real VM: (11,1) 0x00 silent; **(11,2) 0x27/39 silent with the flag set, thug-rescue BANDIT x5 with it clear**; (12,2) 0x00 silent; (13,2) 0x1D/29 "A BRIGHT, MULTICOLORED BANNER FLIES OVER THIS DOOR. ON IT ARE STITCHED THE WORDS: THREE RIVERS FESTHALL". Seed-independent (0x1234 and 0x5678 identical): only two descriptor-0 cells are crossed so `[0x4C00]` ends at 2, below arm 0's ">5" wandering gate, so the RANDOM at 0x843C is never reached. Setter cell also proven reachable with the same tool (again full retail path, `--geo <retail>/GEO3.DAX --block 5`): (8,15)->(5,13), 29 steps, blocked 0, required_interactions [], all seven door edges flag 1.

PERSISTENCE: `[0x4C03]` unset -> 1 across `afterCombat('victory')` (0x91B9, unconditional, after COMBAT); silent legal revisit `{kind:'end', text:''}` with `[0x4C03]`=1 and `[0x4C21]`=1 preserved; the quest flag has no second writer so it is never cleared (again: scoped to ECL operand references, silent about host-side clears). End-to-end golden carries the setter's own memory Map into ECL2#1.

FURTHER CROSS-BLOCK CONSUMERS asserted: 0x9378 (the flag permanently silences the early leg's Yartar thug rescue at (11,2) without writing `[0x4C20]`); 0x8C97 (the Waterbaron at (10,7)/(10,8) records "JOURNAL ENTRY #9." vs "JOURNAL ENTRY #32.", asserted as `toContain` because this arm's `GOTO 0x9A71` reaches the unmodelled host `CALL [0xC01E]` and the collected text repeats — a known VM gap, not retail behaviour).

Golden: `packages/engine/test/gatewayQuestFlag.test.ts` — 14 tests A/B/C/C2/D/E/F/G/G2/H/I/J/K/L, all reading the real retail files, guarded by `describe.skipIf(!haveRetail)` at the suite level plus one `it.skipIf` for the MONnCHA archives (the research doc's header previously said "`it.skipIf` guarded"; corrected). Research doc: `docs/engine/research/gateway-quest-flag.md` (includes a 17-row REJECTED table; its "the Kraken base under Yartar" label for ECL2.DAX#4 is now explicitly marked as inference). Registry seeded: `tools/map_gen1_cross_area_flag_reads.py` gained a `gateway-to-the-savage-frontier` FLAG_REGISTRY entry (additive only; the scan was run with explicit `--json`/`--markdown` into a session scratchpad, the checked-in corpus report was NOT touched).

DISCLOSED LIMITS, do not overstate: (a) `[0x4C03]` is SHARED scratch written by 8 blocks, and 0x9188 tests EQUALITY with 1, so a carried `[0x4C03]==1` (e.g. from ECL3#5's own Everlund street counter at 0x848F, `04 00 01 01 03 4c 01 03 4c` = ADD #1,[0x4C03]->[0x4C03]) suppresses the ambush while 0 or 2..5 do not — whether the retail engine zeroes this range on area change is NOT proven (asserted as a disclosure in test J; the load-bearing fork at 0x917D provably runs first, so the leg does not depend on it). (b) The best story beat, the Yartar city-gate Kraken abduction at `vm_run_1` 0x8665 (`NEWECL #2`), is documented but NOT asserted because it needs `[0x7ED5] != 0` and `[0x7ED5]` has zero ECL writers corpus-wide (host-owned). (c) `[0x4BF2]=21` and `[0x03B2]=2` are host inputs that only select which of the block's own spawn arms runs; the fork itself is asserted independently of the spawn. (d) Cross-block memory continuity is modelled as one flat 16-bit-word Map, never natively observed; the retail scripts use [0x4C20]/[0x4C21]/[0x4C22] as independent adjacent flags, which implies byte-addressed storage — for 0/1 values the two models coincide and nothing here depends on the difference. (e) "Three Rivers Festhall interior" is an inference from the adjacent sign cell (13,2), labelled as such. (f) The `&0x7F` mask IS discriminating on the setter cell (0xF9: &0x7F=121 vs &0x3F=57; the 57 reading produces no encounter — test K), unlike the early leg where it was not. (g) The Gateway dialect discriminates against `ECL_GEN1_SHORT` (which desyncs and loses the roster and COMBAT entirely) but NOT against plain long `ECL_GEN1`, which gives an identical result — so this route alone does not prove the Gateway split (test L). No deferred wiring: no `?explore=` route was added; this is engine-level only.

Gates: `pnpm --filter @goldbox/engine test` and `pnpm -r exec tsc --noEmit` clean.

ecl.detail: Gateway has its own byte-justified dialect ECL_GEN1_SHORT_GATEWAY (headerLen 22, vbase 0x7FFE, short 0x1D/0x22/0x2C, but the LONG 3-operand 0x0C SETUP_MONSTER frame — 237 of 238 reachable sites decode cleanly only under 3 operands, which is what splits it from the DoK/Treasures/PoD sibling). Blocks from all five ECL archives execute against retail bytes: ECL2#1 (Yartar start), ECL4#12 (shipwreck island), ECL5#19 (Sundabar), ECL6#20 (Ascore ending), ECL6#21 (overland), and the cross-archive ECL3#5 -> ECL2#1/#4, ECL3#14 quest-flag dependency.
gaps: Coverage is of REACHABLE code on the routed blocks; the archives' unreached arms are decoded but unexecuted.

The RANDOM (0x08) inclusive-maximum host quirk is byte-proven from GAME.OVR, and as of 2026-09-03 Gateway's full opcode dispatch IS mapped from its own retail bytes: dispatcher 0.9880 at 0x43f3 (runner-up null 0.3419, same-length non-dispatcher null 0.2994), operand parser 0.9917 at 0x9471, 65 handlers (docs/engine/research/gateway-ecl-dispatch-map.md). Six word sets were corrected against the binary (0x1D/0x22/0x2C/0x32/0x40/0x41); five are corpus-null and 0x41 fixes a real desync at ECL5.DAX#99@0x428. Remaining: 6 desyncs where the binary contradicts BOTH the shipped dialect and the plain-Gen1 alternative — these sit in the 'free' partition, which a shipped-vs-alternative comparison structurally cannot see, and 31 of the opcodes stay vacuous because the binary yields no count.

ECL DECODE CENSUS, SHALLOW AND DEEP (round 33 R1, 2026-09-04): disassembleEclBlock stops at each block's FIRST EXIT, so every clean-EXIT count this project has ever published is a LOWER BOUND -- it never walks the combat, quest or descriptor subroutines placed later in a block's own bytes. walkEclReachable (packages/engine/src/ecl/reachability.ts) follows all five ECL header entry points and every GOTO/GOSUB/ON_GOTO/ON_GOSUB. Measured on this title's 26 retail blocks: 0 shallow desync block(s), 0 deep desync site(s). Deep and shallow agree here (0 each), which is a result and not a default -- 6 of the 11 Gen1 titles disagree. Pinned in packages/engine/test/eclReachability.test.ts; the deep counts are SITES and the shallow counts are BLOCKS, so the two are not directly subtractable.

graphics.detail: Gateway's VGA picture family (TITLE, BIGPIC1, BODY, CPIC2..6) is decoded as 17-byte header + 33-byte prefix + five one-bit planes, LSB plane first — a layout corrected against a native CPIC/RAM oracle after an earlier same-byte-count reading was refuted. The intro renders five non-blank retail frames and the wilderness uses the same planar5 compositor over Gateway's recovered 50x25 WILDCOM/RANDCOM floor. EXTENDED 2026-08-09: Gateway is the second GLIB/DataLib-era title with a live in-dungeon DOS-EGA<->Amiga wall-art toggle (?explore=gateway-amiga, ECL2/GEO2 block 2), source-verified rather than approximated — 13 of the Amiga WallDef.glb records are BYTE-IDENTICAL to the DOS WALLDEF blocks of the same id (780 bytes each), tile alignment is shift 0, and the Amiga bank 3 is a complete redraw of every painted wall tile in GEO2#2 with zero padding/painted disagreements. The 5-plane Walls.tlb master carries no colour table, so the palette comes from DiskA/Always.tlb.
gaps: The toggle is area-scoped, not title-wide: 25 of the 26 paired Amiga banks are slot-for-slot stand-ins but block 15 carries real art in slots 186-189 that the DOS bank pads flat, and ECL5#19's LOAD_PIECES (7,15,30) mounts it, so the bankSwapParity guard keeps the Sundabar campaign areas on DOS art.
Default tactical-combat chrome is a presentation gap rather than retail composition.
Native 320x200 screen composition, broad picture/animation coverage, and palette timing parity remain incomplete.

map_container.detail: The selected-folder source drives numbered DAX banks (ECL/GEO/WALLDEF/8X8D/MON*/ITEM per disk) plus Gateway's shared WALLDEF.DAX/8X8D.DAX and its block-201 font / block-202 frame out of 8X8D1, for legal movement on ECL5/GEO5#19 and the ECL6#21 overland map with all six dynamic GEO selectors and their banks.
gaps: No repacking or write-side support for Gateway's archives is claimed.

quests.detail: The cross-archive quest flag [0x4C21] ('Amanitas rescued') is proven engine-level from static retail bytes: written by exactly one instruction in the whole five-archive corpus (ECL3.DAX#5, Everlund) and read by ECL2.DAX#1, ECL2.DAX#4 and ECL3.DAX#14, with the consumers' available content demonstrably changing. A browser route (?explore=gateway-quest) now walks both arms: winning the Amanitas-rescue combat sets the flag and hands the party from Everlund to Yartar's (11,0,south) re-entry spawn, where a six-KRAKEN-SPY ambush is waiting; the negative control (?explore=gateway-quest&yartar=1) reseeds the same host inputs without the flag and lands at the identical spawn with a plain 'WHAT'LL IT BE?' tavern menu (FIGHT/LEAVE) and no combat.
gaps: The Everlund-to-Yartar handover is memory-carry modelled, not natively walked: the engine reseeds [0x4BF2]/[0x03B2] and switches area on combat victory rather than crossing a single continuous GEO map over the disk boundary, so the crossing itself (as opposed to its two endpoints) has no native evidence.
The wider quest graph, journal semantics, campaign choices, and ending state are not covered.
No DOSBox-X or native capture was used for this leg and none is claimed.

retail_save.detail: Greybox save version 2 round-trips Gateway's routed state — area, pose, clock, party, and ECL memory — including the wilderness controller's own dedicated save/reload, and the Sundabar route's consumed word [0x4C6C] survives it. This is Greybox persistence, not original-DOS save interoperability.

gaps: No retail-compatible Gateway party or campaign-save encoder and no retail-executable acceptance proof exist.

gaps: No Greybox reader or writer for Gateway's own SAVGAM/CHRDAT sidecar format exists.
Gateway character, party, quest, and sidecar save structures are not mapped into a shipping importer.
import.scope: No selected-folder importer for Gateway retail party or campaign saves is shipped. A native GameLink session did produce and re-load a genuine 13,149-byte SAVGAMA.DAT (hash/offset manifest committed as gateway-sundabar-native-evidence.json, retail bytes not redistributed), which shows the format is reachable — not that Greybox reads it.

ruleset.detail: Gateway runs on Greybox's shared AD&D party, first-person exploration, dialogue, tactical combat, treasure, and version-2 persistence systems, plus this title's own NPC-companion handling (roster order and the companion-gated wilderness exit are exercised by dedicated browser acceptances).
gaps: Exhaustive retail spell, item, class, XP-table, monster-AI, and combat-rule parity is not claimed.
Savage Frontier NPC join/leave rules are covered only where a routed leg exercises them.

towns.detail: Sundabar is a real GEO-backed town map (GEO5.DAX#19, 16x16, shops at descriptors 6/10, the Auld Macdon tavern at 18, city gates) and is mounted by two browser routes: ?explore=gateway at the natively-captured (15,2,W) arrival pose, and ?explore=gateway-natural at the (0,10,E) west gate the block's own initial_entry writes for the wilderness-arrival branch. Town ENTRY and EXIT are not wired live: the routes mount block 19 directly rather than crossing in from ECL6#21's ENTER SUNDABAR? NEWECL.

ending.citation:
ECL1.DAX = 251,712 bytes, 30 blocks [4,16..40,47,49,50,51]; GEO1.DAX = 29,983 bytes, 41 blocks [16..40,47..62]. Gen1 addressing vbase 0x7FFE, file offset = vaddr-0x8000+2. Block 38 header: vm_run_1 0x8548 / search_location 0x85F9 / pre_camp 0x8059 / camp_int 0x80C0 / initial_entry 0x8014.

DISPATCH: 0x8610 `2f 00 7f 01 2d 00 01 9a 00` = AND #127,[0x002d]->[0x009a] (Treasures reads its cell descriptor from [0x002d], per EclDialect.cellDescAddr, NOT [0xc04f]); 0x861D COMPARE [0x009a],#21; IF_GE; GOTO 0x866D, otherwise the 21-target ON_GOTO at 0x8628 (indices 0..20). 0x866D `05 00 79 01 9a 00 01 bf 00` = SUBTRACT #121,[0x009a]->[0x00bf] (SUBTRACT is op2-op1); 0x8676 ON_GOTO [0x00bf],#7 -> [0x9227,0xA41A,0xA5B6,0xA6C1,0xA789,0xA7A9,0xA849], 0-based, so index 0 (descriptor&0x7F==121) is 0x9227.

GEO: GEO1#38 is 1026 bytes, 16x16, 36 distinct descriptor values; descriptors raw[514:770] index y*16+x. Exactly two cells mask to 121, (2,6) and (3,6), both raw 0xF9; 0xF9 is the only value in the map that masks to 121. find_geo_path (7,8)->(3,6) facing north, event-mask 127 returns 6 steps W,W,N,W,N,W through event indices 12,0,0,0,0,20,121, blocked_cell_count 0, no required interactions, final facing west. The (7,8) re-entry cell's descriptor 0x8C masks to index 12, which the ON_GOTO at 0x8628 dispatches to [0x8B95] (COMPARE [0011],#1; IF_NE; EXIT, then the PRINTCLEAR at ~0x8B9C "AT YOUR FEET IS A STAIRWAY THAT LEADS DOWN INTO A TUNNEL. YOU RECALL THAT THIS IS THE OPENING THROUGH WHICH YOU ENTERED THIS CAVERN."). NB [0x88DA] is index 11, a different cell ("THE PATHWAY ENDS HERE, COVERED BY AN AVALANCHE OF ROCKS AND BOULDERS."). The only non-zero intermediate descriptor, (4,6) index 20, dispatches to [0x9010] (COMPARE [0011],#0; IF_NE; EXIT, then "THE CEILING OF THE CAVERN RISES HIGH OVER YOUR HEADS...").

COMBATS: 0x944A SETUP_MONSTER #112,#0,#255,[00c6]; the placement fork at 0x9415 `03 01 34 00 00 02` = COMPARE [0034],#2; IF_EQ; GOTO 0x944A sets [00c6]=15 from (2,6) and 11 from (3,6). Wave 1 roster is twelve groups: (28x3, 127x1, 112x1, 126x1) TWICE from the [0044] loop (0x9454..0x9493), then 28x3, then 127x[00c7], 112x[00c8], 126x[00c8] scaled by 0x949D `06 01 39 02 00 05 01 c8 00` = DIVIDE [0239],#5->[00c8]; ADD #5,[00c8]->[00c7]; ADD #4,[00c8]->[00c8] (0/25/60/99 -> 5-4-4 / 10-9-9 / 17-16-16 / 24-23-23). Wave 2: 0x9F2B `0b 00 58 00 01 00 58` = LOAD_MONSTER #88 x1; 0x9F32 `24 17 01` = COMBAT; IF_NE; GOTO 0xA91F (defeat).

LATCH: 0x9F3B `09 00 01 01 5c 02` = SAVE #1 -> [0x025C] (Gen1 SAVE is source,dest — destination last), carrying no re-entry guard. Addressing: Gen1 vbase 0x7FFE, file offset = vaddr - 0x8000 + 2; dialect ECL_GEN1_SHORT_TREASURES (word sets {0x0C:4, 0x1D:0, 0x21:2, 0x22:0, 0x23:0, 0x2C:1}, cellDescAddr 0x002d, opcodeOverride 0x42); SAVE is (source, destination) with destination LAST.

CONTAINERS. ECL1.DAX = 251,712 B, 30 blocks, ids [4,16..40,47,49,50,51]; GEO1.DAX = 41 blocks, of which 48 and 52..62 have no same-id ECL block. GAME.OVR = 310,572 B, magic "FBOV" at offset 0 (Borland VROOMM overlay pool). GAME.EXE = 71,971 B; a `CD 3F 00 00` + dword fileofs + word codesz + word fixupsz + word jmpcnt sweep yields 47 records (about nine are obvious junk matches). Descriptor @0x0728 -> GAME.OVR segment base 0x07354, codesz 0x1A42 (the ECL memory accessors); @0x0806 -> base 0x0C5B7, codesz 0x21B0 (SetupGroundTiles). Both bases are corroborated by the code itself: `mov di,0x0EDC` / `mov di,0x0EE4` exactly equal (0xD493-0xC5B7) / (0xD49B-0xC5B7), the DungCom/WildCom literal offsets.

MEMORY MODEL. vm_GetMemoryValueType (my label), local 0x0690 = file 0x79E4. Range ladder at file 0x79F6, 28 bytes `83 7e 06 01 72 0d 81 7e 06 00 04 77 06 c6 46 ff 00 eb 26 81 7e 06 01 04 72 0d 81 7e`: default type 4; 1..0x400 -> type 0 (area struct); 0x401..0x800 -> type 1 (player); 0x8000..0xB6B0 -> type 2 (ECL buffer). Type-0 tail (getter, file 0x7F60, 13 bytes `8b 46 08 c4 3e 10 7e 03 f8 81 c7 ff ff`) = area_ptr + location - 1; the setter's generic tail at file 0x7D56 is identical. The "ax = location-1" reading is PROVEN, not assumed: the setter prologue at file 0x7C4F is `mov ax,[bp+0xA]; dec ax`. New-game init at file 0x1FDB7 memsets 0x400 bytes of the area struct (exactly the type-0 window) and sets area[0x21]=1; a second copy of the same init is at file 0x201AA/0x201BC.

CoAB's 0x4BE6 does not fall in any mapped bucket: it lands in the ladder's default type 4, and the setter's type dispatch (files 0x7D77 / 0x7D87) handles only types 0/1/2 before returning, so a script write to 0x4BE6 would be silently discarded. Consistently, the corpus contains zero such operands.

inDUNGEON. vm_SetMemoryValue special case, file 0x7CE9, 54 bytes `3d 21 00 75 33 c4 3e 10 7e 26 8a 45 21 30 e4 3b 46 08 74 22 c6 06 c0 a0 00 a0 24 7e a2 25 7e 83 7e 08 00 75 0c c6 06 24 7e 03 31 c0 a3 c8 a0 eb 05 c6 06 24 7e 04` = cmp ax,0x21 (ax = location-1, so ECL location 0x0022) / compare against area[0x21] / save old [0x7E24] to [0x7E25] / game_state := 3 (wilderness) when the written value is 0 else 4 (dungeon). Matching getter case, file 0x7F1C, 36 bytes: ECL location 0x0011 (facing) returns the raw 8-way host direction when area[0x21]==0 and the halved 4-way ordinal otherwise. [0x7E25], [0xA0C0], [0xA0C8] and the loader's third argument (0x27 for WildCom vs 0x19 for DungCom) are OBSERVED CONSTANTS, transcribed and explicitly not decoded.

WILDCOM LOADER. Pascal length-prefixed literals at file 0xD493, 16 bytes `07 44 75 6e 67 43 6f 6d 07 57 69 6c 64 43 6f 6d` = ".DungCom.WildCom" (locals cs:0x0EDC and cs:0x0EE4; mixed case is why a "WILDCOM" search finds nothing). SetupGroundTiles predicate, file 0xD4BF, 32 bytes `c4 3e 10 7e 26 80 7d 21 00 74 5b c4 3e 10 7e 26 80 7d 3f 00 75 50 c4 3e 10 7e 26 80 7d 51 00 75`. Jump arithmetic verified with capstone: `je 0xF6E` and `jne 0xF6E` both target loc 0x0F6E = file 0xD525, which is the WildCom arm (`8d 7e f6 16 57 bf e4 0e 0e 57 9a c2 0a 77 0a b0 00 50 b0 00 50 b0 27 50 9a 25 00 59 01` — copy cs:0x0EE4, load with (0,0,0x27)). The fall-through at loc 0x0F29 (file 0xD4E0) is the DungCom arm (`bf dc 0e` = cs:0x0EDC, args ([0xA0C8],0,0x19)); `area[0x51]!=0` diverts to loc 0x0F49, a second DungCom call with area[0x51] as arg1 (untouched by this leg, unexplained). So: **if (area[0x21] == 0 || area[0x3F] != 0) load WildCom, else DungCom.**

The same two-condition predicate picks the floor builder at file 0xD589, 36 bytes `c4 3e 10 7e 26 80 7d 21 00 74 11 c4 3e 10 7e 26 80 7d 3f 00 75 06 0e e8 ab f6 eb 04 0e e8 b1 fe 89 ec 5d cb`, which disassembles as: `je L1` / `jne L1` / fall-through loc 0x0FE8 `push cs; call 0x0697` = the DUNGEON floor builder / `jmp done` / L1 = loc 0x0FEE `push cs; call 0x0EA3` = the WILDERNESS floor builder / done. (Note the arm order: `e8 ab f6` is the dungeon side, `e8 b1 fe` the wilderness side.)

WHY area[0x3F] AND NOT inDungeon — the disjunction counter-argument, settled from bytes. area[0x3F] has ZERO native writes anywhere in GAME.OVR (all `26 C6/88/89/FE` forms with byte-displacement modrm) against 15 native reads: it is written only through the generic ECL setter tail. The setter's special-case ladder (files 0x7C53..0x7D2B) covers ECL locations 0x1A / 0x11 / 0x22 / 0x34 / 0x35 / 0x3A / 0x42 but NOT 0x0040, so a script write to [0x0040] falls through to `area_ptr + loc - 1` = area[0x3F]. area[0x21], by contrast, has exactly four native writes: `=1` twice in the 0x400-byte area-struct init (files 0x1FDD3 and 0x201BC) and a toggle pair at files 0x0F8D2 (`=1`) / 0x0F8DD (`=0`) that sits inside a developer GEO EDITOR — its own Pascal literals at file 0x0F5D0 read "\x08Overland\x08Dungeon " and "Map 1 2 3 Dir Walls Lo Sa Out Ind ExU". In normal play area[0x21] is therefore 1, the `area[0x21]==0` disjunct never fires, and the predicate reduces to `area[0x3F] != 0`. The editor's own Overland/Dungeon labels independently corroborate area[0x21] as the wilderness/dungeon discriminator. (Not enumerated: the other 31 native readers of area[0x21] and 15 of area[0x3F]; no claim that area[0x3F] has no further effects.)

FLAG CENSUS. Scanning every word-operand encoding this VM accepts (codes 0x01/0x02/0x03/0x7F — see packages/engine/src/ecl/vm.ts `rvalue`), not just 0x01: 0x4BE6 = 0 raw hits; 0x0022 = 2 raw hits (`03 22 00` block 32 @0x8A8D, `7F 22` block 51 @0x8A6A), both proven NOT instruction-aligned; 0x0040 = 22 raw hits, all of them `09 00 vv 01 40 00` (SAVE #vv -> [0x0040]). A reachable-instruction walk under this profile's dialect finds 0 references to 0x0022, 0 to 0x4BE6, 0 to 0xC04F and 174 to 0x002D. Of the 22 SAVE sites, 20 write 0 — all 20 verified reachable from their own block's initial_entry — and 2 write 1: block 4 @0x83A7 (`09 00 01 01 40 00 09 00 02 01 42 00 21 00 33 00 33` = SAVE #1,[0x0040]; SAVE #2,[0x0042]; LOAD_FILES #51,#51) and block 51 @0x808E (`09 00 01 01 40 00 09 00 33 01 16 00 21 01 ee 02 01 ee 02` = SAVE #1,[0x0040]; SAVE #51,[0x0016]; LOAD_FILES [0x02EE],[0x02EE]). Block 4 is not a playable area: GEO1.DAX contains no block 4. Nine blocks — 17, 22, 27, 32, 34, 35, 36, 37, 38 — contain no [0x0040] write at all and so neither raise nor clear it.

BLOCK 51. 7,882 bytes; header magic 0x1388; vm_run_1 0x80F9, search_location 0x8158, pre_camp_check 0x80C4, camp_interrupted 0x80EB, initial_entry 0x8014.

HANDOFF — all 20 sites, not a spot check. Every `NEWECL #51` (`20 00 33`) in the corpus: blocks 16 @0x8A52, 18 @0x82E2, 19 @0x8167, 20 @0x8262, 21 @0x80FD and @0x8A32, 23 @0x828F, 24 @0x8590, 25 @0x8139, 28 @0x8877, 29 @0x81A8, 30 @0x837B, 31 @0x848A, 33 @0x83D4, 38 @0xA3BD, 39 @0x84FF and @0x8C3F, 40 @0x81C8, 49 @0x83AB, 50 @0x8344 — each immediately preceded by the same protocol writing [0x02EC] (X), [0x02ED] (Y), [0x02EB] (facing), [0x02EE] (GEO id). The GEO ids handed over are exactly {51,52,53,54,55,56,57}: seventeen sites pass an immediate, and the three GETTABLE sites stay in the same set (block 28 @0xB415 = [51,53,53], block 39 @0x9DF3 = [56,56,56,55], block 50 @0x8A7C = [51,56,54]). "One script, seven maps" is therefore measured, not inferred. One unresolved edge: block 28 indexes a 3-byte table with [0x0011] & 3, so facing 3 would read a 4th byte of 4 — recorded, not explained. Worked example, ECL1#16 (vm_run_1 0x86AC): 0x8A3A `09 00 0e 01 ec 02` (#14 -> X); 0x8A40 `09 00 04 01 ed 02` (#4 -> Y); 0x8A46 `09 00 03 01 eb 02` (#3 -> facing west); 0x8A4C `09 00 39 01 ee 02` (#57 -> GEO id); 0x8A52 `20 00 33` (NEWECL #51). ECL1#51 reads it back at 0x80A1/0x80A8/0x80AF into [0x0035]/[0x0034]/[0x0011].

X/Y IDENTIFICATION — proven from the retail engine. The ECL accessors special-case ECL location 0x0034 -> host byte [0xA0C2] and 0x0035 -> [0xA0C3] (getter file 0x7F00 `cmp ax,0x33` / 0x7F0E `cmp ax,0x34`; setter file 0x7C72 / 0x7C85), and the retail single-step routine at file 0x87FF dispatches on facing [0xA0C4]: 0 -> `dec [0xA0C3]`, 2 -> `inc [0xA0C2]`, 4 -> `inc [0xA0C3]`, 6 -> `dec [0xA0C2]`, each wrapping 0..0x0F on a 16x16 grid. Hence [0x0034] = X, [0x0035] = Y. Corroborating (not load-bearing): GOSUB 0x9A01 walks a 22-row named-site table (`ADD #1,[0xBF]; COMPARE [0xBF],#0x16; IF_NE GOTO 0x9A07` fixes the count at exactly 22) at vaddrs 0x9B3A (geo ids), 0x9B50 (a), 0x9B66 (b), 22 bytes each, comparing [0x02EE] to the id and COMPARE_AND([0x00C1],[0x0034],[0x00C2],[0x0035]); ids = 57 57 56 56 56 55 55 54 54 53 53 52 52 51 51 51 51 52 56 54 52 51. Against the retail GEO descriptor plane raw[514 + y*16 + x], reading (a,b) as (x,y) puts 17/22 rows on a marked descriptor, transposed 1/22; the last five rows land on unmarked terrain under both readings and are NOT claimed to be cities.

ENCOUNTER CHAIN (search_location). 0x82E5 `08 00 63 01 c7 00` RANDOM #99 -> [0x00C7]; 0x82EB `2f 00 0f 01 2d 00 01 bf 00` AND #15,[0x002D] -> [0x00BF]; 0x82F4 `2a 01 f3 9c 01 bf 00 01 c6 00` GETTABLE [0x9CF3],[0x00BF] -> [0x00C6]; 0x82FE `03 01 c7 00 01 c6 00 1b` COMPARE/IF_GE; 0x830A `02 01 01 9a 16` GOSUB 0x9A01/IF_EQ; 0x8313 `02 01 49 97 17` GOSUB 0x9749/IF_NE; 0x831C `24` COMBAT. Retail tables: [0x9CF3] encounter% = 8 0 15 40 15 40 0 65 2 5 2 8 4 0 5 5; [0x9D03] clock cost = 11 11 14 16 12 16 16 16 8 9 5 11 8 8 8 6. vm_run_1 recomputes the terrain at 0x80F9 and charges the clock at 0x813D (`34 01 c0 00 00 03` = ECL_CLOCK [0x00C0],#3). The descriptor address 0x002D is established by these byte assertions plus the corpus counts above, NOT by the VM runs below.

ROUTE + RUNS. GEO1#57 (1026 bytes, 16x16): (14,4)->(14,5)->(13,5)->(12,5)->(12,6)->(12,7)->(12,8)->(12,9)->(12,10); every crossed edge independently re-verified against wall planes raw[2:258]/raw[258:514] and door flags raw[770:1026] — wall slot 0 with door flag 1 in both directions, no flag 2 (bash/pick), no flag 3 (knock). Descriptors crossed: 09 20 25 00 45 05 04 07 07 -> chances 5 8 40 8 40 40 15 65 65. This is *a* legal path chosen to reach a terrain-7 cell, not a canonical player journey.

Real EclVm: initial_entry 0x8014 seeded only with the four handoff words ([0x02EE]=57, [0x02EC]=14, [0x02ED]=4, [0x02EB]=3) exits with [0x0040]=1, [0x0016]=51, [0x0034]=14, [0x0035]=4, [0x0011]=3, [0x0022] untouched, and exactly one effect {type:"loadFiles", geoBlockId:57}. NOTE: this run is dialect-insensitive — the shared ECL_GEN1_SHORT and the long ECL_GEN1 also give [0x0040]=1, [0x0016]=51 and loadFiles 57, halting only later before the pose read-back; only the 0x80A1-0x80AF read-back distinguishes the dialects.

primeSearchLocation(block 51, desc 0x07 at (12,10), rollRandomInclusive: () => 0) -> status awaiting-input with print "SNOWING", partyStrength, print "ENEMIES ATTACK!", encounterSetup, menu {horizontal, ["ATTACK","FLEE"]}; resume(0) -> status "combat" with monsters [{108,1},{53,3},{30,5}], resolving in retail MON1CHA.DAX (102 records) via decodeMonsterArchive(bytes,'treasures-of-the-savage-frontier') to BANSHEE (hp 15), SPECTRE (hp 30) and WIGHT (hp 12). The roster is a forced-all-zero-roll sample and is terrain-dependent (each descriptor 0..15 yields a different group set); it is not "the" wilderness encounter for that cell.

CONTROLS. (1) Roll control: same cell/block/dialect with only the 99-roll forced to 98 -> status "exited", no combat effect, no menu effect, [0x00C6]=65, [0x00C7]=98. (2) Chance-table control (the discriminating one): under the same forced roll of 0, descriptors with terrain 1, 6 or 13 (table chance 0) exit silently, while terrains 0,2,3,4,5,7,8..12,14,15 all fire — so the table, not just the roll, gates the encounter. (3) Named-site control: at the site-table row-0 pose (GEO 57, [0x0034]=15, [0x0035]=4) with roll 0, the GOSUB 0x9A01 guard diverts to a scripted arm producing no encounterSetup effect. Caveat: under the forced roll of 0 the encounter fires on every cell of this route whose chance is non-zero, so the terrain-7 target cell is convenience, not evidence. Second caveat: the positive run does NOT discriminate cellDescAddr — with cellDescAddr removed from the dialect the same chain still fires, because [0x002D] then defaults to 0 (terrain 0, chance 8 > roll 0).

NOT ESTABLISHED. No native or DOSBox-X trace was run (forbidden by the task): every engine-side claim is static disassembly of retail GAME.OVR bytes; the byte assertions are exact, the control-flow readings are capstone-verified interpretations, and the function NAMES ("vm_GetMemoryValueType", "vm_SetMemoryValue", "SetupGroundTiles") are labels by structural analogy to the CoAB decompile oracle, not names in the binary. The runtime claims use this repo's EclVm on retail block bytes, not the shipped DOS interpreter. area[0x51]'s DungCom variant, the loader's 0x27/0x19 third argument, [0x7E25], [0xA0C0] and [0xA0C8] are transcribed, not decoded. ECL1#51 contains a statically reachable bad opcode 0x41 at vaddr 0x8517 on a scripted-site arm this route never touches, so coverage of block 51 is incomplete. ECL1#4's early halt is on opcode 0x42 at vaddr 0x804E — the opcode this profile's dialect already overrides — so block 4 does not actually halt under this dialect and its [0x0040]=1 site is reachable in a fall-through-inclusive walk; it is excluded as a playable-area write because GEO1.DAX has no block 4, and its identification as the attract/demo script rests on prior repo work (the ECL_GEN1_SHORT_TREASURES doc comment in packages/engine/src/ecl/disassemble.ts, which cites a native-RAM observation), not on anything established here. No browser wiring: no ?explore= route id, no e2e, no deployment, no live-site check — the leg is proven at the data/VM level only.

ecl.detail: Treasures' title-specific short ECL dialect is byte-decoded for ECL1#34: both full monster requests, tactical continuations, rescued-miners narration, terminal writes [0x022D]=1 and [0x0232]=1, and the consumed revisit are engine-verified. UPDATED 2026-09-04 (round 33 Phase B): two Treasures-only operand frames that had been measured and withheld are now SHIPPED, and both changed what the engine plays. 0x27 TREASURE is wordSet 4 / countAt 3, transcribed from Treasures' own GAME.OVR handler at file 0x1afd -- retail block ECL1#47 carries an explicit 1..8 count ladder, which treasuresEndingRoute.test.ts's test C had been proving against a test-local dialect all along. 0x37 is wordSet 2, the two-operand party-name lookup, from Treasures' own handler at file 0x2577, dispatched by a straight-line cmp al,0x37 / call 0x2577 pair at 0x33c1 that shares no target with either neighbour -- which falsifies round 32's 'fallthrough-merge misattribution' doubt directly from the dispatcher bytes. Round 32 had bisected 0x37 and called it falsified, but that bisection toggled 0x37 while holding 0x27 at its OWN wrong base frame, so it was never a single-variable test. With both shipped, Treasures' campaign-ending script (block 38) plays end to end under the SHIPPED dialect -- full retail narration through 'IT HAS, INDEED, BEEN GLORIOUS!', the terminal memory writes and the NEWECL #51 chain -- where it previously died on a bad opcode at 0xA1B6.
gaps: ECL DECODE CENSUS, SHALLOW AND DEEP (round 33 R1, 2026-09-04): disassembleEclBlock stops at each block's FIRST EXIT, so every clean-EXIT count this project has ever published is a LOWER BOUND -- it never walks the combat, quest or descriptor subroutines placed later in a block's own bytes. walkEclReachable (packages/engine/src/ecl/reachability.ts) follows all five ECL header entry points and every GOTO/GOSUB/ON_GOTO/ON_GOSUB. Measured on this title's 30 retail blocks: 0 shallow desync block(s), 0 deep desync site(s). Deep and shallow agree here (0 each), which is a result and not a default -- 6 of the 11 Gen1 titles disagree. Pinned in packages/engine/test/eclReachability.test.ts; the deep counts are SITES and the shallow counts are BLOCKS, so the two are not directly subtractable.

TWO PINS THAT LOOKED LIKE ORACLES AND WERE NOT, recorded because the shape will recur. treasuresQuestFlag.test.ts pinned status === 'halted' and its own comment named the cause as 'the disclosed Sec.8.4.2 TREASURE/bad-opcode gap at 0xA1B6' -- halted carries haltReason 'bad opcode at <pc>', so the assertion was pinning the defect BY NAME. The Pools route goldens were generated by the very VM whose opcode table was under test, which poolsMiddleRoute.test.ts's header discloses in as many words. A golden produced by the code under test cannot adjudicate that code. Four route assertions were regenerated rather than obeyed; the shipped frames were mutation-tested (removing 0x27 turns 12 tests red while a mirror test reconstructing the legacy flat frame stays green).

A MNEMONIC-PLUMBING TRAP that reproduces round 32's crash signature exactly, recorded so it is not read as a third falsification: vm.ts's case 0x37 selects the two-operand lookup by MNEMONIC, not by word set. Shipping 0x37 with a name vm.ts did not know sent the instruction down the inherited three-operand loadPieces path, which read an operand the frame never decoded and threw 'Cannot read properties of undefined (reading code)' in EclVm.rvalue -- round 32's literal error text, from a plumbing bug rather than a wrong frame. vm.ts now matches a set (FIND_CHARACTER_MNEMONICS) so Pools and Treasures each keep their own label; eclGen1DispatchRound32.test.ts pins that.

graphics.detail: The selected-folder route renders Treasures' source-specific VGA wall palette and split 8X8D wall/frame banks; release acceptance explicitly confirms that no unverified alternate graphics mode is exposed.
gaps: No Amiga wall-art toggle, and this is now a MEASURED rejection rather than an untried one (2026-08-09): the Amiga WallDef.glb shipped with Treasures is byte-identical to Gateway's across all 12 shared ids — the Savage Frontier duology's shared/stale file — while Treasures' own DOS walldefs are a different 2340-byte format indexing VGA-extended tile ids. The thirds hypothesis (2340 = 3 x 780) was tested and refuted. Mounting that Amiga art over Treasures geometry would render plausible-looking wrong walls, so the toggle is deliberately not offered.
Native 320x200 screen composition, broad picture and animation coverage, exact palette timing, and pixel-level compositor parity remain incomplete.

map_container.detail: A retained selected-folder AssetSource supplies ECL1, GEO1, WALLDEF1, 8X8D0/1, MON1CHA/SPC/ITM, and ITEM0 archives for legal area-34 movement and combat. CORRECTED 2026-08-08: the earlier claim that Treasures' ECL corpus contains no LOAD_PIECES instruction was our decoder's, not the game's. Treasures carries its own combined loader 0x42 LOAD_AREA_PIECES, and 19 of ECL1's 30 blocks supply a real WALLDEF1 piece triple through it (block 16 = 9/10/11). The source-backed wall fallback [1,255,255] is still needed for the 9 blocks that load through plain 0x21 LOAD_FILES.
