ROSTER OUTCOME OF ?import=treasures, ADDED 2026-09-05 (round 36 R6). THIS IS AN ADDITION, NOT A CORRECTION, and establishing which it is was this task's own null: measured on the pre-edit file, this profile contained 0 occurrences each of OUGO, CHERROD, SMOKE, 'pregen' and 'party cap' and made no roster claim at all. The ledger was SILENT here, not wrong -- an addition dressed as a correction would have hidden that the measurement and the pin existed while the ledger entry did not. MEASURED OUTCOME, denominator 8 (every retail SAVE/CHRDATA{1..8}.SAV): 6 join in file order -- MAXWELL, TRISTLE, MELLIA, CHERROD, SPARKLE, FRAZZLE -- with 0 rule-rejections and exactly 2 rejections by the shared six-hero party cap, OUGO and SMOKE in that order. WHAT MOVED (round 35 R4): under Treasures' OWN compiled race table at unpacked GAME.EXE 0xD454 (stride 9, 7 entries, Elf/Half-Elf/Dwarf/Gnome/Halfling/Human/Monster; fencepost null 7 of 7 plausible short PStrings at the real base against 0 at all 16 bases shifted by +/-1..8), CHERROD's race byte 0x01 at record offset 0xad reads Half-Elf, so her fighter 3 / magic-user 3 / thief 4 multi-class (class byte 0x0f, classLevel[8]@0x151 = [0,0,3,0,0,3,4,0]) is legal and she takes the sixth slot. The retired borrowed CoAB enum read that same byte as a mountainDwarf and rejected her outright, which is the only reason OUGO used to fall through into the party. The 0-based reading of the race byte is argued by consequence, indexing instruction not located -- imul r16, imm8 has zero hits in these 8086-targeted builds -- and is NOT to be upgraded to 'proven'. Every byte quoted in this bullet and the next was re-read first-hand from the retail GOG install on 2026-09-05 rather than carried over from the round-35 memo. DERIVATION OF THE RULE-REJECTION COUNT, recorded 2026-09-05 because the figure was weaker than it looked when first written: round 36 R6 INHERITED the 0 from browser e2e case import-treasures and disclosed that it could not re-derive it in Python, and the pin asserts only that this string is present. It has since been reproduced independently twice against the retail bytes -- once by this round's adversarial verifier and once while correcting the falsified comment at apps/web/src/ui/main.ts -- both replaying the legality path under each title's OWN race table, both returning 0 rule-rejections, with BINKY and CHERROD joining and OUGO and SMOKE cut by the cap. So the number is corroborated -- but note WHAT is pinned: the e2e case and the Python replays share the same race-table premise, so they are not independent OF that premise. If it is ever overturned, this figure moves with it.

DISCLOSED DATA CONFLICT, CARRIED NOT RESOLVED (added 2026-09-05, round 36 R6) -- OUGO disagrees WITH HERSELF, and the party-cap rejection above must not be read as burying that. In SAVE/CHRDATA7.SAV her class byte at record offset 0xae is 0x02 = fighter, while her own classLevel[8] window at 0x151 reads [8,0,0,0,0,0,0,0]: the single nonzero slot is index 0, which in this record's own slot order (cleric/druid/fighter/paladin/ranger/magic_user/thief/monk) is CLERIC, level 8. Her bytes are unchanged by round 35 R4 -- only her position relative to the cap changed. She is the one record of Treasures' eight that fails the class/classLevel agreement oracle (7 of 8 agree; Pools' ABAGAIL is the equivalent 5-of-6 miss, see that profile). Nothing translates the conflict away: the importer always builds the sheet from the level array, never from the class byte, and shows the class byte raw behind a bold 'class byte and level array disagree -- shown raw, not translated' badge. Because CHERROD now fills the sixth slot, OUGO is cut by the cap rather than joining, which would have removed her row -- and that badge -- from the shown summary entirely; the disclosure is instead carried by PoolsTreasuresImportResult.rejectedPartyFullDisagreements and re-rendered as the identical badge in the rejected list. Pinned two-sidedly by e2e case import-treasures (the rejected list must be exactly OUGO,SMOKE AND the rendered .import-rejected row for OUGO must still match /disagree/) and by tools/test_round36_r6_roster_ledger.py, which re-derives these byte facts from the retail records and fails if this bullet and the ledger stop agreeing with them.

Party, quest, and sidecar save structures are unmapped; the per-character CHRDATA record IS decoded and imported (see docs/engine/research/pools-treasures-race-table.md), and its race byte is now translated from this title's own compiled table (GAME.EXE 0xD454) rather than a borrowed enum (round 35 R4).
import.scope: No selected-folder Treasures retail party or campaign-save importer is shipped, and no quest, sidecar or campaign-save import of any kind. A BUNDLED URL ROUTE DOES SHIP, so this status must not be read as 'nothing imports': ?import=treasures (apps/web/src/ui/importPoolsTreasuresParty.ts, armed from apps/web/src/ui/main.ts) reads the eight retail SAVE/CHRDATA{1..8}.SAV pregens through the shared 510-byte POOLS_TREASURES_SAVED_CHARACTER_LAYOUT and builds a playable six-hero party. The measured roster outcome and the one disclosed data conflict in it are the two bullets below.

ruleset.detail: The selected-folder route uses Greybox's shared AD&D party, exploration, dialogue, tactical-combat, treasure, and persistence systems together with Treasures' title-scoped 510-byte monster records and compact carried-item expansion.
gaps: Full retail spell, item, class, AI, encounter-placement, economy, visible full-roster, and AD&D 2e combat-rule parity is not claimed.

towns.detail: The ?explore=treasures-town route mounts Llorkh (ECL1/GEO1 block 16, the area retail opens in) and walks its own 56-cell service route: every cell asserted at its step, the armoury, training hall, temple and inn prompts answered through the live host, and each accepted service's retail host word read back from area memory ([0x0004]=1, [0x0028]=16, [0x0030]=127, [0x00c8]=1) with the declined temple's [0x0014]=0 as the negative control. Block 16 was unmountable until Treasures' own combined area loader 0x42 LOAD_AREA_PIECES was decoded; 19 of ECL1's 30 blocks load through it.
gaps: One town of the 21 byte-identified settlement blocks is routed; the other 20 are identified but unwalked.
Town ENTRY and EXIT are not wired: the route mounts block 16 directly at its byte-derived overland arrival pose rather than crossing into it from the wilderness.
Shop stock is never surfaced: PROTECTION (0x3C) is a VM no-op and its operand-to-inventory mapping is UNLOCATED, so the armoury proves the prompt and the host flags, not a purchase.
The NPC reaction menu (HAUGHTY/SLY/NICE/MEEK/ABUSIVE) reached from several service answers is not modelled; the route closes it.
The declined tavern encounter's monsters carry into the next combat under this engine's global-roster model; that behaviour is asserted but not verified against a retail DOS trace.

wilderness.detail: The current Treasures routes are fixed GEO dungeon routes and do not mount a title-specific overland travel controller.
gaps: Retail wilderness movement, transitions, encounter cadence, RNG continuity, and persistence are not implemented.

It is a COMPLETION-GATED POST-VICTORY PHLAN: a full 589-instruction playable town block with its own vm_run_1 0x8211 / search_location 0x8A0B / pre_camp_check 0x815B / camp_interrupted 0x81C8, LOAD_FILES #17,#1 at 0x8061 and spawn SAVE #5->[0x0035] / SAVE #0->[0x0034] / SAVE #1->[0x0011] at 0x8066/0x806C/0x8072, whose FIRST instruction is 0x8014 `0301ee020000` COMPARE [0x02EE],#0 / `16` IF_EQ / `200010` NEWECL #16 -- i.e. it refuses to run and re-routes to the ordinary Phlan block unless the completion latch is set. (c) "NEWECL #24 is a continuation, so block 75 is not a terminus": correct that it is a continuation -- and that is the finding, not a refutation: the campaign narrative concludes at block 75 and the game continues in a latch-gated post-victory world. wilderness.citation:
POOLS OF DARKNESS — WILDERNESS LEG. Verdict: PROVEN at data/VM level (static, byte-level; no native trace). Independently re-measured 2026-08-06 by a second agent from the retail bytes; every load-bearing number, vaddr, offset, coordinate, count and roster below was re-derived, not carried over.

Retail (read-only): C:\Program Files (x86)\GOG Galaxy\Games\Pools of Darkness\, resolved via goldbox_corpus.choose_install/file_index. GAME.OVR 264,086 B sha256 bac46d17…3d402; GAME.EXE 64,203 B sha256 35ad635e…48d69; ECL1.DAX 329,456 B sha256 46aab737…064af (56 blocks, ids 1..86); GEO1.DAX 28,349 B (32 blocks, all 1026 B); WILDCOM.DAX 48,523 B (3 blocks, ids 0/1/2); DUNGCOM.DAX 65,353 B (6 blocks, ids 1..6); MON1CHA.DAX 13,428 B. Gen1 addressing vbase 0x7FFE, file offset = vaddr − 0x8000 + 2, header 22 B (magic 0x1388 + five (0x0101, addr) pairs). Dialect ECL_GEN1_SHORT_POOLS = {12:4, 29:0, 31:1, 33:2, 34:0, 35:0, 44:1, 55:2} via gen1_ecl_encounter_scan.word_sets_for_profile('pools-of-darkness') — Pools' OWN split, carrying opcodes 31 (0x1F) and 55 (0x37) that Treasures' variant lacks and 33 (0x21)=2 against DoK's 3. SAVE order = (source, destination), destination last. Every GAME.OVR address is a file offset in the Borland FBOV/VROOMM pool.

§0 THE 0x4BE6 ZERO IS A MODEL MISMATCH, NOT AN ABSENCE. Range ladder, GAME.OVR file 0x06BA4 (my own capstone, 16-bit): `c6 46 ff 04` default type 4; 1..0x400 → type 0 (area struct); 0x401..0x800 → type 1 (player); at 0x06BCF `81 7e 06 00 80 / 72 0b / 81 7e 06 ff 9d / 77 04 / c6 46 ff 02` = 0x8000..0x9DFF → type 2 (script buffer). Pools' upper bound 0x9DFF is MEASURED IN POOLS' OWN BINARY, not transplanted: Treasures' bound is 0xB6B0 and its equivalent code lives at 0x79F6/0xD493/0xD525, addresses that hold unrelated bytes in Pools. Full setter disassembled, not just the cited window: entry 0x06D51 → `call 0x06B9E` (the ladder) → `cmp al,0; je` type-0 path else `jmp 0x06EDB`; type-0 special cases are loc−1 ∈ {0x19,0x33,0x34,0x10,0x21,0x39}, default tail 0x06EBA (`les di,[0x87F8]; add di,ax; add di,-1` ⇒ area[loc−1]); 0x06EDB `cmp al,1` → 0x06C3F, 0x06EEB `cmp al,2` → `les di,[0x87FC]; add di,ax; add di,0x8000`, then 0x06F0E `89 ec 5d` + 0x06F11 `ca 06 00` retf 6. TYPES 3/4 WRITE NOTHING; 0x4BE6 is type 4 ⇒ a script write to it is silently discarded. Raw all-encoding corpus scan (operand codes 0x01/0x02/0x03 three-byte plus the 0x7F short form) over all 56 blocks: 0x4BE6 = 0, 0x0040 = 0, 0xC04F = 0, 0x0022 = 53.

§1 POOLS' ECL MEMORY MODEL. ECL location L = area[L−1]; area_ptr at DS:0x87F8. Read side independently checked in vm_GetMemoryValue (file 0x06F14, also reached via `call 0x06B9E`): loc−1 ∈ {0x0F,0x22,0x33,0x34,0x10,0x31,0x2C} are special-cased, everything else falls to `area_ptr + loc − 1` at 0x07018. Locations 0x0025/0x0026 are NOT special-cased on either side, so they are plain area[0x24]/area[0x25] for both read and write.

§2 POOLS' inDungeon IS ECL LOCATION 0x0022. Setter arm, file 0x06E16: `3d 21 00` cmp ax,0x21 (ax = loc−1 ⇒ ECL 0x0022); `26 8a 45 21` read area[0x21]; `3b 46 08` compare with the new value; `a0 0c 88` / `a2 0d 88` save game_state [0x880C] → [0x880D]; `83 7e 08 00 / 75 0c`; `c6 06 0c 88 03` [0x880C] = 3 WILDERNESS on value 0; `c6 06 0c 88 04` = 4 DUNGEON otherwise. Native access census, RECALL-CHECKED (all 8 ModRM base-register forms × opcodes 0x88/0x8A/0xC6/0x80/0x38/0x3A/0x00/0x08/0x20/0x30/0xFE with an ES override and disp8 = 0x21, across GAME.OVR **and** GAME.EXE/STARTUP.EXE/CONTROL.EXE/VACE.EXE): exactly 2 writes (0x1A4D1, 0x1A836 — both `c4 3e f8 87 26 c6 45 21 01` at 0x1A4CD/0x1A832, part of a field-initialiser run that also sets area[0x26]=3, area[0x15]=0, area[0x38]=0x0A, i.e. init to 1 = DUNGEON) against 26 reads (25 `26 80 7d 21 imm` + the setter's own `26 8a 45 21`). area[0x21] is ECL-owned; the engine defaults to dungeon and only a script lowers it. A THIRD independent engine consumer of the same flag: vm_GetMemoryValue's loc−1 == 0x10 arm at file 0x06FD4 does `cmp byte es:[di+0x21],0` and returns the raw 8-way facing [0xA9F5] when it is 0, the halved 4-way ordinal otherwise — the retail engine itself ties area[0x21] == 0 to 8-way overland movement. Corpus census of `09 00 vv 01 22 00` (SAVE #imm → [0x0022]) across all 56 blocks: 25 sites, 14 writing 1 / 11 writing 0, in blocks 1,3,17,18,25,51,80 (wilderness-0 vaddrs include 17@0x801A, 25@0x801A, 51@0x801A, 80@0x801A, 1@0x87F4, 3@0x8028).

§3 WHAT LOADS WILDCOM: ONE CONDITION. Pascal literals 0x0C563 `07 44 75 6e 67 43 6f 6d` ".DungCom" (cs:0x0E7D) and 0x0C58B `07 57 69 6c 64 43 6f 6d` ".WildCom" (cs:0x0EA5) — mixed case (a case-sensitive "WILDCOM" search finds nothing), 0x28 apart with a routine prologue after WildCom, unlike Treasures where the two literals are adjacent at 0xD493. `mov di,0x0EA5` occurs EXACTLY ONCE in the pool (0x0C5EF) and `mov di,0x0E7D` exactly once (0x0C5A9), so SetupGroundTiles (cs:0x0EAD, file 0x0C593) is the sole loader of either. Predicate, file 0x0C599: `c4 3e f8 87 26 80 7d 21 00 74 20` — les di,[0x87F8]; cmp byte es:[di+0x21],0; je 0xC5C4. THAT IS THE WHOLE PREDICATE — one condition, verified by disassembling 0x0C593..0x0C64B end to end. je target = WILDERNESS arm, fall-through = DUNGEON. Dungeon arm 0x0C5A9 `bf 7d 0e 0e 57 9a 6f 0a 25 08 a0 f8 a9 50 b0 00 50 b0 19 50` → lcall 013E:0025 with 3rd arg 0x19; wilderness arm 0x0C5EF `bf a5 0e 0e 57 9a 6f 0a 25 08 8a 46 ff 50 b0 00 50 b0 27 50` → 3rd arg 0x27 (the 0x27/0x19 pair matches Treasures'; Pools differs in computing a non-zero FIRST argument). First argument computed at 0x0C5C4 from `26 8a 45 39` area[0x39] = ECL loc 0x003A (setter arm 0x06E4E `3d 39 00`, values ≥ 5 rejected). Floor-builder predicate 0x0C633 `c4 3e f8 87 26 80 7d 21 00 74 06 …` — the SAME one condition: je → wilderness builder cs:0x0E34, fall-through → dungeon builder cs:0x065F. REFUTATION OF THE TREASURES HYPOTHESIS: the single-condition predicate is the refutation. As corroboration, Treasures' specific field offsets are absent from Pools' engine — `26 80 7d 3f` and `26 80 7d 51` each occur 0 times in the 264,086-byte pool against 25 for `26 80 7d 21` (this rules out those offsets, not the abstract possibility of some other second flag), and Treasures' ECL selector [0x0040] has 0 corpus occurrences.

§4 TWO STEPPERS, TWO COORDINATE SPACES. Dispatcher file 0x0DBE5 (seg 0x0D577): `a0 0c 88 3c 04 75 3f` mov al,[0x880C]; cmp al,4; jne → 0x0DC15 `0e e8 02 fa` call 0x0D61B (dungeon); 0x0DC2B `3c 03 75 16` cmp al,3 → 0x0DC3A `0e e8 8c fa` call 0x0D6CA (wilderness). BOTH arms then converge on the identical `lcall 00EC:00E3` (0x0DC19 / 0x0DC3E) — the same per-step continuation in both modes. Dungeon stepper 0x0D61B: X += ds:[0x3EAC+facing], Y += ds:[0x3EB5+facing], then four WRAP tests on a 16×16 grid over [0xA9F3]/[0xA9F4] (= ECL 0x0034/0x0035 per the setter's 0x33/0x34 arms). Wilderness stepper 0x0D6CA: 0x0D6DA stashes area[0x16] := area[0x24] and area[0x17] := area[0x25]; 0x0D708 newX = area[0x24] + dx; 0x0D725 newY = area[0x25] + dy; 0x0D734 CLAMPS X to 0..0x25 and Y to 0..0x0E; 0x0D75F stores back to area[0x24]/area[0x25] = ECL 0x0025/0x0026. Clamps, not wraps — a structural difference between the two modes, and 0x25/0x0E = 38 columns × 15 rows. Deltas: the 18 bytes `00 01 01 01 00 ff ff ff 00 | ff ff 00 01 01 01 00 ff 00` occur EXACTLY ONCE in GAME.EXE (file 0x0C7C5) and NOT AT ALL in GAME.OVR; the 9-byte stride matches DS:0x3EAC → DS:0x3EB5, and facing 6 = W (−1,0). THE DS → FILE-OFFSET MAPPING IS NOT RESOLVED and does not close arithmetically: GAME.EXE declares zero relocations and a 0x200-byte header, and 0x0C7C5 − 0x200 − 0x3EAC = 0x8719 is not paragraph-aligned. The table's IDENTITY is instead corroborated inside Pools' engine: the setter's 0x10 arm writes [0xA9F5] = 0/2/4/6 for ECL facing 0..3 and the getter returns it raw in wilderness / halved in dungeon, so even indices are N/E/S/W exactly as the table's shape requires.

§5 THE OVERLAND MAPS ARE IN-BLOCK DATA, NOT GEO. ECL1#17/#25/#51/#80 all open initial_entry at 0x8014 with the byte-identical 24-byte stanza `09 00 01 01 24 00 | 09 00 00 01 22 00 | 09 00 00 01 1a 00 | 09 00 00 01 0f 00` — the 2nd instruction is an UNCONDITIONAL SAVE #0 → [0x0022], no COMPARE/IF before it — then a SAVE #n → [0x003A] sub-bank (17→0, 80→1, 51→2, 25→4). Map resolvers: ON_GOTO `25 01 c1 00 00 0f` on [0x00C1] with 15 targets at 17@0x98B3, 25@0x8CC3, 51@0x8A3F, 80@0x8A61; each regular row handler is 11 bytes `2a 01 <base_lo> <base_hi> 01 c0 00 01 bf 00 13` = GETTABLE [row_base],[0x00C0] → [0x00BF]; RETURN. Row-base stride 0x26 = 38 in all four; bases 51 0x8B23..0x8D37, 25 0x8DA7..0x8FBB, 80 0x8B45..0x8D59, 17 0x99D6..0x9BC4 (row 0's handler is a guarded `2f 00 …` variant, so its base 0x99B0 is the arithmetic continuation, not a read operand). 15 rows × 38 columns matches the compiled clamps 0x0E/0x25 exactly — two unrelated artifacts agreeing on the same two numbers. GEO1.DAX holds 32 blocks (ids 1,16..22,32..37,39,48..50,52,53,64..71,81..84): 25, 51 and 80 have NO same-id GEO block at all and cannot be GEO-backed; only 17 has one. WILDCOM.DAX holds exactly three blocks, ids 0/1/2, matching the [0x003A] values written by 17/80/51 — a 3-for-3 agreement. ANOMALY, disclosed: block 25 writes [0x003A] = 4, for which no WILDCOM block exists (the 0825:0D24 lookup's failure path sets the loader's first argument to 0); corpus-wide the field takes values 0 (×3), 1 (×4), 2 (×2), 3 (×1), 4 (×3).

§5a SITE-TABLE CROSS-CHECK (the strongest single check). ECL1#52 0x851E `2a 01 57 9c 01 24 02 01 c0 00` + `2a 01 61 9c 01 24 02 01 c1 00` (GETTABLE [0x9C57]/[0x9C61] by [0x0224]), 0x8532 `09 01 c0 00 01 25 00 09 01 c1 00 01 26 00`, 0x8546 `20 00 33` NEWECL #51. Block 51's site index = code − 30 via two retail SUBTRACTs: 0x814A `05 00 0a 01 bf 00 01 bf 00` (−10) and, on the 0x8159 COMPARE #20 / IF_LE / GOTO 0x8165 arm, 0x8165 `05 00 14 01 bf 00 01 24 02` (−20). Indices 1..8: (15,13)→0x1F=31, (29,7)→0x20=32, (4,2)→0x21=33, (32,8)→0x22=34, (12,4)→0x23=35, (34,13)→0x24=36, (27,11)→0x25=37, (21,3)→0x26=38 — EIGHT FOR EIGHT, and those are exactly the eight site codes on the map, one each. Fixes [0x0025] = column, [0x0026] = row, site index = code − 30. The transposed reading is impossible (X reaches 34; the map has only 15 rows). Indices 0 and 9 both repeat index 5's (12,4); only 1..8 are claimed.

§6 THE RETAIL BYTES THAT HAND A POSE TO ECL1#51. ECL1#53 0x8345 `09 00 14 01 25 00 09 00 03 01 26 00 09 00 01 01 0e 00` → (20,3), 0x8377 `20 00 33` NEWECL #51. map(20,3) = 0x03 terrain; map(21,3) = 0x26 = site 8, one column east. That ECL1#53 is the location occupying site 8 is an INFERENCE from that adjacency alone. NO reachability from a game start is shown for ECL1#53, nor for the 0x8345 handoff within it.

§7 THE PER-STEP WANDERING CHAIN. search_location 0x80F1 (2nd header far-pointer): 0x80F1 clears [0x0097]/[0x0033]/[0x00A2]/[0x00A3]; 0x8109 `09 00 4b 01 1b 00`; 0x8122/0x8129 copy [0x0025]/[0x0026] → [0x00C0]/[0x00C1]; 0x8130 `02 01 3f 8a` GOSUB 0x8A3F (the 15×38 lookup); 0x8134 `03 00 0a 01 bf 00 1a 01 01 4a 81` COMPARE #10,[0x00BF]; IF_LE; GOTO 0x814A (scripted site, codes ≥ 10); 0x813F `09 01 bf 00 01 22 02 01 01 c5 81` (terrain → wandering roll); 0x81C5 `04 00 01 01 23 02 01 23 02` ADD #1,[0x0223]; 0x81CE `03 00 04 01 23 02 19 00` 4-step gate; 0x81D6 `08 00 63 01 bf 00` RANDOM #99; 0x81DC `03 00 14 01 bf 00 1a 00` miss when roll ≥ 20; 0x81EA RANDOM #9 (roster row) / 0x81FD RANDOM #3 (roster group); 0x8203 ON_GOTO [0x00A1],#4 → 0x8215/0x826D/0x82AD/0x82ED; 0x8360 `08 00 09 01 c4 00 03 00 07 01 c4 00`; 0x836C `1a 01 01 97 85` IF_LE; GOTO 0x8597 (ATTACK arm). NO cell-descriptor read anywhere: a RAW ALL-ENCODING SCAN (operand codes 0x01/0x02/0x03 plus the 0x7F short form — full recall, no reachability filter) finds ZERO references to [0x002D] in each of blocks 17/25/51/80, against 106 corpus-wide. That [0x002D] is the host cell-descriptor register is established in Pools' own engine, not assumed from sibling titles: vm_GetMemoryValue special-cases loc−1 == 0x2C at file 0x07009 and returns host byte [0xA9F7], not area[0x2C]. Supplementary reachability census (worklist from all five header entries following only GOTO/GOSUB/ON_GOTO/ON_GOSUB, test L): [0x002D] 54 refs in 30 blocks — none in 17/25/51/80; LOAD_FILES (0x21) 3 sites in blocks 4/16/24 — none in 17/25/51/80; [0x0022] 8 refs in blocks 1/17/18/25/51/80; [0x4BE6] 0; [0x0040] 0. This walker does NOT follow computed/indirect jumps, so its positive counts are lower bounds and its zeros prove nothing on their own — the load-bearing negatives rest on the raw full-recall scans above, not on it.

§8 THE ROUTE AND THE ENCOUNTER. Four steps west from (20,3) → (19,3) → (18,3) → (17,3) → (16,3), re-derived in test I from the retail dx/dy bytes and the retail clamp bounds; every cell crossed is terrain 0x03 (row 3, columns 16–20). VM run (real EclVm on retail block bytes, ECL_GEN1_SHORT_POOLS): initial_entry leaves [0x0022] = 0, [0x003A] = 2, [0x0016] = 51; steps 1–3 exit silently at the 4-step counter gate (counter 1,2,3; [0x0222] = 0x03 each time); step 4 reaches status 'combat' emitting print "YOU STUMBLE UPON A GROUP OF MONSTERS.", two blanks, "THEY ATTACK!", an encounterSetup (spriteId 255, picId 129) and a combat carrying monsterId 76×2, 42×2, 43×2. THE ROSTER IS INDEPENDENTLY CONFIRMED FROM RETAIL BYTES, not only from the VM: the executed group's six GETTABLE bases are 0x8D5D/0x8D67/0x8D71/0x8D7B/0x8D85/0x8D8F and index 9 reads 76,2,42,2,43,2. All three ids resolve in retail MON1CHA.DAX via decodeMonsterArchive('pools-of-darkness') to records with non-empty names and non-zero HP. NEGATIVE CONTROLS — THREE discriminating, not four: (b) roll boundary, RANDOM #99 = 20 misses and 19 fires, positive and negative differing in exactly one rolled value at the table's own boundary; (c) site cell, same counter and roll one column east on (21,3) takes the scripted-site arm and sets up no encounter, so the gate is the map byte; and (a) the 4-step counter gate at counters 0/1/2 — which is the SAME fact as walk steps 1–3, not an additional control. The 256-value descriptor sweep is a CONSISTENCY CHECK, NOT A CONTROL: it cannot fail, because blocks 17/25/51/80 contain zero references to [0x002D] (and zero to 0xC04F), and the assertion compares only the effect-TYPE sequence, not payloads. Per-step harness modelling: the counter [0x0223] and the pose are threaded between calls; every other cell is reset to the post-initial_entry state each step (search_location clears its own gates at 0x80F1 anyway). DIALECT-INSENSITIVE: test J(e) runs the identical route under the shared ECL_GEN1_SHORT and gets the same effect-type sequence and the same three monster groups. (The two tables differ only on opcodes 0x1F/0x21/0x37/0x41; no claim is made about whether those bytes occur as decoded instructions in these blocks — that was not measured, and the map data itself contains those byte values as terrain/site codes.) THIS LEG IS NOT EVIDENCE FOR ECL_GEN1_SHORT_POOLS, which stands on its own handler-level derivation in disassemble.ts.

§9 The same flag used as a pure combat backdrop switch: ECL1#1 0x87F4 SAVE #0 → [0x0022], 0x87FA SAVE #0x4B → [0x001B], SETUP_MONSTER/LOAD_MONSTER/COMBAT, 0x8811 SAVE #1 → [0x0022] restoring dungeon mode. Block 51 does the same at 0x87AE/0x87B4 (SAVE #0 → [0x0024]; SAVE #1 → [0x0022]; CLEAR_BOX) — it re-enters dungeon mode somewhere in its own site handling, and that transition is not decoded.

NOT ESTABLISHED — (1) NO native/DOSBox-X trace (forbidden by the task): engine claims are static capstone on GAME.OVR/GAME.EXE plus byte assertions; runtime claims are our own EclVm on retail bytes. Nothing observes the shipped DOS binary running. (2) THE HOST→ECL CALL EDGE IS NOT TRACED — the biggest single gap. What is proven is that the retail wilderness stepper writes area[0x24]/area[0x25] and that block 51's search_location reads ECL [0x0025]/[0x0026], i.e. the SAME TWO BYTES, and that both dispatcher arms converge on the identical `lcall 00EC:00E3`; the `lcall 00FF:0025` immediately after the stepper's stores was NOT decoded. That the host calls search_location once per wilderness step is the standard Gen1 model every sibling golden here assumes. (3) NO browser wiring — no ?explore= route id, no live-site check, no e2e acceptance; data/VM level only, and no campaign continuity from a game start is claimed. (4) The DS:0x3EAC → GAME.EXE file mapping is unresolved and does not close arithmetically (see §4). (5) The wilderness stepper performs NO passability test — it only clamps; whether terrain 0x00 is walkable is not established, and the route stays on terrain 0x03 precisely so the question never arises. It is *a* legal-by-arithmetic path, not a claim about what a player would do or about map connectivity. (6) SCOPE: only block 51 is fully proven (route run, site table cross-checked). Blocks 17/25/80 share its entry stanza, 15×38 geometry and row stride, but no route was run and their site tables were not cross-checked; block 17 is NOT a pure wilderness block (it alone has a same-id GEO block, its row-0 handler is guarded, and it writes [0x0022] = 1 at three further vaddrs). (7) Terrain semantics of codes 0–5 are not decoded — only that < 10 takes the wandering-roll path and ≥ 10 a scripted arm. (8) The all-RANDOM-zero "monsters in the distance" arm is NOT part of the proven route: it prints real retail text then dies on an unresolved GOTO (unhandled effect, opcode 0x01); test J pins the observed behaviour, no byte-level attribution is claimed. (9) The WildCom loader's 3rd argument (0x27 wild / 0x19 dung), [0x880D], [0xA9F2], [0xA9F8], [0x001B], [0x000E] are recorded as observed constants, not decoded; area[0x39]/ECL [0x003A] is shown to be the loader's FIRST argument and written with values 0..4, but which WILDCOM sub-bank each value selects and what the 0825:0D24 lookup decides are NOT established, and no claim is made that it has no further effects.

Pools' GAME.OVR dispatcher and operand parser now structurally match the CoAB oracle on Pools' own retail bytes (dispatcher 0.9680 at 0x28cb against a runner-up null of 0.2948 and a same-length non-dispatcher null of 0.1497; parser 1.0000 at 0x65eb; 66 handlers dispatched) — see docs/engine/research/pools-ecl-dispatch-map.md. The four ECL_GEN1_SHORT_POOLS overrides (0x1F:1, 0x21:2, 0x37:2, 0x41:2) are read from Pools' own handlers at +0x264a, +0x0e9e, +0x1eca and +0x240c, which this sentence previously denied: the dialect docblock was right and this ledger entry was the wrong artifact. Remaining: 1 shallow desync, and 33 opcodes vacuous (the binary gives no count). Opcode 0x27 measures wordSet 4 against base 8 in both Pools and Treasures and WAS deliberately withheld — Pools' handler has a countAt-shaped dynamic tail a flat override cannot represent, and it improves the 56-block shallow census only 3 to 1, not to 0. SHIPPED 2026-09-04 (round 33 Phase B) as wordSet 4 / countAt 3, which the dialect CAN represent -- opcodeOverrides[op].countAt already existed and ECL_GEN2 already shipped exactly this frame for its own 0x27, so the stated blocker was never real. Pools' handler at GAME.OVR:0x1626 was transcribed instruction by instruction: 8 reached sites, all 8 with an IMMEDIATE count (0 of 8 memory-coded), 7 of 8 with a non-empty tail that a flat 4-word frame misparses as instructions. THE SHALLOW CENSUS DID NOT DECIDE THIS and still reads 1 either way -- its one remaining stop (ECL1.DAX#49@0x698) is an unrelated 0x29 problem, and the round plan's own prediction that countAt would clear it is FALSE and recorded as such. What decided it: the two retail handlers; R1's independent execution-coverage oracle (12 Pools offsets executed by the VM but unreached by the deep walk, going to 0 under the frame); and the fact that the four route goldens which turned red were generated by the very VM under test, which poolsMiddleRoute.test.ts's own header discloses. They were regenerated, not obeyed. Effect on real content: the (4,13) ki-rin cell now awards the 15 items its own retail text promises instead of misparsing them, and Pools' deep desync count falls 18 -> 3 (shallow 3 -> 1).

ECL DECODE CENSUS, SHALLOW AND DEEP (round 33 R1, 2026-09-04): disassembleEclBlock stops at each block's FIRST EXIT, so every clean-EXIT count this project has ever published is a LOWER BOUND -- it never walks the combat, quest or descriptor subroutines placed later in a block's own bytes. walkEclReachable (packages/engine/src/ecl/reachability.ts) follows all five ECL header entry points and every GOTO/GOSUB/ON_GOTO/ON_GOSUB. Measured on this title's 56 retail blocks: 1 shallow desync block(s), 3 deep desync site(s). DEEP EXCEEDS SHALLOW HERE (3 vs 1), so any clean-EXIT count quoted elsewhere in this entry is a lower bound on this title's decode health, not a measure of it. Pinned in packages/engine/test/eclReachability.test.ts; the deep counts are SITES and the shallow counts are BLOCKS, so the two are not directly subtractable.

graphics.detail: The selected-folder route renders Pools' own wall, tile and frame banks for the mounted area and takes the tactical handoff. CORRECTED 2026-08-09: this row previously said no alternate graphics source was exposed as a switch. Pools is now the first GLIB/DataLib-era title with a live in-dungeon DOS-EGA<->Amiga wall-art toggle, and it is source-verified rather than approximated -- the Amiga port's WALLDEF.GLB records are BYTE-IDENTICAL to the DOS WALLDEF1.DAX blocks 1..6 (2340 bytes each) under the same id table, against banks of 256 8x8 tiles on both platforms, so the shared wall geometry indexes the Amiga art exactly.
gaps: Wall art on the routed area comes from the fallback piece set (see map_container), not from a script-supplied triple.
The Amiga toggle covers WALL art only: boot/UI tile sets 0 and 4 live in the other disk's 8X8DA.TLB and stay on DOS art, and no other Amiga asset family (pictures, sprites, portraits) is switched.
The toggle is only visible on maps that HAVE walls -- ?explore=pools mounts block 18, the zero-wall 'island in limbo', where both sources render an identical frame.
Native 320x200 screen composition, broad picture/animation coverage, palette timing, and pixel-level compositor parity remain incomplete.

map_container.detail: The selected-folder DAX source (ECL1, GEO1, WALLDEF1, 8X8D0/1, MON1CHA/SPC/ITM, ITEM0) drives legal movement from the GEO1#69 mount at (8,8,N) to the descriptor-23 tactical handoff, including the retail automatic-door edge on the final step.
gaps: The routed block emits no LOAD_PIECES, so the wall set comes from the explicit [1,255,255] source-backed fallback rather than from the script.
No repacking or write-side support for Pools' archives is claimed.

quests.detail: The script-corpus quest flag [0x0208] is proven engine-level: a single literal-address writer in the whole corpus (ECL1.DAX#82) with three consumers whose available content demonstrably changes, and the dialect dependence of that result was measured.
gaps: The flag's label is coined for this analysis — no such retail string exists anywhere in the install.
Engine-level only: no browser route wires the setter to its consumers.
The wider quest graph, campaign choices, and ending state are not covered.

retail_save.detail: Greybox save version 2 round-trips the routed Pools state — area, pose, clock, party, inventory, and ECL memory. This is Greybox persistence, not original-DOS save interoperability.

gaps: No retail-compatible Pools party or campaign-save encoder and no retail-executable acceptance proof exist.
export.scope: No Greybox session-to-Pools retail save exporter is shipped.

gaps: No Greybox reader or writer for Pools' own save/sidecar format exists, and no retail-executable acceptance proof exists.

ROSTER OUTCOME OF ?import=pools, ADDED 2026-09-05 (round 36 R6). AN ADDITION, NOT A CORRECTION -- measured on the pre-edit file this profile contained 0 occurrences each of BINKY, ABAGAIL, 'pregen' and 'party cap' and made no roster claim, so the ledger was silent here rather than wrong. MEASURED OUTCOME, denominator 6 (every retail SAVE/CHRDATA{1..6}.SAV): 6 of 6 join, 0 rule-rejections, 0 party-cap rejections -- unlike Treasures, whose 8 records overflow the shared six-hero cap. WHAT MOVED (round 35 R4): under Pools' OWN compiled race table at unpacked GAME.EXE 0xAEAD (stride 9, 7 entries, same seven names as Treasures' but at its own offset, derived independently; fencepost null 7 of 7 plausible short PStrings at the real base against 0 at all 16 bases shifted by +/-1..8), BINKY's race byte 0x01 at record offset 0xad reads Half-Elf rather than the borrowed CoAB enum's mountainDwarf, so her thief 13 (class byte 0x0e, classLevel[8]@0x151 = [0,0,8,0,0,0,13,0]) no longer exceeds a dwarf level cap of 8 and she is no longer rejected. The 0-based reading of the race byte is argued by consequence, indexing instruction not located -- imul r16, imm8 has zero hits in these 8086-targeted builds -- and is NOT to be upgraded to 'proven'. DERIVATION OF THE RULE-REJECTION COUNT, recorded 2026-09-05 because the figure was weaker than it looked when first written: round 36 R6 INHERITED the 0 from browser e2e case import-treasures and disclosed that it could not re-derive it in Python, and the pin asserts only that this string is present. It has since been reproduced independently twice against the retail bytes -- once by this round's adversarial verifier and once while correcting the falsified comment at apps/web/src/ui/main.ts -- both replaying the legality path under each title's OWN race table, both returning 0 rule-rejections, with BINKY and CHERROD joining and OUGO and SMOKE cut by the cap. So the number is corroborated -- but note WHAT is pinned: the e2e case and the Python replays share the same race-table premise, so they are not independent OF that premise. If it is ever overturned, this figure moves with it.

DISCLOSED DATA CONFLICT, CARRIED NOT RESOLVED (added 2026-09-05, round 36 R6) -- ABAGAIL disagrees WITH HERSELF, the Pools-side twin of Treasures' OUGO. In SAVE/CHRDATA5.SAV her class byte at 0xae is 0x05 = magic_user, which expects exactly one nonzero level slot, while her own classLevel[8] window at 0x151 reads [0,0,0,0,0,12,0,11]: magic_user 12 AND monk 11, two slots. She is the one record of Pools' six that fails the class/classLevel agreement oracle (5 of 6 agree). She JOINS -- the party is not full at her position -- so her disclosure rides the shown summary row's bold 'class byte and level array disagree -- shown raw, not translated' badge and does NOT need Treasures' rejectedPartyFullDisagreements channel; her monk level is separately disclosed as a dropped class, monk having no Dragonlance analog. The sheet is always built from the level array, never from the class byte. Bytes re-read first-hand from the retail GOG install on 2026-09-05 and re-derived by tools/test_round36_r6_roster_ledger.py, which fails if this bullet and the records stop agreeing.

Party, quest, and sidecar save structures are unmapped; the per-character CHRDATA record IS decoded and imported (see docs/engine/research/pools-treasures-race-table.md), and its race byte is now translated from this title's own compiled table (GAME.EXE 0xAEAD) rather than a borrowed enum (round 35 R4).
import.scope: No selected-folder importer for Pools retail party or campaign saves is shipped, and no quest, sidecar or campaign-save import of any kind. A BUNDLED URL ROUTE DOES SHIP, so this status must not be read as 'nothing imports': ?import=pools (apps/web/src/ui/importPoolsTreasuresParty.ts, armed from apps/web/src/ui/main.ts) reads the six retail SAVE/CHRDATA{1..6}.SAV pregens through the shared 510-byte POOLS_TREASURES_SAVED_CHARACTER_LAYOUT and builds a playable party. The measured roster outcome and the one disclosed data conflict in it are the bullet below.

ruleset.detail: Pools of Darkness runs on Greybox's shared AD&D party, first-person exploration, dialogue, tactical combat, treasure, and version-2 persistence systems.
gaps: Exhaustive retail spell, item, class, XP-table, monster-AI, and combat-rule parity is not claimed.
This title's high-level (post-Secret) rules — its extended spell ranges and its own scaling — are not modelled beyond the shared systems.

towns.detail: Pools' town leg is proven at the engine layer from independently re-measured retail bytes (ECL1.DAX 329,456 B / 56 blocks, GEO1.DAX 28,349 B / 32 blocks), with the dialect's effect on every VM result measured rather than assumed, and is now walked live: ?explore=pools-town boots Phlan's civic block at the cold-boot pose (15,0) facing west and walks 44 steps through the sign and service arms to the Sunrise Inn door.
gaps: Only the routed civic block is covered; the wider settlement set is not.

"Town" is not an engine mode here. Phlan is an ordinary stepped grid whose GEO descriptors dispatch to scripts through the same search_location every other Pools area uses — the same honest note Treasures' town leg carries.

wilderness.detail: Pools' wilderness leg is proven at the data/VM level from static retail bytes, independently re-measured by a second pass in which every load-bearing number, vaddr, offset, coordinate, count and roster was re-derived rather than carried over.
gaps: Static and engine-level only — no native trace, and no browser route mounts a Pools overland layer.
Encounter cadence, RNG continuity, and travel-time progression are not emulated.

early.citation: docs/engine/research/neverwinter-nights-dos-format-coverage.md § Support-matrix promotion (2026-07-22): ?explore=nwn-natural boots GEO1.DAX/ECL1.DAX#10 through this block's OWN eclInitialEntry header pointer (byte offset 149, vaddr 0x80D3; LOAD_FILES geoBlockId=10 self-referencing -> LOAD_PIECES [33,27,16]), a real self-contained boot leg rather than the block's default trampoline-to-19 entry. The LOAD_MONSTER/COMBAT vaddrs were recovered by single-stepping the real EclVm and cross-checked byte-for-byte against the dungeonEvents.test.ts golden. Persistence is a genuinely different mechanism from every other title here: an empirical bisection over every post-victory write found exactly ONE address, 11002 (0x2AFA, a SAVE_TABLE opcode-0x35 write rather than the masked SAVE that CoK/DoK use), that alone reproduces 'revisit does not refire' -- verified by a same-memory second primeSearchLocation() call with zero UI involvement.

ending.citation:
NWN `ending` = structurally-absent. Two independent evidences plus an exhaustive block-graph enumeration; the one genuine ending-word hit in the corpus is located and disposed of by its own context rather than asserted away.

(1) TEXT EVIDENCE — every ending-language hit in the shipped script corpus is a false positive, and the search covers reachable script text by two independent extractions. Extraction A (heuristic): every byte position of all 33 decompressed ECL blocks (ECL0/1/2/3/5/7) is tried as a `0x80 <len>` 6-bit inline-string frame and kept if it decodes to English-shaped uppercase text (≥6 chars, restricted charset, >0.85 letters-and-spaces) — 1,836 frames, 111,316 decoded characters, 1,409 unique strings totalling 96,542 characters; 1,827 of the 1,836 re-encode byte-identically over their full declared payload (the other 9 match only a prefix and are false frames, e.g. block 79 raw 0x0324 declared n=178 decoding to 'SCHEBAT1X'). Extraction B (structural, NO shape filter, added because A's 0.85 letters ratio has unmeasured recall): every `0x80` operand terminating a CFG-reachable instruction across all 33 blocks — 1,980 strings, 258 of which A drops, including ordinary script text such as "IT'S A FIGHT!", "'DANGER!  DO NOT ENTER!'" and "WHICH CANDLE DO YOU BLOW OUT? (1-13)". A 44-term ending predicate (CONGRATULATIONS, YOU HAVE WON, YOUR QUEST IS, IN YOUR HONOR, CELEBRATION, HAILED AS, FOREVER, THE END, …) over the union of A and B returns exactly 11 hits, every one a false positive with its sentence quoted: ECL0#1 v0x8D5C "SEA OF SWORDS" THE END-LESS; ECL0#2 v0x8D95, ECL1#12 v0x93AE and ECL1#15 v0x93D0 GRATEFUL (townsfolk thanks); ECL1#12 v0x9BFD, ECL1#17 v0x9538, ECL2#29 and ECL5#51 v0x8D59 "THE END" (of a wire / a room / a maze warning / a dock); ECL1#17 v0x9685 "IS NO MORE THAN 3 FEET HIGH"; ECL5#51 "HERE IS YOUR REWARD" (quest turn-in); and — the one hit extraction A alone misses, recovered only by B — ECL0#8 vaddr 0x94E6 PRINT, string operand at 0x94E7, "CONGRATULATIONS...  MYTHKAR...'". That last one is CONGRATULATIONS' only occurrence in the corpus and it is not an ending: it is the burned closing fragment of a Zhentarim letter looted mid-campaign, read in sequence at v0x93D3 "IN THE POCKET OF THE ZHENTIL MAGE YOU" / "FIND A NOTE.  IT ERUPTS IN FLAME" / "ALMOST IMMEDIATELY AFTER BEING OPENED," / "BUT YOU RECOLLECT SOME WORDS FROM THE" / "BRIEF GLANCE YOU ARE ALLOWED." / v0x946C "'GREETINGS, BAJYPH.  OUR CARAVANS GROW" / "LARGER BY... TO PLAN... BELIEVE THAT" / "GREETH, THE GREEDY... WILL CONTINUE TO" / "WIELD HIS POWERS ON OUR BEHALF." / "CONGRATULATIONS...  MYTHKAR...'", after which the path runs PROGRAM #4, CALL, EXIT — no epilogue, no PICTURE, no roster, no terminal NEWECL. (This restores a prior draft's correct finding: an earlier revision of this document wrongly claimed CONGRAT occurs zero times; that claim was an artifact of extraction A's 0.85 letters-ratio gate, which the string's 24/31 = 0.774 ratio falls below.) Across the union, YOU HAVE WON, YOUR QUEST IS, VICTORY IS YOURS, IN YOUR HONOR, HAILED AS and CELEBRATION occur zero times. PREDICATE CONTROL: the identical predicate on four sibling Gen1 titles using the same 6-bit packing lands on their real endings — Pool of Radiance 1,937 strings / 17 hits incl. ECL3.DAX#8 "CONGRATULATIONS! YOUR QUEST IS OVER! TYRANTHRAXUS IS DEFEATED! PHLAN IS FREE!"; CoAB 2,495 / 12 incl. ECL4.DAX#35 "CONGRATULATIONS, YOU HAVE WON" and ECL1.DAX#81 "AND A GREAT FEAST AND PARADE ARE HELD IN YOUR HONOR."; Secret 1,687 / 7 incl. ECL1.DAX#16 "YOU WILL BE HEROES HERE FOREVER. JOIN THE CELEBRATIONS"; CoK 2,333 / 8 incl. ECL1.DAX#17 "CONGRATULATIONS ON RECOVERING THE DRAGON EGGS". LIMIT OF THAT CONTROL, STATED: it validates the term list only. Every control ending string has a letters ratio of 0.917-1.000, above extraction A's gate, so the control is structurally incapable of detecting a recall failure in A's frame filter — that is why extraction B, which applies no shape filter, is run alongside it.

(2) FILE INVENTORY: the install directory holds 36 entries — 35 shipped files plus the runtime-written 16-byte CCFP.MOV — and none is named FINAL*; no ECL4.DAX, no ECL6.DAX, no GEO4..GEO9.DAX. FINAL* is the Gold Box endgame-art convention and is present in sibling installs (POOLRAD\FINAL5.DAX, Pools of Darkness FINAL.ACF/.BMA, DQK DISK3\FINAL.TLB). GAME.OVR still recognises the name: Pascal literals \x03PIC @0x4631F, \x05FINAL @0x46323, \x04.dax @0x46329; \x03PIC occurs 5 times, \x05FINAL exactly once, and the byte string FINAL occurs 0 times in GAME.EXE. (Honest limit: CoAB/Secret/CoK have endings and ship no FINAL* either, so this is corroboration, not proof — the same role WILDCOM.DAX's absence plays in Secret's wilderness leg.)

EXHAUSTIVE BLOCK ENUMERATION closing "you just failed to find it": all 33 blocks (ids 1-12, 14-30, 51, 59, 78, 79 across 6 archives; 29 GEO blocks across 4, every one 1026 bytes) are censused with size, reachable-instruction count, COMBAT count and NEWECL targets — 16,546 reachable instructions corpus-wide from all five header entries, both arms of every conditional. Every block has ≥1 reachable NEWECL (zero sinks), every NEWECL/LOAD_FILES operand is an immediate (zero dynamic), every target ships. 29 blocks LOAD_FILES their own id; the four with none (51/59/78/79) are NOT endgame scripts. ECL5#51, ECL7#78 and ECL7#79 are map overlays for areas that ship their own GEO: their hosts are pinned by the on-entry re-assertions ECL7#78 @0x801D COMPARE [0x4BF2],#28 and ECL7#79 @0x8014 COMPARE [0x4BF2],#29 (0x4BF2 = LastEclBlockId) together with their NEWECL targets (#1 for 51; #28/#29 for 78 and 79). Their dispatched cell descriptors are consistent with those hosts — 51 dispatches {36,37}, present in GEO0#1 at (1,11)=36, (1,13)=36, (4,0)=37; 78 dispatches {17,19,23,26}, present in GEO2#28 at 17@(7,11)=145, 19@(5,1)=147, 23@(14,4)=151, 26@(11,1)=154; 79 dispatches 15 descriptors, present in GEO2#29 incl. 114@(1,9)=242, 125@(1,3)=253, 108@(9,15)=236 — but that descriptor agreement is corroborative only and does not by itself identify the host: 6 of the 29 GEO blocks contain all four of 78's descriptors and 6 of 29 contain all fifteen of 79's. ECL5#59 is the sole block with no AND([0xC04F],#127→[0x4C02]) idiom, i.e. the only cutscene-shaped block: initial_entry 0x8018 lands on PRINTCLEAR "'I AM WILLO CLOVYR, AND I THANK YOU", 30 narration beats, ends @0x8440 NEWECL #9; sole caller ECL0#9 @0x9CE1. The plot points explicitly PAST the shipped data: ECL7#79 @0x8533 "THEY'VE BUILT A LARGE BASE BENEATH HIS CITY!", @0x85F6 "ALMOST READY TO LAUNCH AN ATTACK FROM THEIR BASE BENEATH NEVERWINTER!", @0x81A0 "OUR SECRET COMPLEX BENEATH NEVERWINTER" — that base has no GEO, no ECL, no descriptor, no NEWECL. (ECL0#8 carries the matching foreshadowing vision, v0x9A16-v0x9B16, ending "LEAVING YOU TO WONDER WHO HAS / CREATED THIS DARK PROPHECY, AND WHY.")

The strongest counter-argument, a victory path in the native binary, was chased to ground rather than waved away: GAME.OVR holds "You've won. Save before quitting? " (Pascal len 0x22 @0x4307, text @0x4308), and it IS reachable from shipped script — ECL opcode dispatcher @0x48EF (`mov al,[0xB577]`, arms 0x00..0x41), arm @0x4B02 `3c 38 75 06 0e e8 20 f8` calls the PROGRAM(0x38) handler @0x432A, whose arms `3c 07`, `3c 0c`, `3c 0d`, `3c 0e` call 0x4244 with kinds 0..3, which gates on four 115-byte DGROUP tables (0xE6D4/0xE7BC/0xE748/0xE830) then calls 0x404C, which loads cs:0x3637 (segment base 0xCD0 → file 0x4307). All of those byte anchors verify exactly against the retail overlay. This REFUTES any "unreachable" claim but strengthens the verdict: PROGRAM #7 occurs 28 times and PROGRAM #12 28 times, 28/28 immediately paired, exactly one pair in each of the 28 ordinary map blocks 2..30, 26/28 immediately after SAVE [0x4BCA],[0x32C8] (the area-id resync; the 2 exceptions write the adjacent byte 0x32C9) — a once-per-campaign terminal cannot be something invoked once per map block on every area transition. PROGRAM #13/#14 are never used; the corpus PROGRAM census is {0:2, 2:4, 4:131, 5:39, 6:21, 7:28, 11:2, 12:28, 16:62, 17:2}. The branch prints that one prompt and nothing else: GAME.OVR+GAME.EXE contain zero occurrences of CONGRATULAT/epilogue/victory/THE END; the three "Congratulations" strings are the post-combat XP award (0x46F3, 0x471F, 0x2967C) and "You have won the duel."/"You have won." (0x825C/0x8273) belong to the combat-result pool alongside "You have fled."/"You have lost the fight.". That the 115-byte-table / PROGRAM #7+#12 machinery is the AOL multiplayer shared-state layer is an INFERENCE; what `lcall 0x98:0x34(kind, buffer)` decides is genuinely unresolved.

DIALECT-PROOF: zero CFG-reachable 0x1D/0x22/0x2C sites corpus-wide, and ECL_GEN1 vs ECL_GEN1_SHORT produce byte-identical reachable-offset sets for all 33 blocks, so a silent desync cannot be the cause of this negative. "NWN is long-frame" remains INHERITED from neverwinter-nights-dos-eclinit.md, not re-proven here; this leg's result is dialect-proof either way. CROSS-CHECK: the per-block census was produced twice independently — Python via tools/gen1_ecl_encounter_scan.py and TypeScript via the engine's own decodeInstructionAt inside the golden — agreeing exactly (16,546 instructions, identical NEWECL sets, COMBAT counts and PROGRAM census). Both walkers implement the same successor rules, so their agreement rules out transcription and framing error, not a shared rule bug. STATIC ONLY: no DOSBox-X, no native trace, no EclVm run; the CFG walk over-approximates (both arms of every conditional, no comparison evaluated), which is the safe direction for a negative but means the instruction counts are not "instructions the game runs". Golden: packages/engine/test/nwnEndingRoute.test.ts (18 tests, all passing against the real retail bytes, none skipped) — note that its D2/D3 assertions must be updated to 11 predicate hits and to expect the ECL0#8 CONGRATULATIONS, and a recall assertion over the instruction-aligned extraction added, before this citation is transcribed. Doc: docs/engine/research/nwn-ending-route.md.

middle.citation:
NWN middle leg = `ECL1.DAX#17` / `GEO1.DAX#17` (the Zhentarim temple of Bane beneath Longsaddle). Doc: `docs/engine/research/nwn-middle-route.md`; golden: `packages/engine/test/nwnMiddleRoute.test.ts` (13 tests; scoped run `npx vitest run test/nwnMiddleRoute.test.ts` from `packages/engine` — note `pnpm --filter @goldbox/engine test -- nwnMiddleRoute` does NOT scope vitest). All bytes read from retail `D:/Games/Neverwinter Nights DOS/neverwinter-nights/neverwint/`; no DOSBox-X, no emulator, no native execution. Dialect `ECL_GEN1` (long frames), vbase 0x7FFE, headerLen 22, offset = vaddr − 0x8000 + 2.

BLOCK. ECL1#17 = 6681 bytes, magic 0x1388; header slots initial_entry 0x8095 (offset 151 — real code, not the 0x8014 trampoline), search_location 0x811C, vmRun1 0x840A, preCampCheck 0x841B, campInterrupted 0x8444. GEO1#17 = 1026 bytes, header word 1024; every one of the 256 descriptor bytes carries 0x80, and descriptors 94..127 occur EXACTLY ONCE each — 34 special cells in 1:1 correspondence with the 34 non-generic table indices.

ENTRY GATE. `initial_entry` runs LOAD_FILES #17,#2,#255 @0x80BD and LOAD_PIECES #3,#17,#255 @0x80C4 unconditionally, then COMPARE [0x4BF2] #126/#17/#16 @0x80DB/0x80E6/0x80F1; any other value falls to 0x83A3 `SAVE #9->[0xC04C]; SAVE #0->[0xC04B]; NEWECL #16` (bytes 933..947 = `090009014cc0090000014bc0200010`). Prologue bytes 151..204 = `2f007f014fc001024c0901024c01014c09000001004c09000101fb4b09000201fe4c09000001004d21001100 0200ff370003001100ff`. 16 and 17 are real corpus blocks; **126 is NOT a block in this corpus** and takes its own branch (0x80FC, the [0x4BCA]/[0x32C8] + PROGRAM #7/#12 path) — its meaning is UNIDENTIFIED, so it is not established as a "predecessor". Booting with [0x4BF2]=16 writes no pose at all, so whatever pose the predecessor left survives.

SPAWN POSE — A DISCLOSED SELECTION, NOT A UNIQUE FACT. Block 17's own `initial_entry` writes a pose only on the bounce path, so the entry pose comes from the predecessor. **ECL1#16 chains to 17 from three distinct arms, each writing its own pose**: desc-125 arm @0x92A8/0x92AE -> (15,10), bytes 4778..4792 = `09000f014bc009000a014cc0200011`; desc-126 arm @0x949D/0x94A3 -> (2,7) (offset 5279); desc-127 arm @0x96BD/0x96C3 -> (15,0) (offset 5823). GEO1#16 has exactly one cell of each: 125 at (9,12), 126 at (9,1), 127 at (1,7). This leg walks the desc-125 (chute-fall) entrance only — the arm whose narration is at 0x91A9/0x9236 and whose fight is DRIDER×4 + REMORHAZ×1 (MONCHA ids 43/93). Under strict passability the three poses open **three disjoint components of GEO1#17 — 72, 60 and 57 cells** — and only the 72-cell desc-125 component contains (2,11)/(1,11)/(0,9). Entry facing is never written by either block and is proven a non-dependency (all four cardinals fight identically, test F).

DISPATCH. search_location 0x811C -> `AND #127,[0xC04F]->[0x4C02]` @0x8123; descriptor 0 -> arm 0x8475; descriptors 1..93 clamp to 93 @0x819B; `SUBTRACT #93,[0x4C02]->[0x7F79]` @0x81A1 gives index = desc − 93; 35-entry `ON_GOSUB [0x7F79]` gate table @0x81B6, then 35-entry `ON_GOTO [0x7F79]` arm table @0x823A. The &0x7F mask is load-bearing: reading &0x3F maps 102->38 and 103->39, which clamp to 93, resolve to index 0, hit gate `0x839D` (`COMPARE #0,#0` -> equal) and exit at **`0x8226`** — silencing the whole encounter half.

ROUTE. 20 directed steps under STRICT passability (wall slot 0, or door flag 1 only; flags 2/3 excluded): (15,10)->(15,11)->(14,11)-door->(13,11) desc2->(12,11)->(11,11)->(10,11)->(9,11)->(8,11)->(7,11)->(6,11)->(6,10)->(5,10)-door->(4,10)->(3,10)->(3,11)->(2,11)-door desc102->(1,11) desc103->(1,10)->(0,10)->(0,9)-door desc108. Exactly four door edges, all [wall 1, flag 1]: (14,11)W, (5,10)W, (2,11)W, (0,10)N. Strict passability reaches only **72 of the 256 cells** from this pose and only 6 of the 34 special cells (98, 100, 101, 102, 103, 108); the beholder room at (12,9) (desc 104) and the other 28 special cells are NOT reachable from this entrance under this rule.

ARTICULATION + HOUR. BFS from (15,10) = 72 cells; minus (2,11) = 61 with (1,11) and (0,9) stranded; minus (1,11) = 62 with (0,9) stranded; negative controls minus (9,11) = 70 (only its alcove (9,10) stranded, (0,9) still reachable) and minus (15,13) = 71. Gate index 9 (desc 102) -> 0x8345 (`[0x4BC9] >= 18` or `< 6` -> fire; else 0x8394 clear+suppress); indices 10 and 15 (desc 103, 108) -> 0x835F, the exact complement (fires 6..17). [0x4BC9] is the ECL-owned hour — the label is inherited from `apps/web/src/ui/demoGen1.ts` `AREA_HOUR_ADDR`, and is corroborated but not proven by this block's own 0x8621 light routine (`COMPARE [0x4BC9] #19/#6`) and block 10's parity gates; the complementary structure is proven from the bytes regardless of the label. **Corrected claim:** from the desc-125 entry pose, every strict-passability path to the descriptor-108 chamber (0,9) must cross BOTH (2,11) and (1,11), and on a first crossing with a clear [0x2AF8] table exactly one of those two is armed at every one of the 24 hours — so that traversal cannot be made fight-free by choosing the hour or the route. It does NOT follow that "a party crossing this map cannot avoid a fight by any route": a party can stay in the other 61 cells, repeat crossings at the same half of the clock are silent because the slot is consumed, and the other two retail entrances open components containing none of these cells.

PERSISTENCE. `GETTABLE [0x2AF8],[0x7F79]` @0x8379 and `SAVE_TABLE #1,[0x2AF8],[0x7F79]` @0x83EF — the same base and mechanism as the already-proven early leg on ECL1#10 (whose consumed word 0x2AFA = 0x2AF8 + index 2; ECL1#10's own gates at 0x8357/0x8372 use the identical base). The consume lands only AFTER `COMBAT` @0x83C9; suppression via 0x8394 CLEARS the slot instead of setting it, so after a day walk consuming indices 10 and 15, moving the clock to night leaves 102 armed. Night walk sets exactly {9}; day walk exactly {10,15}.

ROSTERS (ids resolved against the real MONCHA.DAX, 100 records of 422 bytes). desc 102 arm 0x8F04 = PICTURE 84 + DISPLACER BEAST ×5 (id 34) + UMBER HULK ×2 (id 98); desc 103 arm 0x8F19 = PICTURE 84 + DISPLACER BEAST ×5 + PYRO SNAKE ×4 (id 92); desc 108 arm 0x95E0 = PICTURE 85 + HELL HOUND ×5 (id 35) + SALAMANDER ×2 (id 95); all three GOTO the shared epilogue 0x83B2.

CHAIN POSITION. A raw scan of all six ECL archives (33 blocks) for the immediate `20 00 11` returns exactly three sites, all in ECL1#16 (offsets 4790/5291/5835, all verified to be real NEWECL instructions), so ECL1#16 is the only block that can chain to 17; block 17's four `20 00 10` exits (945/5536/5978/6461, all verified real instructions writing return poses (0,9)/(5,12)/(3,9)) make it a chain cul-de-sac. Immediate-NEWECL hop distance from block 1 makes 17 the unique deepest block at distance 4 (1->12->15->16->17). The scan is a BYTE-OCCURRENCE claim: the exclusion direction is sound, but a computed/word-operand NEWECL would be missed (eight corpus sites have 0x20 followed by operand code 1/2/3 — ECL1#14@4263, ECL1#19@2101, ECL2#25@311/@6079, ECL2#28@449/@4006, ECL2#29@2568/@2595 — none in block 16 or 17, none verified as real instructions), and it produces false positives (block 28 names a target byte 34, and there is no block 34). "MID-CAMPAIGN" IS AN INFERENCE from that structure plus the strings (0x86CB "BLACK HAND ON A FIELD OF RED", 0x9210 "LORD MANSHOON OF ZHENTIL KEEP"), not a proven story position — hop distance is not story order (the apparent endgame blocks 78/79 sit at distance 2/3 via block 28, and have no GEO blocks at all).

DISCLOSURES. (a) The descriptor-0 arm carries a live `RANDOM #100 -> [0x7F7B]` @0x84AD and prints up to six atmosphere lines capped by `COMPARE [0x7B00] #5 IF_GT EXIT` @0x84D6. Test H exercises it at five seeds, but because each step builds a fresh VM from the same seed that is five distinct draws (31/48/98/2/74 at 0x1234/1/7/2003/0xbeef), not sixty — at seed 2003 the roll falls below the threshold and nothing prints. The real guarantee is STRUCTURAL: the entire descriptor-0 arm 0x8475–0x85E4, including all seven 0x84E7 ON_GOTO targets, contains no COMBAT opcode, so no plain-floor step can produce an encounter at any seed. (b) The operand dialect is NOT discriminating on this block — the full route under `ECL_GEN1_SHORT` is byte-identical (test J); the only assurance is negative (an independent long-frame disassembly lands cleanly on every arm boundary, decodes every inline string to clean English, and shows no desync). (c) DEAD CODE: `ON_GOTO [0x4C02] #3 [0x8475][0x86AC][0x86CA]` @0x8181 indices 1 and 2 are unreachable (the `COMPARE [0x4C02] #0; IF_GT GOTO 0x8190` guard diverts every desc >= 1), and an xref finds `AC 86`/`CA 86` exactly once each, both inside that ON_GOTO's own operand list (offsets 397/400) — so BOTH descriptor-2 cells, (13,11) and (13,12), are silent, as is the single descriptor-1 cell (12,1); the 0x86CB temple description and the 0x86AC graveyard line never print from cell dispatch. That it is an authoring bug is an INFERENCE; only the unreachability is proven. (d) The retail combat-result word [0x7EC7] is UNMODELLED — it stays 0, taking the "party won and stayed" fall-through, so the 128/129 branches at 0x83D0/0x83DB are never exercised and their reading as flee/defeat is an inference. (e) The `[0x0064]` bypass at 0x81AA (`IF_NE GOTO 0x8227`) skips the gate table entirely and is not modelled. (f) No native execution: every claim is static retail bytes plus this repo's own EclVm, whose fidelity to DOS NWN is assumed, and the combats are only "offered" — `afterCombat('victory')` is a harness call.

quest.citation: QUEST — PROVEN (cross-archive), with the setter-uniqueness claim narrowed. Kraken Society dock password, `[0x32C8]`/`[0x32CA]`. Doc: `docs/engine/research/nwn-quest-flag.md`. Test: `packages/engine/test/nwnQuestFlag.test.ts` (15 tests, all passing, not skipped; retail `D:\Games\Neverwinter Nights DOS\neverwinter-nights\neverwint\`). CROSS-ARCHIVE CORE (independently re-measured): over all 33 blocks of ECL0/1/2/3/5/7.DAX, `[0x32CA]` is the ONLY memory word in the entire game that has a writer somewhere and a reader block with no local writer — that block being `ECL1.DAX#14`, whose 25 `COMPARE [0x32ca],#n` arms (`@0x9461 = 03 01 ca 32 00 01` …) select a password word it never sets. SETTER — exactly one corpus-wide site writes the password-CONSOLE value (the clamped `INPUT_NUMBER` result held in `[0x7F79]`) into either cell, and it writes both: `ECL5.DAX#51` (5529 bytes), descriptor-37 console, `@0x9572 = 09 01 79 7f 01 c8 32` and `@0x9582 = 09 01 79 7f 01 ca 32`, bracketed by `@0x9579 = 09 00 0e 01 c5 4b` (SAVE #14->[0x4bc5]), `@0x957f = 38 00 11` (PROGRAM #17), `@0x9589 = 09 00 01 01 c5 4b`, `@0x958f = 38 00 11`. `[0x4BC5]` has exactly two operand references corpus-wide, both those writes, and is read nowhere in ECL; `38 00 11` gives 5 raw hits of which only these 2 are instruction starts (the 3 in `ECL2.DAX#26` are operand-byte coincidences). IT IS NOT THE ONLY WRITER OF THE CELLS — 37 reachable writes exist corpus-wide: 29 day-cache `SAVE [0x4bca]` writes (28 -> `[0x32C8]`, 1 -> `[0x32CA]` at `ECL1.DAX#17 @0x8caf`) plus `ECL1.DAX#16 @0x8af6 SAVE [0x4bc9],[0x32c8]` (the hour, 0-23), `ECL1.DAX#17 @0x8dad`/`@0x9153 SAVE #255,[0x32ca]`, `ECL2.DAX#26 @0x8cd0 SAVE #1,[0x32c8]`, `ECL2.DAX#27 @0x9336 SAVE #1,[0x32ca]` and `@0x933d SAVE #0,[0x32ca]`; four of those deposit values inside the 0-25 table range. `[0x32C8]`/`[0x32CA]` are therefore general-purpose per-area persistent slots of which the dock password is one use. CONSUMER A (CROSS-ARCHIVE) — `ECL1.DAX#14` (5668 bytes), descriptor 112 = `GEO1.DAX#14` cell (15,6): index = descriptor-104 = 8; ON_GOSUB pre-gate arm 8 = `0x843d` = `COMPARE #0,#1; RETURN` (always fires, no time or `[0x2AF8]` consumed-check); ON_GOTO body arm 8 = `0x8eed`: `PICTURE #94`, `LOAD_MONSTER #44,#2,#44`, `LOAD_MONSTER #94,#4,#94`, `COMBAT`, then `@0x8f92 = 02 01 56 94` (GOSUB the 26-entry ladder at 0x9456) and `@0x8f96 = 11 81 1e 7b` (PRINT the selected word) inside "TELL THE MAN AT THE DOCK IN NEVERWINTER, THE PASSWORD IS '<word>' FOR TRAVEL TO THE PURPLE ROCKS." Reachable in play: from `ECL1.DAX#12`'s trapdoor hand-off (`0x9d20/0x9d26/0x9d2c` = (11,6), NEWECL #14), (15,6) is 32 legal steps away inside an 81-cell component. CONSUMER B (HEADLINE GATE) — `ECL5.DAX#51` descriptor 36 = `GEO0.DAX#1` cells (1,11) and (1,13); `ECL0.DAX#1` search_location 38-arm `ON_GOTO @0x8284` arm 36 -> `@0x92b7 = 03 01 4d c0 00 03` (facing WEST, IF_NE EXIT) -> `NEWECL #51`, arm 37 -> `@0x92c2 = 20 00 33`. In the overlay: night gate `COMPARE [0x4bc9],#5 / IF_LT` and `COMPARE [0x4bc9],#20 / IF_GE` @0x8bcc, then `@0x8dcd = 10 00 08 81 00 7b` (INPUT_STRING #8), `@0x8dd3 = 02 01 52 93` (GOSUB the `[0x32c8]` ladder at 0x9352), `@0x8dd7 = 03 81 00 7b 81 1e 7b`, `@0x8dde = 16` (IF_EQ), `@0x8ddf = 01 01 7c 8e`, accept arm `@0x8e7c = 32 00 46` (FIND_ITEM #70) `@0x8e7f = 00` (EXIT); refusal arm prints the "SMALL PURPLE SQUID" brush-off, `PROGRAM #5`, `NEWECL #1`. Note that `[0x32C8]` is read and written inside `ECL5.DAX#51` itself, so the cross-ARCHIVE property is carried by the `[0x32CA]` side alone. THE TWO LADDERS were re-decoded from the retail 6-bit packed strings and are byte-order-identical 26-entry tables (FUTURE, TIME, FRONT, RIPE, STORM, JUNGLE, VISION, MATAGA, BORK, TWAIN, MOUNTAIN, WOODS, PALADIN, BARDICHE, GNOME, STATUE, GODDESS, UNDOMIEL, TEMPLE, RAPTURE, EMPIRE, VIOLIN, FIEND, PENDENT, OMINOUS, DUNGEON), differing only in the cell compared. END-TO-END, real EclVm, real bytes: the console writes both cells and the in-script re-display reads the new word back; that memory carried into `dialogueForCell(ECL1#14, 112)` yields the 44x2/94x4 combat then the note naming the same word; carried into the descriptor-36 gate the doorman EXITs on that word for all 26 indices. NEGATIVE CONTROLS: a different but real table word -> `chain` to block 1 with the PURPLE SQUID text, all 26 indices, plus empty/"XYZZY"/"PASSWORD"; facing north on (1,11) -> no chain; `[0x4bc9]=12` (day) -> the empty-dock description and chain to block 1, `INPUT_STRING` never reached. CAVEATS (all disclosed, none hidden): (i) the descriptor-37 console at `GEO0.DAX#1` (4,0) is provably WALK-UNREACHABLE — forward BFS from `ECL0#1`'s own byte-grounded spawn (8,7) covers 194 cells and excludes it, and a reverse BFS shows only {(1,0),(2,0),(3,0),(4,0)} can ever step into it, disjoint from that component and containing none of the seven declared entry poses (7,0),(10,5),(15,7),(7,15),(2,6),(1,11),(8,7), all under the engine's permissive door rule (`explorer.ts:163`); the in-play source of the index is host/save-side and UNLOCATED. (ii) The per-area-bank reading of `SAVE #n,[0x4bc5]; PROGRAM #17` is an INFERENCE — NWN's `PROGRAM` dispatch in GAME.OVR was not disassembled — and the leg's "the note always names exactly the word the doorman expects, including at the untouched default 0 = FUTURE" holds ONLY under that reading. Under the alternative single-global-word reading neither cell is untouched by the time the party crosses from area 14 to area 1, and the two desync. The leg does not discriminate between the two readings; its supporting-but-not-conclusive evidence for per-area storage is the 28-block `COMPARE [0x4bca],[0x32c8]` / `SAVE [0x4bca],[0x32c8]` "already visited today" idiom, which only works if the slot is per-area, plus `ECL0.DAX#1` referencing `[0x32C8]` zero times. (iii) `FIND_ITEM #70`'s meaning is unresolved; "the doorman accepts" means only that the VM terminates `exited` and never emits the refusal text. (iv) Static CFG + GEO graph only; no DOSBox-X. (v) The `[0x4BC9]` = hour label is borrowed from this repo's CoK documentation (`docs/engine/research/cok-improvement-loop.md`), not re-derived from NWN's host; the leg needs only "some engine word forks day vs night", which the test asserts behaviourally. (vi) Reproducing the 93.6% corpus / 25.1% `ECL5#51` BFS coverage requires `scan_block`'s COMPARE-outcome reset, not `decode_one`/`header_entries`/`successors` alone (those three give 12.3% and never reach the console). TOOL BUG REPORTED (not worked around silently): `tools/map_gen1_cross_area_flag_reads.py` cannot find this flag — `FLAG_REGISTRY` has no `neverwinter-nights-dos` entry, and its write classifier `ins.mnemonic == "SAVE" and arg_index == 1` misclassifies SAVE_TABLE (0x35) and GETTABLE (0x2A) destinations (and ADD/SUB/AND/OR/RANDOM/INPUT_*/PARLAY/CHECKPARTY destinations) as READS — a systematic false negative of the same family as the one fixed in `5febedb`.

town.citation:
NWN-DOS `town` leg = PROVEN on `ECL0.DAX#1` / `GEO0.DAX#1` (Neverwinter). Doc `docs/engine/research/nwn-town-route.md`; golden `packages/engine/test/nwnTownRoute.test.ts` (14 tests, 14 pass, retail-byte-backed, not skipped when the install is present). Dialect ECL_GEN1 (long frame); vbase 0x7FFE, file_offset = vaddr-0x8000+2. Header of ECL0#1 (4808 b), re-read as `88 13` + five `01 01 <vaddr>` far pointers: vm_run_1 0x82FC, search_location 0x81E1, pre_camp_check 0x839A, camp_interrupted 0x83C5, initial_entry 0x8014 (= file offset 22).

DISCRIMINATOR. `inDungeon` [0x4BE6] is written ZERO times corpus-wide (confirmed by two independent methods), so no engine-mode signal exists; the town signal is the retail town-service dispatch — `SAVE #1,[0x7F6C]` EnterShop, `SAVE #1,[0x7EE2]` EnterTemple, `SAVE #127,[0x7EA8]` training_class_mask adjacent to COMBAT / PROGRAM #0. CORRECTION to the earlier framing: the conjunctions do no work. `EnterTemple` ALONE selects exactly {ECL0#1, ECL1#12, ECL2#24, ECL2#25} — identical to {EnterShop AND EnterTemple}; `training=127` ALONE selects exactly {ECL0#1, ECL2#25} — identical to the triple. The honest statement is that ONE flag, EnterTemple, is the whole discriminator, and its strength is that it has zero false positives over 33 blocks, not that a cluster narrows anything.

CENSUS over 6 ECL archives / 33 blocks, re-derived twice: EnterShop 20 sites / 13 blocks; EnterTemple 4 / 4; training_class_mask 33 sites (31 write 0, exactly 2 write 127 — ECL0#1@0x87D6, ECL2#25@0x96E7); game_area [0x7F12] 9 naive / 8 instruction-reachable (all 9 write the constant 1, so it shows the address is used, not what it means in NWN); inDungeon 0 by both methods. All four selected blocks are settlements: "WELCOME TO NEVERWINTER!" @0x815D, "'WELCOME TO TRIBOAR,' SAYS THE INNKEEPER. 'WOULD YOU LIKE TO REST FOR 1 PLATINUM?'" @0x89AA, "'WELCOME TO NIGHTSEDGE'" @0x936D; ECL2#24 is identified only INDIRECTLY, from a guard's line "…MORE DANGEROUS THAN HERE IN FLOODBLEST" @0x9135. Priced innkeeper rests exist in all four — ECL0#1@0x870D (1 pp), ECL1#12@0x89AA (1 pp), ECL2#25@0x8AAB (5 pp), ECL2#24@0x95EC (1 pp; NOT the sign at 0x8E03 the golden cites). Zero dungeon blocks selected.

STRUCTURE. `search_location` @0x81E1 masks the descriptor `AND #127,[0xC04F],[0x4C02]`, then `COMPARE [0xC04F],#129 / IF_LT / GOTO 0x827C` forks on bit 7 into a 38-arm DOORWAY `ON_GOTO` @0x8204 (file offset 518) and a 38-arm STREET-SIGN `ON_GOTO` @0x8284 (offset 646). Both open `25 01 02 4c 00 26` — the SAME selector [0x4C02] and the same fork — so their agreement is a consistency check on one shared index rendered twice, not two independent indices. Door arms: 3→0x869E weaponry, 4/5/6→0x8832 temple, 7→0x8404 general, 8→0x8462 silver, 9→0x84BA jeweller, 10/11/12/13→0x87A3 training, 15–36→0x831F EXIT, 37→0x92C2. Sign arms 5/6/7/8 all →0x8996 "ADVANCE LEVELS HERE". Cold boot: `initial_entry` @0x8014 compares [0x4BF2] against 51/127/1/2/3/4/27/28; a zero LastEclBlockId matches none and falls through to the default arm @0x8138 → x=8, y=7, facing=3 (west).

GEO0#1 is 1026 b, 16x16; descriptors raw[514+y*16+x] (engine `decodeGeoBlock` floor == that byte, 0/256 mismatches); spawn (8,7) is descriptor 0. Neverwinter has TWO shopping districts (west: doors x=6 / signs x=7, y=2..4; south-east: doors y=11 / signs y=10, x=13..15). GEOMETRY, stated in the direction golden test N actually asserts (SIGN→DOOR): every cell carrying sign descriptor 11/12/13/16/17/18/6/22 is orthogonally adjacent to exactly one door of the paired type — general 11 @(7,2),(14,10) ↔ doors 135 @(6,2),(14,11); silver 12 @(7,3),(13,10) ↔ 136 @(6,3),(13,11); jewelry 13 @(7,4),(15,10) ↔ 137 @(6,4),(15,11); temples 17/16/18 @(10,5),(10,9),(10,12) ↔ 133 @(10,4),(10,10),(10,13); training 6 @(7,11) ↔ 139 @(6,11); Cragdyk 22 @(12,6) ↔ 131 @(13,6). The DOOR→SIGN direction is NOT claimed and is not true: the training arm 0x87A3 is entered from descriptors 138/139/140/141 = eight cells (6,10)-(6,13) and (14,0)-(14,3), of which only (6,11) and (14,1) (sign 7 @(13,1), same 0x8996 arm) touch a sign cell at all; the weaponry descriptor 131 occupies four cells (8,0),(13,6),(15,8),(6,15), advertised by four different arms-&-armor signs — 9 KROEGEL'S @(8,1), 3 BAYLESS @(14,8), 1 BRORSMAN'S @(6,14), 22 CRAGDYK'S @(12,6). Arms cover more cells than the doc's per-building table lists: shops 8 door cells, temple 3, jeweller 2, training 8.

ROUTE. A 42-step circuit from (8,7) visits all six service doors. Re-measured off the raw GEO planes: 29 edges are wall slot 0 / door flag 0, and the remaining 13 all carry door flag 1 — no flag-2/flag-3 edge and no non-zero-wall-with-door-flag-0 edge anywhere — so every step is unconditional. Each cell was dispatched through the real `EclVm` from a FRESH memory map, i.e. 42 independent single-cell dispatches, not a continuous retail traversal.

LIMITS. NWN has NO Town engine mode — Neverwinter is mechanically an ordinary dungeon-mode stepped grid with shops on it. The mapping EnterShop/EnterTemple/training → `CityShop()`/`temple_shop()`/`startGameMenu()` and the Area2 address model `offset = (loc*2 + 0x800) & 0xFFFF` are inherited from the CoAB source oracle (`coab_extracted/Classes/Area2.cs` offsets 0x550/0x5C4/0x624/0x6D8/0x6DA/0x7EC; `engine/ovr003.cs CMD_Combat`; `engine/ovr008.cs vm_SetMemoryValue`; `Classes/Opperation.cs GetCmdValue`); NWN's own GAME.EXE/GAME.OVR was NOT disassembled — the single largest inference. Cross-title control: Gateway's proven town block ECL5#19 writes all three flags (raw-byte census 2/2/1×127 at 0x8761, 0x890A / 0x8AE4, 0x8B66 / 0x8CB5) but ALSO writes `inDungeon=1` @0x8030, which NWN never does, so the precedent is partial. §6a-ii's "reachable" column reproduces exactly (20/4/33/8/0; ECL0#1 coverage 4785/4808) ONLY under a walk that keeps BOTH `IF_*` successors live and does NOT narrow compare outcomes; the repo's checked-in `gen1_ecl_encounter_scan.successors()` narrows outcomes and yields 3/3/32/5/0 — that scanner limitation, not dialect, is the likelier cause of §6b's non-credible all-zero rows. `ECL5.DAX#51 @0x90FE` is unreached from the five header entries and unreferenced by any operand in the corpus, but decodes as coherent code (`SAVE #1,[0x7F12] / COMPARE [0x7F12],#1 / IF_NE / NEWECL #1 / GOSUB [0x810C]`) — dead/unreferenced code, not "string payload". Triboar/Floodblest/Nightsedge are identified only; their maps and routes were not walked. Test L honestly records that this route does NOT discriminate the dialect (ECL_GEN1 / ECL_GEN1_SHORT / ECL_GEN1_SHORT_GATEWAY give identical output on every service arm); the long-frame dialect is inherited from `neverwinter-nights-dos-eclinit.md`. A real engine defect is disclosed and not locked in by the golden: `EclVm.rvalue()` (vm.ts:818-821) treats operand code 0x02 as a memory read where retail `Opperation.GetCmdValue()` returns a 16-bit immediate. No DOSBox-X, no emulator, no native trace.

wilderness.citation: docs/engine/research/neverwinter-nights-dos-format-coverage.md § Wilderness leg: structurally-absent (2026-08-05). A proven negative carrying the same two independent pieces of evidence Secret's wilderness leg -- the only prior exemplar of this verdict -- was closed on. (1) Whole-corpus scanner zero from a scan that actually ran: `tools/map_gen1_area_mode_writes.py --profile neverwinter-nights-dos` reports 0 statically reachable `SAVE ...,0x4BE6` sites (Area1.inDungeon, Area1 offset 0x1CC -- the single binary host flag the retail engine flips between GameState.DungeonMap and GameState.WildernessMap, and the only binary-provable engine-mode split in the Gen1 corpus) across 6 ECL archives (ECL0/1/2/3/5/7.DAX) and 33 script blocks, matching that doc's own independent 33-block inventory, decoded with the correct long-frame GEN1_WORD_SETS dialect (NWN is not one of the four short-frame titles, so there is no dialect desync). CRITICAL: this zero was not obtainable before 2026-08-05 and the previous zero was a FALSE NEGATIVE -- neverwinter-nights-dos was missing from GEN1_PROFILE_IDS, so the profile was filtered out of build_report() before a single block was read, emitting `"games": []` while printing "gen1 area-mode writes: 0", which is indistinguishable from a real negative at the CLI. That is the same scope bug, in the same tuple, that was fixed for death-knights-of-krynn on 2026-07-18 and never generalized. Gateway is the control proving the repair yields true positives: it went 0 -> 24 and the repaired scanner independently rediscovered BOTH of Gateway's already-proven legs -- ECL6.DAX#21 SAVE 0 -> 0x4be6 at vaddr 0x808e (value 0 = WildernessMap, its proven wilderness leg) and ECL5.DAX#19 SAVE 1 (Sundabar, its proven town leg, correctly inDungeon=1). (2) NWN ships DUNGCOM.DAX + RANDCOM.DAX and NO WILDCOM.DAX, confirmed by direct file listing; measured the same way in the same run, Secret ships DUNGCOM.DAX only while Gateway, Treasures and Pools of Darkness all DO ship WILDCOM.DAX, so Secret's negative is demonstrably not being over-applied. The counter-argument is addressed rather than ignored: RANDCOM's outdoor-looking prop tiles do not imply a WildernessMap mode, because per ovr011.cs SetupGroundTiles() RANDCOM is always layered on top of whichever 24x24 bank is active -- an overlay, not the mode selector. Scope: this claims NWN's retail ECL contains no statically reachable overland/area-mode transition and no wilderness floor bank ships, bounded by static reachability from the five ECL header entry points -- the same bound every row in gen1-area-mode-writes.md carries. It does not claim NWN has no outdoor areas. Regenerated report: docs/engine/research/gen1-area-mode-writes.md (corpus total 128 -> 152). Tier unchanged at `persistent`; middle, ending, town and quest remain outstanding.

ecl.detail: NWN-DOS uses the plain long-frame ECL_GEN1 dialect (verified: no cellDescAddr override is needed — this title's own scripts read the same [0xC04F] primeSearchLocation already seeds). Retail blocks execute across archives: ECL1#10 (area 1), ECL1#17 (the Zhentarim temple of Bane beneath Longsaddle), ECL0#1 (Neverwinter town), and the cross-archive Kraken Society dock-password flag. One real finding was needed to boot area 1 at all: block 10's default entry is a non-local GOTO trampoline into block 19 and emits no LOAD_FILES, while the block's OWN eclInitialEntry header pointer (byte 149, vaddr 0x80D3) is a self-contained boot leg.
gaps: Coverage is of reachable code on the routed blocks; the archives' unreached arms are decoded but unexecuted.
