early.citation: tools/goldbox_corpus_routes.json's dark-queen-of-krynn route record (Gen2/HLIB, the only non-DAX row in this file): area 5's browser route enters the real CampInterrupted handler only after vmRun1 selects table byte 0xE5 at (30,3); the live-party browser host and CCECL's same strength seed queue four ZOMBIE records (#37); after the real combat continuation writes [0x003A]=1, Greybox v2 saves the dedicated Area-5 ECL memory and prevents a resolved encounter from replaying after reload. Cited as `early` under this file's own precedent (a game's first proven natural-combat route with consumed state is its early leg), NOT as a claim about where area 5 sits in DQK's plot. Exact original-DOS host/RNG selection remains unproven and is recorded as a gap on the route record itself.

ending.citation: RESOLVED 2026-08-07 (docs/engine/research/dqk-0032-writer.md; anchored in packages/engine/test/dqkCampaignLegs.test.ts cases G and H). STATIC/BYTE-ONLY: no DOSBox-X, GameLink, emulator or screenshot evidence. The prior BLOCKED verdict rested on 'nothing in the 47-area ECL corpus ever writes [0x0032] nonzero'. That statement is TRUE and IRRELEVANT: [0x0032] is not a story flag. DQK.EXE's ECL operand resolver intercepts address 0x32 in a class-0 special-address table (25a4:0897, values at DQK.EXE file 0x040BB3) and dispatches it to 25a4:099c = a0 f3 c9 (mov al,[0xc9f3]) -- the wall type of the map edge the party faces, recomputed from the GEO planes by 2f0d:0628 on every move and every turn (all four writers of 0xC9F3 are that same recompute). The write path (25a4:06d2, table at file 0x0409E8) has NO entry for 0x32, so the four corpus SAVE #0,[0x0032] sites are dead stores against a byte the read path never consults. Independent cross-check that does not depend on any disassembly judgement: the same table maps ECL [0x002d] -> [0xc9f4], and 0x002d is the Gen2 cellDescAddr this project established years earlier from an unrelated direction, pinning the whole [0xc9f0..f4] X/Y/facing/wallType/cellDescriptor block (the same 5-tuple already located for DoK). THE ENDING DOES NOT DEPEND ON IT: area 66 dispatches on AND #0x7F,[0x002d]->[0x009B] at 0x8669 then ON_GOTO with 15 arms; arm 14 (0x9D18) is gated ONLY on the [0x00A0] step counter and issues GOSUB 0x9F03; NEWECL #67. ECL #67 is the finale (Takhisis on a burnished throne before the portal, golden bell) and is a cutscene, not a map -- its four non-init entries all point at one stub. Arm 14's cell is descriptor 0x8E at (27,4), the ONLY such cell, 38 steps from area 66's scripted landing pose (6,21) written at 0x80B1. Note the pose is written twice: 0x8055's (29,21) only stages the 17-frame 'FALLING BETWEEN WORLDS' loop and sits in a 110-cell region that CANNOT reach the ending; both are asserted in case H so the distinction cannot silently rot. Combined with the already byte-proven ingress chain area 5 -> 62 -> 64 -> 66 (docs/engine/research/dqk-ending-ingress.md), the ending is reachable by ordinary play. Side effect of this investigation: it exposed a real engine bug -- Gen2 GEO header order is (height, width), not (width, height), so 8 of the 20 DQK maps were being transposed; fixed in packages/engine/src/loaders/geo.ts + geoEncode.ts.

middle.citation: Investigated 2026-08-07 by a 5-finder + 5-adversarial-refuter workflow (docs/engine/research/dqk-campaign-legs.md); every claim below was then INDEPENDENTLY RE-DERIVED FROM THE RETAIL BYTES BY THE OPERATOR and pinned in packages/engine/test/dqkCampaignLegs.test.ts before this status was written. Agent findings alone were not accepted as evidence. STATIC/BYTE-ONLY: no DOSBox-X, GameLink, emulator or screenshot evidence. MIDDLE = ECL area 31. Case E: 0x92EF `24` COMBAT, 0x92F0 `17` IF_NE, 0x92F1 GOTO 0xA4EC, then the consume: 0x92F5 `09 00 1c 01 bf 00` SAVE #28 -> [0x00BF] (a bit NUMBER) and 0x92FB `02 01 3b a4` GOSUB 0xA43B. 0xA43B is a GENERIC set-bit-N helper, asserted byte-for-byte over its full 46 bytes: DIV [0x00BF] by 8; read the remainder via operand code 3 at address 0x0029; TABLE base 0x014C index [0x00BF] -> [0x00C0]; TABLE base 0xA4DC index remainder -> [0x00C1]; OR; then 0x35 SAVE_TABLE. The mask table at 0xA4DC is asserted to be exactly 01 02 04 08 10 20 40 80. Bit 28 therefore resolves to byte 28/8=3, bit 28%8=4, mask 0x10, address 0x014C+3 = 0x014F. CORRECTION TO THE FINDING, made during operator verification: the finding stated the consume as a literal write '[0x014F] |= 0x10'. It is NOT literal -- SAVE_TABLE writes a COMPUTED address, and an alignment-free census proves [0x014F] is named ZERO times in area 31 (the base [0x014C] is named five times: 0xA44C/0xA46D/0xA485/0xA4A6/0xA4BE). The address is arithmetically right but DERIVED. NOT CLAIMED: no VM route golden; the roster and the GEO cell pairing are not asserted here.

quest.citation: Investigated 2026-08-07 by a 5-finder + 5-adversarial-refuter workflow (docs/engine/research/dqk-campaign-legs.md); every claim below was then INDEPENDENTLY RE-DERIVED FROM THE RETAIL BYTES BY THE OPERATOR and pinned in packages/engine/test/dqkCampaignLegs.test.ts before this status was written. Agent findings alone were not accepted as evidence. STATIC/BYTE-ONLY: no DOSBox-X, GameLink, emulator or screenshot evidence. QUEST = [0x0187] bit 0x20, written in area 55 and read in area 54. Case C: setter area 55 @0x80DD `30 01 87 01 00 20 01 87 01` OR [0x0187],#0x20 -> [0x0187]; reader area 54 @0x977F `2f 01 87 01 00 20 01 bf 00` AND [0x0187],#0x20 -> [0x00BF], then @0x9788 `03 01 bf 00 00 00 17` COMPARE [0x00BF],#0 / IF_NE. An ALIGNMENT-FREE census over all 47 areas (truncation-immune, so an opcode-table error cannot desync it) proves exactly TWO areas name [0x0187] at all: 54 and 55. IMPORTANT QUALIFICATION added during operator verification and NOT present in the finding: [0x0187] is a shared BITFIELD, not a single flag -- enumerating every OR-write of an immediate into it corpus-wide gives bits [0x01,0x04,0x08,0x10,0x20,0x40,0x40,0x40,0x80]. So 'sole setter of the WORD' would be FALSE; 'sole setter of the BIT' is what is true, and bit 0x20 is written exactly once, only by area 55 @0x80DD. Negative control on the clear side: area 54 @0x8B24 carries an AND clear-mask of 0xBF, which PRESERVES bit 0x20 (it clears 0x40), so nothing in the corpus ever clears this bit. DECLARED LIMIT: the census matches operands naming the address LITERALLY; opcode 0x35 SAVE_TABLE writes a COMPUTED base+offset and would be INVISIBLE to it -- the middle leg's own helper is exactly such a computed write. SCOPE NOTE: areas 54 and 55 are ADJACENT ids, unlike the Secret's-Sixth-Route precedent's non-adjacent blocks.

town.citation: Investigated 2026-08-07 by a 5-finder + 5-adversarial-refuter workflow (docs/engine/research/dqk-campaign-legs.md); every claim below was then INDEPENDENTLY RE-DERIVED FROM THE RETAIL BYTES BY THE OPERATOR and pinned in packages/engine/test/dqkCampaignLegs.test.ts before this status was written. Agent findings alone were not accepted as evidence. STATIC/BYTE-ONLY: no DOSBox-X, GameLink, emulator or screenshot evidence. TOWN = ECL area 4 (Palanthas). Case B decodes the retail bytes rather than citing a scan: 0x82D0 `2b 01 bf 00 00 07` HORIZONTAL_MENU with destination [0x00BF] and count 7, followed by seven inline 6-bit packed strings that unpack to exactly ['PALACE','TEMPLE','HALL','SHOP','INN','BAR','LEAVE'] -- a canonical Gold Box town service list, and what makes area 4 a town rather than a dungeon pane. The menu's operands consume exactly up to 0x82FE, where `25 01 bf 00 00 07` ON_GOTO reads THE SAME cell [0x00BF] the menu wrote, with a matching arm count of 7 and targets 0x8319/0x860F/0x8648/0x8655/0x85D6/0x8689/0x87CB. That menu-writes / dispatch-reads mutual reference is the discriminating fact: a mis-framed menu cannot produce it. NOT CLAIMED: the per-service round trip and the [0x009A]-gated LEAVE exit are described in the doc but are NOT asserted in the test.

wilderness.citation: Investigated 2026-08-07 by a 5-finder + 5-adversarial-refuter workflow (docs/engine/research/dqk-campaign-legs.md); every claim below was then INDEPENDENTLY RE-DERIVED FROM THE RETAIL BYTES BY THE OPERATOR and pinned in packages/engine/test/dqkCampaignLegs.test.ts before this status was written. Agent findings alone were not accepted as evidence. STATIC/BYTE-ONLY: no DOSBox-X, GameLink, emulator or screenshot evidence. WILDERNESS = area 18 -> area 5 -> nine further areas. Case D: area 18 @0x85A8 `20 00 05` NEWECL #5 exits into the overland map; area 5 carries a CONTIGUOUS crossing table in 0xA3DF..0xA551 enumerated exhaustively as ten immediate NEWECLs to areas [18,22,38,26,30,46,50,58,62,54], including the cited 0xA40C `20 00 26` NEWECL #38; every destination is asserted to exist in the archive, so the fan-out does not point at nothing. (The finding said 'nine crossings'; the operator's own enumeration of the contiguous table finds TEN, plus one outlier at 0xAE32.) DECLARED OVERLAP, asserted in the test rather than narrated: this leg necessarily transits area 5, which is ALREADY this game's proven `early` leg. DQK ships exactly one overland hub, so the overlap is structural and unavoidable; the two legs rest on different evidence within that area (early = the campInterrupted ZOMBIE encounter; wilderness = this crossing table). A reviewer applying a strict 'no shared area id' rule should downgrade this leg -- the gate outcome is unchanged either way, because `ending` fails regardless.

audio.detail: DQK is the best-covered title for audio decoding: its Miles AIL XMIDI music (ADDQ1..3.XMI plus the Roland/Tandy/PC-speaker variants), its OPL2/AdLib instrument bank and player, and BOTH of its digitized SFX banks (SFXDQ.VOC 4-bit ADPCM and the SOUNDS.GLB DIG4 library, 13 effects in a fixed order) have real decoders, and a SoundDispatcher drives per-event combat sound.
gaps: No DQK acceptance asserts retail music playback in a routed session — the decoders are proven, the in-route sequencing is not.
Music timing, instrument-patch fidelity, and scene-transition parity with the original are unverified.

ecl.detail: DQK is the only Gen2/HLIB title in the corpus and its ECL is executed, not merely decoded: the Gen2 dispatch table is located at 2033:0d34 with exactly one extended opcode (0x41; anything above it is a silent no-op), the per-cell descriptor dispatch and the vmRun1 per-step main loop both run, and area 5's route enters the real CampInterrupted handler only after vmRun1 selects table byte 0xE5 at (30,3). All six campaign legs are pinned in packages/engine/test/dqkCampaignLegs.test.ts, each independently re-derived from the retail bytes by the operator before its status was written — agent findings alone were not accepted as evidence.
gaps: The campaign legs are STATIC/BYTE-ONLY: no DOSBox-X, GameLink, emulator or screenshot evidence backs them.
Coverage is of reachable code on the routed areas; the 47-area corpus's unreached arms are decoded but unexecuted.

ECL DECODE CENSUS, SHALLOW AND DEEP (round 33 R1, 2026-09-04): disassembleEclBlock stops at each block's FIRST EXIT, so every clean-EXIT count this project has ever published is a LOWER BOUND -- it never walks the combat, quest or descriptor subroutines placed later in a block's own bytes. walkEclReachable (packages/engine/src/ecl/reachability.ts) follows all five ECL header entry points and every GOTO/GOSUB/ON_GOTO/ON_GOSUB. Measured on this title's 47 retail blocks: 2 shallow desync block(s), 0 deep desync site(s). Deep is BELOW shallow here (0 vs 2): the shallow scan's stop sits on a path no entry point actually reaches, so it is not a defect in reachable code. Pinned in packages/engine/test/eclReachability.test.ts; the deep counts are SITES and the shallow counts are BLOCKS, so the two are not directly subtractable.

graphics.detail: The route renders DQK's native VGA 256-colour art from its own TILE chunks and their embedded palettes — dungeon views, the VGA overland, the title screen, and the real decoded attract demo (ECL.GLB id 7) rather than a synthetic substitute.
gaps: Native 320x200 screen composition, broad picture/animation coverage, palette timing, and pixel-level compositor parity remain incomplete.

ROUND 35 R3 (2026-09-05): HLIB method-25 / GLIB method-0x19 composite assembly, previously decoded but not wired into any `?game=` route (loadGameComposites.test.ts), now reaches the DOS route (dark-queen-dos gains exactly 3 composite frames, all from DISK3/FRAME.TLB) and the Amiga route (dark-queen-amiga gains exactly 3 composite frames via the GLIB method-0x19 twin decoder). HONEST GAP KEPT WITH THE WIN: DQK DISK2/PICC.TLB holds 4 more composites (measured, decode verified) but that file is in no manifest, so those 4 are reachable only through the single-file asset browser, not through any `?game=` route -- 12 of the 16 DOS composites are route-reachable, not 16. packages/engine/test/loadGameComposites.test.ts, docs/engine/research/hlib-glib-composites.md.

map_container.detail: DQK's HLIB 'DataLib' containers are read for real: .TLB/.GLB with typed TILE (frames plus embedded 6-bit-DAC VGA palette), DATA (ECL scripts and GEO maps) and DIG4 sub-chunks. The browser route mounts 20 maps out of GEO.GLB/ECL.GLB and walks them.
gaps: Write-side HLIB support exists for the rebuild tooling but is not part of any DQK playback acceptance.

quests.detail: The quest and ending legs are proven from retail bytes and pinned in packages/engine/test/dqkCampaignLegs.test.ts. The ending leg is a genuine correction of a prior BLOCKED verdict: 'nothing in the 47-area ECL corpus ever writes [0x0032] nonzero' is true but irrelevant, because [0x0032] is not a story flag. The QUEST leg now also runs in the browser: ?dqk=quest drives both arms of [0x0187] bit 0x20 — area 55's BE FRIENDLY is the sole setter in the whole 47-area corpus, and area 54's house cell is the reader, chaining to the Hamhand scene before the flag and printing 'THE HOUSE IS EMPTY AND DARK.' after it.
gaps: The Hamhand HORIZONTAL_MENU is auto-answered by the route (BE FRIENDLY, index 0) rather than presented as a live menu the player clicks. The panel says so on its face.
One leg only: the wider quest graph, journal semantics, and campaign choices are not covered.

retail_save.detail: Greybox save version 2 round-trips the routed DQK state. Separately, and unlike the Gen1 siblings, DQK's OWN save file is decoded roster-and-all and a shipping ?import=dqk route converts its six pre-generated heroes into a live Greybox party: see the import row below.

gaps: No retail-compatible DQK party or campaign-save encoder and no retail-executable acceptance proof exist.
export.scope: No Greybox session-to-DQK retail save exporter is shipped.

gaps: There is no complete bidirectional DQK party/campaign save bridge and no retail-executable save acceptance proof.

Name, the twelve stored current/max ability bytes, HP and level are byte-faithful. Class is byte-faithful only for neacail (code 6, the sole one of the six that lands in the validated M37 NPC-class enum); the other five saved codes (16, 130, 11, 9, 3) fall outside that enum, so their classes are derived from the same disclosed ability-score heuristic importParty.ts's CoK importer uses, and every imported hero is labelled classSource: 'code' | 'ability-heuristic' accordingly.

The save has no established player-race enum, so all six imported heroes are built as race: 'human' (disclosed); three of the six saved DEX 19s (JORIS, neacail, ALARIC) clamp to the human 3-18 range's 18. The built sheet's ac/thac0 are recomputed by createCharacter() from the inferred class+level table, shown beside — not replacing — the save's own raw bytes, so they will not equal the save's stored values.
import.scope: The engine decodes the SAVGAMA.QSV global game-state header — the party flags, position and time that prefix the file — re-verified field by field against the real 7,965-byte shipped DQK save rather than trusting the classic-era SAVGAM.TXT documentation (partySize @31 = 6, speed @17 = 4, currentModule @18 and eclMemberId @21 = 0, with the @21 label corrected from the CoK-era 'initiated' reading against DQK runtime traces). It also decodes the file's six per-character roster records (reusing moncha.ts's decodeNpcRecord at the same ability offset MONCHA framing already uses), and a shipping ?import=dqk route converts them into a live Greybox party — not just a build-tooling sanity check — pinned against the real save's six named heroes: SIR DRYDEN, JORIS THE WISE, LENDUIRA, neacail, ALARIC THE BOLD and MAIGUREIGNE.

ruleset.detail: DQK runs on Greybox's shared AD&D party, exploration, dialogue, tactical combat, treasure, and version-2 persistence systems, plus this title's OWN rules where they diverge from the Gen1 siblings: its Training Hall enforces DQK's own real finite level cap (not CoK's and not 'none'), and leaving its Town returns to the DQK dungeon rather than a Gen1 wilderness. Both are browser acceptances.
gaps: Exhaustive retail spell, item, class, XP-table, monster-AI, and combat-rule parity is not claimed.
Gen2-specific rule divergences beyond the two pinned above are covered only where a routed leg exercises them.

DQK dungeon fights are now fought on a 50x25 surface transcribed from DQK.EXE's own population cluster (dispatcher 0x02cb60, population 0x02c397, cell writer 0x02bcf0), covering 20 of DQK's 21 GEO dungeon areas; buildDqkDungeonCombatMap carries the DQK.EXE file offset on every branch. One limit remains, and one closed. (1) CLOSED 2026-09-04 (round 33 R3): area 5, DQK's ECL-owned wilderness area with no GEO grid, was the last DQK fight still on the engine's generic flat 13x9 fallback. Its wilderness-population routine is now transcribed and buildDqkWildernessCombatMap gives area 5 its own real 50x25 field, so all 21 DQK areas now fight at retail size. The e2e explore-dqk case pins the area-5 field at 50x25 inside the existing case, and the disclosure paragraph that carried this gap was retired in the same commit rather than left standing. (2) The evidence separating DQK's routine from CoAB's SetupDungeonFloor is thin and is reported as such: on a real GEO area the two builders agree on 1250 of 1250 cells, but so does the shuffled-wall null, because that area has no doors -- the entire discriminating set is a single crafted door cell (527) where DQK writes tile 8 and CoAB writes tile 2, via the northOfEast==3 branch of the NE-corner helper. Read that as 'CoAB's routine differing in one helper branch', not as an independent reconstruction. DQK reads the RNG 0 times (proved with a poisoned throwing RNG), against CoAB's addRandomFurniture at 0 on the same input and 140 when its own 0x40 gate bit is forced open.

gaps: Only the routed town behaviours are covered; the full set of shops, temples, and service branches is not.
Town entry from the campaign map is not exercised live.

gaps: Static/byte-only for the campaign leg — no native trace.

ecl.detail: FRUA ships no ECL bytecode at all — it is a construction set, and its per-cell logic lives in the .DSN design's own event records. That format is decoded rather than guessed: GEOxxx.DAT is transcribed from hackdocs GEODATA/GEOGRIDS/GEOENTRY/GEOEVENT and arithmetic-verified against the file's own marker lines (grid start 322 + 576x6 = 3778 'encr'; event table 3786 + 100x20 = 5786 'strg'), with a matching event compiler, runtime, and state layer. The routed HEIRS events (12, 14, 45, 46) are pinned to exact record bytes and SHA-256-pinned source files.

gaps: Source pictures and source terrain are explicitly outside the bounded contract and are not executed.

audio.detail: PARTIAL as of 2026-09-04 (round 33 R5), upgraded from unsupported: the DOS install's MUSIC.DAX is now DECODED, not merely catalogued. Its song blocks carry the GLBR magic and decode through the same already-shipped Gen1 note-event decoder proven on Death Knights, Gateway, Treasures and Pools of Darkness -- making GLBR a FIVE-title DOS format (Death Knights, Gateway, Treasures, Pools of Darkness, and this title), not the four docs/glbr-format.md originally claimed, and NOT the SIX round 33 briefly claimed -- CORRECTED 2026-09-04 (round 34 R4, docs/engine/research/matrix-cubed-audio.md): Matrix Cubed's own MUSIC.DAX, byte-identical to this title's file, is a leftover copy that Matrix's own engine never opens; Matrix's real music is Miles AIL XMI, unrelated to GLBR (see Matrix Cubed's own audio entry). loadGame reports a {songs, events, channels} census and the game-view header renders it: 8 songs, 1959 events, 31 channel streams. THE DECODER WAS ALREADY CORRECT AND CALLED BY NOTHING; wiring the census is what makes it reachable rather than merely tested (packages/engine/test/loadGameGlbrMusic.test.ts, plus the buck-rogers-view / matrix-cubed-view e2e cases, which pin the exact three numbers rather than a loose 'some songs' match).
gaps: THIS IS A DECODE-AND-CENSUS CLAIM, NOT A PLAYBACK CLAIM. No route plays a Buck song, there is no sequencer, no timing model and no instrument mapping, and no acceptance asserts audible output. The song data decodes; nothing here shows it reaching sound hardware.

The Buck/Matrix driver does NOT generalize from the other four GLBR titles, and that is measured rather than assumed: docs/midi-dax-format.md 1.5a's byte-level scan finds no AdLib (0x388) or C/MS (0x220) port immediate anywhere in the shared 11,358-byte block-1 driver blob, while it writes the same PIT/speaker/Tandy ports as DoK's. The two titles' driver blobs are byte-identical to each other, which is also why both censuses are the same three numbers -- that agreement is file identity, not two independent confirmations. NOTE (round 34 R4 correction): this driver-blob byte-identity is still an accurate statement about the two MUSIC.DAX FILES, but Matrix's own engine never opens its copy of that file, so this is no longer evidence about Matrix's own playback path -- see Matrix Cubed's own audio entry.

MUSIC.DAX is catalogued one level further as of 2026-09-03: its block-1 driver blob is byte-identical to Matrix Cubed's (11358 bytes) and writes the same PIT/speaker/Tandy ports as DoK's shared driver, with no AdLib (0x388) or C/MS (0x220) port literal anywhere in the blob — so the hardware backends are a measured gap, not an unknown one (docs/midi-dax-format.md 1.5a). Still no decoder, note-event mapping, or playback path. NOTE (round 34 R4 correction): the comparison to 'Matrix Cubed's' block-1 driver blob above is a comparison to bytes Matrix's own engine never reads -- see Matrix Cubed's own audio entry for its real (XMI) music path.

ecl.detail: ECL_GEN1_BUCK (headerLen 22, vbase 0x7ffe, 8 word-set overrides at opcodes 0x0c/0x1d/0x22/0x23/0x27/0x3c/0x3f/0x40, plus 11 opcode-table extensions at 0x41 and 0x43..0x4c that Gen1's 0x00-0x40 ceiling has no entry for) was derived from Buck's own retail GAME.OVR dispatcher and operand parser by tools/map_buck_ecl_dispatch.py (docs/engine/research/buck-ecl-dispatch-map.md), not borrowed from a sibling title's dialect. Every operand count is read from its handler's own prefetch (mov al,N; push ax; lcall 0xb8,0x2a), NOT fitted to make the corpus decode: for both swept opcodes the corpus actively prefers a different value than the binary states, and the binary was taken anyway (0x4c binary=2 yields 4 desyncs where corpus-best 0 yields 1; 0x43 binary=1 is tied for the worst value swept). Measured against Buck's own 25 retail blocks across ecl1..ecl6.dax (packages/engine/test/buckEclDialect.test.ts): 21 disassemble to a clean terminating EXIT and 4 desync (ecl1#17@0xec, ecl1#18@0x395, ecl6#94@0x50, ecl6#99@0x2c0). A single-step browser inspector (?ecl=buck, documented in docs.ts) opens ecl2.dax#32-35 under this dialect; e2e case ecl-buck pins the dialect-dependent first-instruction address (0x8014) and an 8-instruction clean EXIT.
gaps: 2 of 25 retail blocks still desync under this dialect -- ecl1#18@0x395 and ecl6#99@0x2c0 -- and both are explicitly UNATTRIBUTED rather than explained: neither sits downstream of any opcode this project has modeled, and ecl6#99 stops at byte 0x80, whose handler calls an unidentified far routine. The count reached 2 in two recorded steps, neither smoothed into the other: 7 -> 4 in round 29 (R6's attribution of opcode 0x4c), then 4 -> 2 in round 32 (0x29/0x2c/0x42 given a measured wordSet 0). ecl1#17@0xec and ecl6#94@0x50, both immediately downstream of a decoded 0x29, now resync cleanly and have left the sample. ROUND 32 RETRACTS ROUND 31'S NEGATIVE ON THOSE THREE OPCODES, and that retraction is why the count moved. Round 31 reported that 0 of 140 CoAB oracle calls land on Borland function prologues and called the result decisive; round 32 (R5) found that measurement was taken against still-EXEPACK-compressed bytes. All eight Gen1 loaders are genuine Microsoft EXEPACK v1 (relocations 0, 'RB' at CS:0010, the standard entry stub, dest_len in PARAGRAPHS not bytes). Against the unpacked resident image the same measurement reads 66 of 140 (47%) at shift 0 versus 0 of 140 at +/-1 byte. A negative measured through an un-inverted transform is not a negative about the data. This is a retraction, not a narrowing -- round 31 had already narrowed the sentence once. What round 30 and round 31 established about far-call resolution still stands and is kept here rather than dropped, because it is the machinery the round-32 read runs on: following those routines needs a segment-to-file-offset mapping; a LINEAR mapping calibrated on Curse of the Azure Bonds (where an oracle names each call's true target) landed only 9 of 103 calls against that round's 10-call bar and its winning constant did not generalize, so no address from that attempt was ever written into the dialect. Round 31 partially retracted the FRAMING of that negative, not its arithmetic: the linear fit really does fail, but a linear fit cannot describe a descriptor/stub lookup, and the non-linear resolver in tools/vroomm_layout.py already handled exactly that. Calibrated on the same CoAB oracle (0x4c:0x2a lands exactly on 0x810a; 229 of 240 distinct stub-routed targets land on real oracle function starts, against a shifted null of 1/0/0/0 at +/-1 and +/-16 bytes and a uniform-random null averaging 0.72 hits that never exceeded 6 in 3000 trials), it resolves 3 of the 7 blocking targets: 0xb8:0x7f -> 0x1e0f2, 0xb8:0xb6 -> 0x1e98e, 0x10f:0x4d -> 0x2d9cd. That claim is scoped to those three of seven, not to Buck's binary as a whole, which carries 16 distinct unresolved segments. STILL OPEN after all of it: the remaining two desyncs, the four unresolved targets of the seven, and the semantics of 0x29/0x2c/0x42 -- round 32 measured their operand WIDTH from the unpacked handlers' own prefetches, which is what a wordSet is; it did not establish what they do, and their mnemonics remain inherited Gen1 labels. AND THE CORPUS CENSUS IS NOT EVIDENCE FOR THIS DIALECT, in either direction. On the same 25 blocks ECL_GEN1, ECL_GEN1_SHORT and ECL_GEN1_SHORT_GATEWAY all score 7/18, so beating them only shows that modeling 0x4c helps; and ECL_GEN1_SHORT_POOLS -- a dialect that is wrong for Buck -- scores 5 desyncs by trading them for a wrong 0x21 read. The dialect's support comes from the binary dispatch map, not from this count. tools/buck_far_targets.py, tools/map_buck_ecl_dispatch.py, docs/engine/research/buck-ecl-desyncs.md.

The corpus cross-check of the override table is partial at best: of the watched overrides only 0x0c is reached (twice), every other one zero times, so most of the table's correctness still rests entirely on the binary dispatcher map. Eleven extension opcodes carry uncertain: true, and 0x42 and 0x2c PARLAY were disassembled and left deliberately unmeasured because their handlers call far routines this pass could not identify.
No gameplay route ever executes Buck ECL against a live game state (no ?explore= route, no GEO map, no combat or dialogue outcome); the only consumer is the standalone single-step inspector.

ECL DECODE CENSUS, SHALLOW AND DEEP (round 33 R1, 2026-09-04): disassembleEclBlock stops at each block's FIRST EXIT, so every clean-EXIT count this project has ever published is a LOWER BOUND -- it never walks the combat, quest or descriptor subroutines placed later in a block's own bytes. walkEclReachable (packages/engine/src/ecl/reachability.ts) follows all five ECL header entry points and every GOTO/GOSUB/ON_GOTO/ON_GOSUB. Measured on this title's 25 retail blocks: 2 shallow desync block(s), 195 deep desync site(s). DEEP EXCEEDS SHALLOW HERE (195 vs 2), so any clean-EXIT count quoted elsewhere in this entry is a lower bound on this title's decode health, not a measure of it. Pinned in packages/engine/test/eclReachability.test.ts; the deep counts are SITES and the shallow counts are BLOCKS, so the two are not directly subtractable.

ROUND 35 R1 CORRECTION (2026-09-05, re-verified against packages/engine/test/buckEclDialect.test.ts, 12/12 green): the paragraph above's '4 -> 2 in round 32 (0x29/0x2c/0x42 given a measured wordSet 0)' mis-attributes that movement to 0x42. Opcode 0x42 was INERT through round 34 -- its wordSetOverrides entry had no matching opcodeOverrides definition, so byte 0x42 still decoded as a bad opcode -- so the round-32 movement came from 0x29/0x2c alone; drop the '/0x42' from that clause. Round 35 R1 moved 0x42 from a bare wordSetOverrides key to a real opcodeOverrides entry ({wordSet: 0, mnemonic: 'BUCK_EXT_42', uncertain: true}) in both ECL_GEN1_BUCK and ECL_GEN1_MATRIX, which is what actually makes it decode. With 0x42 now live, ecl1.dax#18@0x395 closes this round (it sat on that opcode), leaving ONE residual desync, not two: ecl6.dax#99@0x2c0 (pinned: {desync: 1, cleanExit: 24, desyncSample: ['ecl6.dax#99@0x2c0']}). No semantics beyond operand width are claimed for 0x42; BUCK_EXT_42 is a deliberately opaque mnemonic. docs/engine/research/buck-matrix-opcode-42.md.

graphics.detail: Two full asset manifests are shipped and reachable from the Library game picker (apps/web/src/ui/gameview.ts GAME_IDS): buck-rogers-countdown-to-doomsday (DOS VGA, 489 frames across TITLE/PIC/CHARS/COMSPR/SPRIT/MARSCOM/VENUSCOM/HITEK/LOTEK/SHIPS/8X8D1, pinned by e2e case buck-rogers-view) and buck-rogers-amiga (WHDLoad Amiga dump, 454 frames across the equivalent DAA families, pinned by e2e case buck-rogers-amiga-view). Both decode with the SAME unmodified DAX/DAA decoders already shipped for CoK/DoK; no new decoder was written for either platform, and TS decodeDaa pixel-parity with the Python reference decoder is proven on 3 real Amiga blocks (packages/engine/test/buckAmigaArt.test.ts).
gaps: This is asset-browser-level graphics only: no exploration, town, wilderness, or combat screen composites this art in a live route.

DOS SPRIT1..6 (35 blocks x 3 view distances) are missing their entire 32..175 palette range; both the manifest's own note and the loader's module docblock report 8.81% of non-transparent pixels rendering as flat white placeholder, and no in-file colour source exists anywhere in Buck's own DAX corpus to recover them. That 8.81% figure is documented in two independent places but is not asserted by any standing test; an independent re-derivation this round bracketed it at 8.53%-8.96% under two plausible 'non-transparent' definitions, confirming the order of magnitude without pinning the exact original formula.

The DOS 8X8D1.DAX block-201 text font is decoded (packages/engine/test/gen1Font.test.ts) but, like every Gen1 title, is deliberately excluded from the whole-game GraphicSet dashboard and, unlike Champions of Krynn's cok-8x8d1 precedent, has no single-asset catalog entry of its own, so it is unreachable in the UI.
Amiga SHIPS.daa is not cross-mapped block-for-block against the DOS SHIPS.dax; only block-id overlap is noted, not identity.

map_container.detail: CORRECTED 2026-09-04 (round 33 R4, docs/engine/research/buck-containers.md). This entry read unsupported and said Buck's containers 'have not been reverse-engineered'. That was wrong: every GEO, WALLDEF and ECL block decodes with the SAME Gen1 loaders already proven on CoK/DoK, measured on real bytes -- 17 GEO blocks all exactly 1026 bytes (100% decodeGeoBlock), 9 WALLDEF blocks each a multiple of 780 (100% decodeWalldefBlock), 25 ECL blocks all carrying the Gen1 0x1388 magic. Every size quoted is the DECOMPRESSED size, i.e. the bytes a loader actually consumes, not the compressed bytes on disk. listPairedGen1Areas finds 16 paired GEO/ECL areas across Buck's six C64 disk sides (1/2/4/3/2/4) under the exact criterion gen1AreaIndex.ts uses; the alternative ('Buck's ids are not paired the CoK way') predicts 0 on every disk and is rejected. Pinned in packages/engine/test/buckContainers.test.ts and tools/test_buck_container_census.py.
gaps: MONSTER RECORDS ARE PARTIALLY MAPPED, ITEM RECORDS REMAIN GENUINELY UNMAPPED. UPDATED 2026-09-04 (round 34 R2, docs/engine/research/buck-record-layout.md): mon0cha.dax's 54 name-plausible 263-byte records and Matrix Cubed's MON0CHA.DAX's 63 name-plausible 259-byte records are ONE XXVc record family, also shared with Buck's own six pregenerated chrdata{n}.sav party saves (259 bytes, uncompressed, no DAX wrapper) -- Buck's own monster record is that SAME 259-byte layout with 4 bytes inserted near offset 249-255 (best single estimate 251, located by a per-offset A/B crossover analysis; the plan's own shuffled-pairing null numbers, 662 vs 1111, did NOT reproduce and are VOID as stated -- a different, more discriminating oracle was used instead). packages/engine/src/loaders/buckSavedCharacter.ts locates name@1, a 7-byte ability septet@16 (order STR/DEX/CON/INT/WIS/CHA/TECH is this round's hypothesis, NOT independently verified against any digitized Buck Rogers reference), hitPoints@69 mirrored @227 (100% agreement on both full corpora: 54/54 Buck, 63/63 Matrix), and a control_morale-gated moralePercent@231 (reusing monster.ts's decodeMorale). AC, THAC0, damage, category, hitDice and XP were NOT located -- no copy/lookup routine was found in GAME.OVR (a TPOV overlay pool) or START.EXE, and no Buck Rogers monster-manual table is digitized in this repo to cross-check against -- so no MonsterLayoutProfile was added to monster.ts (MonsterLayout.ac/.thac0 are non-optional fields; fabricating an offset was rejected per this project's own standing warning against fitting to the nearest size). CORRECTED 2026-09-05 (round 35 R6, docs/engine/research/prose-wiring-claims.md): this bullet used to end 'buckSavedCharacter.ts is not yet called from packages/engine/src/index.ts or any UI import route (Phase B)'. The tree falsified that one commit later. buckSavedCharacter.ts IS called from packages/engine/src/index.ts (the barrel re-exports decodeBuckSavedCharacter / sniffBuckSavedCharacter / BUCK_SAVED_CHARACTER_SIZE at index.ts:1134-1138) and from the live ?import=buck panel (apps/web/src/ui/importBuckParty.ts:33 imports it, main.ts:2070 arms the route), both landed in commit e156eec. The SCOPE of that wiring is display-only and is the part that must not be dropped: unlike Secret's importSecretParty.ts, importBuckParty.ts deliberately never calls createCharacter / addToParty, because no race, class or level field has been located in this record -- so no decoded Buck value reaches the rules layer or a playable party. This is still a DECODE finding, not a rules one. item0.dax is unchanged by this item: still 1456 bytes, still no seventh profile, still just the 16-byte/91-record plausible reading (raw[0:2] a sequential item id) with no field offsets derived.
Still NO ROUTE mounts a legal Buck dungeon or overland walk, and no Buck leg is claimed in the campaign matrix. Container decode is not gameplay.

The C64 disk set corroborates GEO identity but not the other families, and the numbers are not uniform. 15 of 17 shared GEO ids are byte-identical (88.2%) against a 200-trial shuffled-pairing null whose maximum was 4/17 (23.5%) -- clearing the null by about 3.7x, though NOT reproducing the plan's predicted 'at least 30 shared ids, 100% identical'. WALLDEF is 0 of 10 identical (98-99% DIFFERENT, so it is not an identity oracle at all) and ECL is 1 of 25. The two non-identical GEO pairs (DOS ids 67 and 82, 28 and 19 of 1024 bytes differing) were not diagnosed. ITEMFILE00 is byte-identical (0 of 1456 differing) -- a positive result the project's blanket 'compare from offset 2' rule had been hiding as '72% different', because only GEO and ECL carry a DOS-side 2-byte header.

Monster and item container layouts for Buck remain unmapped (see the first gap above); GEO and WALLDEF ARE reverse-engineered (see detail above), correcting this bullet's earlier blanket denial. None of the four families -- GEO, WALLDEF, monster, or item -- is wired to any exploration or combat surface (round 34 R5, docs/engine/research/ledger-stale-claims.md).
The 25-block ECL corpus is disassembled (see ecl above) but never executed against a GEO map or live game state.

retail_save.detail: UPDATED 2026-09-04 (round 34 R2, docs/engine/research/buck-record-layout.md): Buck's own chrdata{1..6}.sav pregenerated-party save format IS now identified, located and decoded -- six plain, uncompressed 259-byte files (no DAX container, no TOC) via the new packages/engine/src/loaders/buckSavedCharacter.ts. Decoded fields: name (PString@1), a 7-byte ability septet@16 (STR/DEX/CON/INT/WIS/CHA/TECH order is this round's hypothesis, NOT independently verified against any digitized Buck Rogers reference), hitPoints@69 (mirrored @227, matching this codebase's Gen1 'HP stored twice' convention), and a control_morale-gated moralePercent@231. All 6 real pregens decode with names matching the embedded PString length byte, 6 distinct nonzero HP values, and 6/6 HP-mirror agreement. This is a DECODE-ONLY result: there is still no encoder. CORRECTED 2026-09-05 (round 35 R6, docs/engine/research/prose-wiring-claims.md): this detail used to continue 'and buckSavedCharacter.ts is not yet wired into packages/engine/src/index.ts or any selected-folder import UI (unlike Secret's importSecretParty.ts) -- both are Phase B work'. Phase B did that work in commit e156eec, and the sentence outlived it. The loader IS exported from packages/engine/src/index.ts (:1134-1138) and IS consumed by the live ?import=buck panel (apps/web/src/ui/importBuckParty.ts:33/99, armed at main.ts:2070). The comparison to importSecretParty.ts still holds in the one way that matters and is retained deliberately: Buck's panel is DISPLAY-ONLY. It never calls createCharacter / addToParty, because no race, class or level byte has been located in the 259-byte record, so nothing it decodes reaches the rules layer, a playable party, or a save writer.

gaps: No retail-compatible Buck save encoder exists; the format is now understood for the decoded fields (round 34 R2) but nothing round-trips it back to disk.

ruleset.detail: packages/engine/src/ruleset/buckrogers/index.ts defines a buckrogers ruleset that extends addnd1e with a naming/approximation layer only: BUCK_ROGERS_CAREERS maps Buck's 5 real player careers (warrior, rogue, medic, engineer, rocketJock) onto existing 1e classes (fighter, thief, cleric, magicUser, ranger). Ability modifiers, XP tables, and THAC0 are the unmodified addnd1e originals, and the ruleset resolves through the default registry (defaultRulesets().resolve('buckrogers') = [addnd1e, buckrogers]).
gaps: No Buck Rogers XXVc-specific combat, weapon, vehicle, or XP math exists; every mechanical number used is the AD&D 1e original, not a science-fiction rule.
No gameplay route ever instantiates a character on this ruleset; it is exercised only by its own unit tests, not by exploration, combat, or import.

ROUND 35 R4 (2026-09-05): the detail above undersells the game's own data. BUCK_CAREER_LABEL (read from START.EXE 0xECDC) has SEVEN entries, not five -- six non-monster careers, INCLUDING Scout, plus one sentinel. The ruleset overlay's mapping to five 1e classes therefore omits a sixth real career the retail table defines. Whether the character-creation screen actually offers Scout is UNMEASURED. Separately, no career/race/sex field is decoded from the saved-character record at all: the plan's own null swept (column 39/40) x (career/race table) x (0-based/1-based) -- 8 combinations -- and came back 8/8 non-discriminating, i.e. every reading is equally plausible, which is why none is claimed. docs/engine/research/buck-string-tables.md, tools/test_buck_string_tables.py, packages/engine/test/buckSavedCharacter.test.ts.

audio.detail: UPDATED 2026-09-04 (round 34 R4, docs/engine/research/matrix-cubed-audio.md): Matrix Cubed's OWN music is NOT its MUSIC.DAX. That file is byte-identical (sha256) to Buck Rogers: Countdown to Doomsday's own MUSIC.DAX and is never opened by Matrix's own unpacked START.EXE or GAME.OVR (tools/matrix_music_strings.py: 0 file-open references in either binary, against Countdown's own 2 -- a Pascal-string 'MUSIC'+'.dax' construction found only in Countdown's loader). Matrix's real music is Miles AIL: three XMI files (BUCKA/B/C.XMI, 7 songs each -- BUCKA 897/134/244/82/213/146/968 events per song, BUCKB 844/109/209/62/221/139/1039, BUCKC 153/27/68/30/24/11/82) plus a 152-instrument FATV9.AD timbre bank (the same container shape as DQK's own 199-instrument INSTR.AD, a smaller bank as predicted), decoded through the EXISTING packages/engine/src/audio/xmi.ts / instrAd.ts decoders with ZERO code changes. apps/web/src/audio/gameAudio.ts's ensureLoaded() now routes game === 'matrix' through this XMI path (MATRIX_MUSIC_XMI / MATRIX_INSTR_AD, mirroring DQK's ADDQ1.XMI + INSTR.AD wiring) instead of GLBR_MUSIC_GAMES, which no longer lists 'matrix' at all.
gaps: THIS CORRECTS ROUND 33's OWN CLAIM FOR THIS TITLE: the '8 GLBR songs, 1959 events, 31 channel streams' this entry previously reported for Matrix was Countdown's file identity, not two independent confirmations of Matrix's own music -- Matrix's own engine never opens that file.

CLOSED IN ROUND 34 PHASE B (this gap read 'THE DASHBOARD CENSUS HAS NOT CAUGHT UP' when R4 measured it, because the manifest had not yet been patched). apps/web/games/buck-rogers-matrix-cubed.json now lists BUCKA/B/C.XMI (plus FATV9.AD/.BNK/.CAT and the five .ADV drivers), which flips loadGame.ts's manifest-driven hasXmiSiblings rule: the GLBR census is suppressed for this title's leftover MUSIC.DAX and xmiMusicCensus reports 21 songs / 5702 events / 95 channel streams instead. Those three numbers were re-measured through the SHIPPED code path (not the test-local manifest clone R4 used) and agree with R4 exactly, per file: BUCKA 7/2684/45, BUCKB 7/2623/43, BUCKC 7/395/7. GameMusicSummary gained a `format` field so the dashboard stops labelling every census 'GLBR'. Pinned two-sided in apps/web/test/e2e.mjs's matrix-cubed-view case (MATRIX_MUSIC_ROW must match AND Countdown's GLBR row must NOT), and in packages/engine/test/loadGameGlbrMusic.test.ts, whose test-local clone is now inverted: it STRIPS the .XMI rows and shows the same MUSIC.DAX bytes revert to 8/1959/31, so hasXmiSiblings is proven to be what drives the switch.

Which of the five .ADV hardware drivers (ADLIB/MT32MPU/SBFM/TANDY/PCSPKR) Matrix selects at runtime, and which of BUCKA/BUCKB/BUCKC.XMI plays at which scene, are both undetermined -- gameAudio.ts's own choice of BUCKA.XMI's first song is an honest-arbitrary pick, not a verified 'this is the title theme' claim, the same evidentiary level DQK's own ADDQ1.XMI pick already carries.
This remains a decode-and-playback-WIRING claim, not an audible-output proof: no acceptance test asserts that sound actually reaches the speaker.

ecl.detail: Round 31 built a dispatch map from Matrix Cubed's OWN GAME.OVR (tools/map_matrix_ecl_dispatch.py) and shipped the result as ECL_GEN1_MATRIX in packages/engine/src/ecl/disassemble.ts, wired to the ?ecl=matrix inspector route. The starting point remains true and is why this is not a copy of Countdown's entry: Matrix's GAME.OVR carries FBOV -- Curse of the Azure Bonds' overlay magic -- not Countdown's TPOV, so nothing was assumed to carry over. The dispatcher and operand parser were located by the same structural match against the CoAB oracle that Countdown's own tool uses (dispatcher similarity 0.8885/trigram 0.6087; operand parser 0.8750/0.9059). Header shape was read from Matrix's own ECL1.DAX bytes, not inherited: all 33 blocks open with the 0x1388 magic and put the fifth far pointer's vaddr at 0x8014, giving headerLen 22 / vbase 0x7ffe. Matrix dispatches the same 75 opcodes as Countdown with an identical measured word set and 0 disagreements. How much of that agreement is DISCRIMINATING was computed after an adversarial pass attacked the original wording, which said '53 agreeing on a concrete value, 22 both-unmeasured, 0 disagreements' without naming the alternative: the alternative is 'Matrix follows the plain Gen1/CoAB base table', and on most opcodes Countdown's dialect never diverged from that base, so agreeing there costs the alternative nothing. The real arm is 16 of 75, not 53 -- 8 opcodes where the effective word set differs from the base table AND Matrix's own handler yields a concrete value (0x0c, 0x1d, 0x22, 0x23, 0x27, 0x31, 0x3f, 0x40, including 0x27 jumping from base 8 to 2), plus the 8 beyond-0x40 extension opcodes with a measured width, for which the base table has no row at all. Matrix matches Countdown on 16 of 16. 56 shared-range opcodes carry the same word set under plain Gen1 as under ECL_GEN1_MATRIX and so separate nothing, and 22 are vacuous because neither handler reaches the parser. 0x3c is the instructive near-miss: Buck overrides it (base 1 -> 0) so it looks discriminating, but Matrix's own handler is no_far_call and measured nothing, which is why the arm is 8 and not 9. packages/engine/test/matrixEclDialect.test.ts computes this partition rather than restating it. Also 0x2b/0x31 share one compiled handler at offset 0x1c99 in Matrix's binary too, the code-identity evidence Countdown's SHORT_MENU override rests on. Against the corpus, 29 of the 33 retail blocks reach a clean terminating EXIT and 4 desync (blocks 1, 18, 20, 24) -- but that census is NOT the evidence and must not be read as it. Plain Gen1 scores 26/7 on the same blocks, and ECL_GEN1_SHORT_POOLS, a dialect that is wrong for Matrix, ties at exactly 29/4. A raw clean-exit count does not discriminate here; the binary does. WHY THIS IS 'partial' AND NOT 'supported': the derived table came back field-for-field equal to ECL_GEN1_BUCK, so the corpus census under the two dialects is identical BY CONSTRUCTION, not because it was measured twice -- that agreement is arithmetic and is evidence about the two dispatchers, not about these blocks. The eleven beyond-0x40 extension opcodes keep uncertain:true here for the same reason they do in Countdown: their word set was read from a handler prefetch, their MEANING never was. ECL_GEN1_MATRIX is a separate literal rather than an alias precisely so the deep-equal pin in packages/engine/test/matrixEclDialect.test.ts stays able to fail.
gaps: 3 of the 33 retail ECL blocks still desync under ECL_GEN1_MATRIX (blocks 18@0x14b0, 20@0x2f2, 24@0x26c) -- the same unresolved class as Countdown's own remaining two. Round 31 recorded 4 (1@0x66e, 18@0x135, 20@0x2f2, 24@0x26c); round 32 gave 0x29/0x2c/0x42 a measured wordSet 0, read from Matrix's OWN handlers under a stated claim boundary that forbids inheriting from Countdown, and the sample moved for two DIFFERENT reasons that are kept apart here. Block 1 is FULLY RESOLVED -- its stop sat on what is now a decoded 0x2c. Block 18 is ATTRIBUTED BUT NOT CLOSED: decoding runs much further, past the old 0x29 stop at 0x135, and then hits a NEW, later, previously-masked desync at 0x14b0. That is a site this patch REVEALS rather than fixes, and counting it as progress would be counting the same block twice. Blocks 20 and 24 are untouched and unrelated to the three opcodes. TWO NUMBERS HERE MUST NOT BE OVERSTATED. First, the census is weak evidence for the dialect: in the four-way null on these same blocks, ECL_GEN1 and ECL_GEN1_SHORT score 7/26 and ECL_GEN1_SHORT_POOLS -- wrong for Matrix -- scores 4/29. Through round 31 Pools TIED ECL_GEN1_MATRIX exactly; it now trails by one block only because Buck/Matrix moved and Pools did not. The tie was never evidence, and its disappearance is not evidence either. Second, the discriminating share of the 75-opcode Countdown agreement moves 16 -> 18, NOT 19: 0x42 does not join the extension bucket, because it carries a bare wordSetOverrides value with no opcodeOverrides mnemonic entry (unlike 0x41 and 0x43+), so the partition helper cannot read its width at all. The other 56 of the 75 remain free for the plain-Gen1 alternative and 22 are vacuous. tools/map_matrix_ecl_dispatch.py, docs/engine/research/matrix-ecl-dialect.md.
The eleven 0x41..0x4c extension opcodes carry a measured operand width and an INVENTED mnemonic; none of their semantics has been established from Matrix's binary, and all eleven stay uncertain:true.
The mnemonic strings across the whole table are inherited Gen1 labels. Matrix's binary evidence proves operand counts and the 0x2b/0x31 code identity; it does not independently name any opcode.
The ?ecl=matrix route single-steps four blocks in an inspector. No gameplay route executes a Matrix Cubed ECL block, and no Matrix leg is claimed in the campaign matrix.

ECL DECODE CENSUS, SHALLOW AND DEEP (round 33 R1, 2026-09-04): disassembleEclBlock stops at each block's FIRST EXIT, so every clean-EXIT count this project has ever published is a LOWER BOUND -- it never walks the combat, quest or descriptor subroutines placed later in a block's own bytes. walkEclReachable (packages/engine/src/ecl/reachability.ts) follows all five ECL header entry points and every GOTO/GOSUB/ON_GOTO/ON_GOSUB. Measured on this title's 33 retail blocks: 3 shallow desync block(s), 452 deep desync site(s). DEEP EXCEEDS SHALLOW HERE (452 vs 3), so any clean-EXIT count quoted elsewhere in this entry is a lower bound on this title's decode health, not a measure of it. Pinned in packages/engine/test/eclReachability.test.ts; the deep counts are SITES and the shallow counts are BLOCKS, so the two are not directly subtractable.

ROUND 35 R1 CORRECTION (2026-09-05, re-verified against packages/engine/test/matrixEclDialect.test.ts and eclReachability.test.ts, both green): the same false '/0x42' attribution applies to this row's round-32 clause -- 0x42 was inert through round 34, so that wordSet-0 read came from 0x29/0x2c alone. Wiring 0x42 into a real opcodeOverrides entry this round (same value in both dialects, {wordSet: 0, mnemonic: 'BUCK_EXT_42', uncertain: true}) closes block 24@0x26c, leaving TWO residual desyncs, not three: 18@0x14b0 and 20@0x2f2 (pinned: {desync: 2, cleanExit: 31}). Deep reachability moves too once 0x42 stops being a dead key: deep desync sites 452 -> 16, shallow 3 -> 2, reachable bytes 217,569 -> 236,375, with 528 0x42 instructions across 24 blocks now decoding. DECLINED, NOT CORRECTED HERE: this row's '16 -> 18, NOT 19' discriminating-opcode-share claim and its stated reason ('0x42 ... carries a bare wordSetOverrides entry with no opcodeOverrides mnemonic in either dialect') are also stale -- 0x42 DOES carry an opcodeOverrides entry in both dialects as of this round -- but packages/engine/test/matrixEclDialect.test.ts's own pinned MATRIX_MEASURED set still explicitly excludes 0x42 from that computation as read on 2026-09-05 (discriminatingOverrides stays at 10 entries, extensionsBeyondBase at 7, total 17), which disagrees with a same-round handoff claim that the share becomes 19. Re-measure that specific number against the test file's own pinned arrays before restating it either way; this entry does not adjudicate it. docs/engine/research/buck-matrix-opcode-42.md.

All 19 graphics-bearing .DAX files (TITLE/BIGPIC1/PIC1/PIC7/PIC8/SPRIT1/BACK1/BORDERS/CPIC1/CHARS/8X8D0/8X8D1/COMSPR/MARSCOM/VENUSCOM/HITEK/LOTEK/SHIPS/CURSOR) decode with the SAME unmodified DAX decoder path (tools/dax_decode.py's own vga-chunky-items / vga-compressed-picture classifiers, the same classification order its main() uses) already shipped for Countdown to Doomsday; no new decoder was written.
